papers.title: Tilting theory on continuous quivers (I) maximal rigid and tilting subcategories
papers.authors: Haowei Liu, Zonghui Liu, Shijie Zhu
papers.abstract: Let $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$ be the category of finitely generated persistence modules on the interval $\mathbb I\subseteq\mathbb R$. We study the maximal rigid subcategories of $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$. Maximal rigid interval consistent subcategories are classified via tilting modules over the corresponding discrete type $A$ quiver. We compare several related notions, (weak) tilting and maximal rigidity, in both the context of hereditary abelian categories with enough projective objects and $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$ and prove that every maximal rigid interval consistent subcategory is weak tilting and every maximal rigid consistent below subcategory is tilting. We also establish a continuous analogue of Ingalls-Thomas's bijection by showing a bijection between integrally supported maximal rigid consistent below subcategories and integrally generated torsion classes.

papers.title: Sub-Laplacian Comparison Theorem and Gradient Estimates on Complete Noncompact Contact Riemannian Manifolds
papers.authors: Guilin Yang, Biqiang Zhao, Weihao Zheng
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first derive the Bochner-type formulas of the Hermitian-Tanno connection on contact Riemannian manifolds. Second, we prove a sub-Laplacian comparison theorem on complete noncompact contact Riemannian manifolds with bounded geometric conditions. Finally, we obtain the gradient estimates of a positive eigenfunction on a complete noncompact contact Riemannian manifold which satisfies similar geometric conditions.

papers.title: Free energy fluctuations of symmetric perceptron models up to and including criticality
papers.authors: Hang Du, Shuyang Gong, Brice Huang, Zhangsong Li
papers.abstract:
We study the free energy fluctuations of spherical and Ising perceptron models with general even activations. These include the symmetric binary perceptron, the $U$-perceptron, and the bipartite Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model. Our main result is a Gaussian CLT for the free energy that holds both in the ``high-temperature'' interior of a second moment RS regime and on its ``critical'' boundary. At criticality, the CLT has scale $(\frac{\log N}{6})^{1/2}$, which matches the free energy fluctuations of the critical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model and suggests this scaling is universal.
  The proof shows that the perceptron model's free energy fluctuations are explained, up to an additive $o(1)$ error with high probability, by those of a corresponding spherical Hopfield model, and that this relation persists even at criticality. This proof strategy builds on a critical reweighted moment method developed by the first and third authors \cite{du2026fluctuations} to identify the critical fluctuations of the SK free energy, which links these fluctuations to the spectral edge spacing of the disorder.

papers.title: Strongly non-linear continuous model for wave propagation in 2D granular media: derivation and hyperbolicity analysis
papers.authors: Sebastiano Cominelli, R\'egis Cottereau, Sergey Gavrilyuk, Bruno Lombard, Fabien Petitpas
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop a nonlinear continuum model for wave propagation in two-dimensional granular materials, building on key ideas from Nesterenko's work. Starting from the Hertzian contact law and neglecting contact friction, we derive an effective continuum description through homogenization, assuming spherical, monodisperse grains, local periodicity, and the Cauchy--Born hypothesis. The resulting strain-gradient model depends on both the first and second gradients of the displacement field. We analyse the hyperbolicity of the leading-order system through its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, establishing conditions for hyperbolicity within a restricted deformation domain. The model is solved using an explicit finite-volume method to investigate gravitational settling and wave propagation. We derive analytical expressions for the longitudinal and transverse wave speeds and highlight their dependence on depth. Finally, the predictions of the continuum model are compared with existing discrete-element simulations. This formulation allows several extensions, including more complex packing geometries, contact laws, and large-deformation regimes in which the contact network can evolve.

papers.title: On the Hodge conjecture for hyper-K\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by four
papers.abstract: We prove the Hodge conjecture for all hyper-K\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension $2n$ with $n+1$ a prime number, and all powers of these varieties. For any variety $X$ of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by 4, we show that the Lefschetz standard conjecture for $X$ implies the Hodge conjecture for $X$ and all its powers.

papers.title: Biases in gaps between zeros of Dirichlet L-functions
papers.authors: Jonathan W. Bober, Zhenchao Ge, Micah B. Milinovich
papers.abstract: We describe a new family of Dirichlet L-functions that provably have an unusual value distribution. Experimentally, we find that the L-functions in this family have a significant and previously undetected bias in the distribution of gaps between their zeros. These phenomena appear to have an arithmetic explanation that corresponds to the nonvanishing of a certain Gauss-type sum. We give a complete classification of the characters for which this sum is nonzero and count them. This sum vanishes for 100% of primitive Dirichlet characters, so L-functions in our newly discovered family are rare (a set of density zero among all primitive characters). The nonvanishing of this sum implies that there is a main term when one integrates the Z-function associated to a Dirichlet L-function over a long interval. We prove that the L-functions in this family are the only GL(1)/Q or GL(2)/Q cuspidal automorphic L-functions whose Z-functions have a "large" mean value when integrated. We discuss analogous results for the Riemann zeta-function.

papers.title: Random Cellular Automata and deBruijn Graphs
papers.abstract: Update rules of a one dimensional Cellular Automaton can be expressed using an edge-labeled deBruijn graph. We explore various questions about the image of a cellular automaton given by a randomly selected update rule by considering a random deBruijn graph.

papers.title: Relative Langlands duality for linear periods
papers.authors: Tsao-Hsien Chen, Sanath K. Devalapurkar, Mark Macerato, David Nadler
papers.abstract: We prove relative Langlands duality for $X = GL_{p+q}/(GL_p \times GL_q)$. These symmetric spaces arise in the setting of the linear period of Friedberg-Jacquet when $p=q$, and exhibit non-tempered behavior when $q>p+1$. Via the real-symmetric correspondence, we establish a derived Satake equivalence for the real group $G_{\mathbb R}=U(p,q)$, and use it to obtain a constructible realization of coherent sheaves on Kato's exotic nilpotent cones. Along the way, we describe the dual variety of $X$ in terms of the Whittaker cotangent bundle and regular centralizers, viewed as Coulomb branches.

papers.title: The Strength of Root Cuts in an Extended Abstract Branch-and-Cut Model
papers.abstract: The branch-and-cut paradigm has led to effective solvers for a wide range of mathematical optimization problems. Despite significant theoretical work on pure branching and pure cutting, less is known about their interaction. We study an extended abstract branch-and-cut model to investigate tradeoffs between branching and cutting, including the time to generate cuts. We prove that, under symmetric branching, some minimal-time tree has all cuts at the root, before the first branching node, and that there is an asymmetric setting where some minimal-time tree has no internal cuts, i.e., cuts both preceded and followed by branching. For other settings, although a root-cut tree may be suboptimal and differ substantially in structure from a minimal-time tree, it nevertheless provides a reliable approximation whose tree time does not deviate arbitrarily from the optimum. For constant cut strength and bounded time functions, we show that the best root-cut tree is asymptotically optimal as the target bound grows. In addition, under a single-cut-per-path restriction, we characterize when some minimal-time tree has an internal cut. Lastly, simulations indicate that the best root-cut tree is much closer to a minimal-time tree than our worst-case approximation guarantee suggests.

papers.title: Ozone groups and centers of two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras
papers.authors: James G\'omez, H\'ector Su\'arez, Helbert Venegas
papers.abstract: Let $p,q$ be roots of unity with $pq\neq1$, and put $\ell=|\langle p,q\rangle|$ and $t=\ord(pq)$. Up to isomorphism, the two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras $\mathcal H_{p,q}$ are exactly the noetherian PI graded down-up algebras, so everything here holds for that whole class. The ozone group is $\mu_\ell\times\mu_{\ell/t}$, generated by conjugation by three normal elements, and the center is recovered from the fixed ring of the ozone group as the invariants of a cyclic group of order $t$. We give a presentation of the center as a hypersurface over a cyclic quotient surface singularity. It is regular exactly when $1$ is a characteristic root, which disproves a conjecture of Chan, Gaddis, Won and Zhang, and Gorenstein exactly when $p^{m/h}=q^{n/h}$, where $m=\ord(p)$, $n=\ord(q)$ and $h=\gcd(m,n)$; for $p=\zeta_5$, $q=\zeta_5^{2}$ it is not. We also decide when the fixed ring of the ozone group is Gorenstein and when $\mathcal H_{p,q}$ is Calabi--Yau, and show that the algebras with regular center have non-affine automorphisms and nonzero locally nilpotent derivations.

papers.title: Principal specializations of the $t$-chromatic symmetric function
papers.authors: Aram Bingham, Kyle Celano, Patricia Commins, Rosa Orellana, Jianping Pan, Mary Claire Simone
papers.abstract: We introduce the $t$-chromatic symmetric function $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$, a variant of Stanley's chromatic symmetric function in which the variable $t$ records the number of distinct colors used in a proper coloring. Although $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$ is equivalent to the chromatic symmetric function as a graph invariant, its principal specializations retain substantially more information than those of the chromatic symmetric function. This construction is motivated by the work of Bajo--Beck--Vindas-Mel\'endez on the $q$-chromatic polynomial and the conjecture of Loehr--Warrington that the $n$th principal specialization of the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees on at most $n$ vertices, both of which stem from Stanley's longstanding question of whether the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees. We determine the classes of caterpillars resulting from the second principal specialization of $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$, showing that the second specialization already captures some of the structure of trees. We then prove that the third principal specialization distinguishes and explicitly reconstructs caterpillars with three spine vertices as well as elongated bistars. Finally, we conjecture, based on computational data, that the fourth principal specialization distinguishes all caterpillars.

papers.title: Rapid stabilization for Stokes and Navier-Stokes systems with localized disturbance
papers.authors: Christian Calle, Patricio Guzm\'an, Hugo Parada, Jefferson Prada
papers.abstract: In this study, we analyze the rapid stabilization of Stokes and the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems in the presence of an unknown spatially localized disturbance. A multivalued feedback control strategy is proposed which combines the Lyapunov frequency method with the multivalued sign operator. This methodology connects Lyapunov-based stability analysis with spectral inequalities, while the inclusion of the sign operator provides robustness against disturbance. The closed-loop system is governed by a differential inclusion, for which well-posedness is proved via the theory of maximal monotone operators. This approach guarantees global rapid exponential stabilization for the Stokes system and local rapid exponential stabilization for the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems, with arbitrarily large disturbance bounds. In three dimensions, we obtain global strong solutions and rapid exponential stabilization for initial data sufficiently small in the $L^2$-norm with a prescribed, arbitrarily large bound in the $H^1$-norm.

papers.title: Stochastic Geometry Meets Optimization: Data-Driven Cellular Planning
papers.authors: Abhishek K. Shukla, Abhishek K. Gupta, Ketan Rajawat
papers.abstract: Deployment optimization of base stations (BSs) is critical for improving cellular network performance metrics such as coverage and capacity, impacting user experience, scalability, and infrastructure cost-effectiveness. Traditional methods that optimize precise BS locations do not generally provide broader insights into spatial deployment priorities or alternative viable deployments. Stochastic geometry approaches, on the other hand, offer a more interpretable intensity-based framework, but rarely utilize real-world user location data or investigate optimal BS deployment strategies. In this work, we propose a data-driven stochastic geometry-based approach that optimizes BS deployment intensity to maximize a network performance metric using samples from an unknown user-location distribution. We specialize the framework to an inhomogeneous Poisson point process (PPP) for cellular coverage analysis. The resulting infinite-dimensional problem is discretized over the deployment area and solved using sampled user locations. We characterize the discretization and sampling errors, apply stochastic mirror ascent to solve the empirical problem, and analyze the selection of concrete BS deployments using independent validation samples. Unlike traditional methods, our approach yields an optimized spatial intensity that reveals deployment priorities across regions and accommodates practical deployment constraints, multi-tier networks, and incremental deployment scenarios. Numerical experiments with synthetic and real-world spatial demand data demonstrate the proposed approach under different network configurations.

papers.title: Quasideterminants and differential realizations of W-algebras
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the Hamiltonian reduction, used in constructing finite rectangular $W$-algebras, of the big-cell differential realization of $\mathfrak{gl}_{np}$. We establish an intrinsic factorization of the reduced differential realization, identifying its Yangian action with the coproduct action on a tensor product of $n$ evaluation differential realizations of $\mathfrak{gl}_p$. Corner quasideterminants provide the essential noncommutative mechanism through which Hamiltonian reduction transforms the higher-rank differential realization into a factorized lower-rank Yangian action.

papers.title: Affine Higher Bruhat Orders
papers.authors: Sara Billey, Herman Chau, Kevin Liu
papers.abstract: The higher Bruhat orders are partial orders originally constructed by Manin and Schechtman, with an equivalent construction from Ziegler. These partial orders generalize the weak order on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$, and the second higher Bruhat order is a poset on commutation classes of reduced words for the longest element in ${\mathfrak{S}}_n$, where covering relations correspond to braid relations. Like the weak order, each of the higher Bruhat orders is a ranked poset with unique minimal and maximal elements. Constructing analogs of the higher Bruhat orders in other settings is an area of recent interest, including recent work of Hothem for permutations in $S_{n}$. We give a construction that generalizes any interval $[\mathrm{id},w]$ in the weak order where $w$ is an element of the affine symmetric group $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$. Our construction recovers the classical higher Bruhat orders when $w$ is the longest element in $\mathfrak{S}_n$. Paralleling the classical case, we show that the second higher Bruhat order is a ranked poset on commutation classes of reduced words for $w\in \widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$, allowing us to prove a conjecture due to Elias. When $w\in \mathfrak{S}_n$, we also establish results for our higher Bruhat orders that are direct analogs of numerous results in the classical higher Bruhat orders.

papers.title: Sphere decomposition for finite subgroups of 3-manifold mapping class groups
papers.abstract: For a closed, oriented 3-manifold $M$, we show that any finite subgroup of its mapping class group preserves an isotopy class of filling sphere system on $M$. This is an isotopy version of the "equivariant sphere theorem" of Meeks-Yau. As part of our analysis, we establish a bijection between simplices of the Guirardel--Levitt outer space for $\pi_1(M)$ and filling sphere systems in $M$, generalizing an argument of Hatcher. We also compute the image of $\mathrm{Homeo}(M)\to\mathrm{Out}(\pi_1M)$ for any such $M$.

papers.title: Research profiles and the mathematical landscape: A grassroots proposal for mathematics with AI
papers.abstract: Repeated mathematical work with AI leaves behind corrections, failed arguments, and sometimes useful ways of asking questions. I propose keeping these in a research profile that the mathematician develops and controls. The profile marks parts of the mathematical landscape according to the researcher's understanding and makes those markings available to later work with AI. This suggests experiments with individual profiles, shared readings of papers, and graduate education. It also raises mathematical questions about the landscape itself: its connections, distances, and changes under discovery. I describe two examples, searching for branches of mathematics with a common base and recovering useful questions from the history of Floer theory. The aim is to give mathematicians something to try and a part in deciding how mathematical AI develops.

papers.title: Tate Frobenius and chromatic blueshift of finite spectra
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $n\geq 1$. We prove that the Tate-Frobenius of the $\operatorname{K}(n)$-local sphere induces an equivalence between $L_{n-1}L_{\operatorname{K}(n)}Y$ and $(L_{\operatorname{K}(n)}Y)^{t\Sigma_p} \cong (L_nY)^{t\Sigma_p}$ for any finite $p$-local type $n-1$ spectrum $Y$ with trivial $\Sigma_p$-action.

papers.title: Additive energy and Fourier complexity of graphs
papers.authors: Vishal Gupta, Sam Ferguson, Alex Iosevich, Joshua Iosevich, Haoyuan Tian, Ben Song
papers.abstract:
We study the additive energy and the Fourier approximation of graph adjacency matrices labeled by a cyclic group. For a graph with $N$ vertices, $s$ edges and adjacency matrix $M$, the additive energy of its directed edge set is at most $\min\{(2s)^3,N^2\operatorname{tr}(M^4)\}$, and equality in the spectral bound holds exactly when the labeling attains the graph-energy lower bound for the Fourier ratio. Such a labeling also minimizes every best $k$-term Fourier approximation error, whose square equals the tail of the squared adjacency singular values. We prove that graphs of odd prime-power order admit an equality-attaining labeling exactly when they are cyclic Cayley graphs, and a connected example on $15$ vertices shows that equality need not imply vertex transitivity at other orders.
  We construct regular graph families with asymptotically maximal normalized additive edge energy and unbounded minimum Fourier ratio, one of them with density tending to one half. For dense graph sequences under uniformly random labelings, the collision dimension differs from the reciprocal squared edge density by a quantity tending to zero in probability. We also prove a quantitative stability estimate for the graph-energy bound and show why its dependence on a spectral scale cannot be omitted, even for regular graphs. For a rank-$m$ orthogonal projector we prove $m\leq D_4\leq\operatorname{FR}^2$, characterize the equality $D_4=m$ by cyclic translation invariance, and obtain a quantitative approximation by a circulant projector.

papers.title: Finite element approximation on piecewise smooth domains
papers.abstract: The approximation theory by finite elements is usually described on the simplified geometry of polygonal or polyhedral domains. While avoiding the question of boundary approximation makes the analysis simpler, real applications may involve piecewise smooth domains and in some cases the extension of classical results to general boundaries may be tricky. In this paper we discuss in a systematic way the approximation properties and the error analysis of standard non-isoparametric finite element spaces on piecewise curvilinear domains in two and three dimensions. We show in detail how the geometric error introduces a barrier for the $H^1$ and $L^2$ error of the solution of both Dirichlet and Neumann elliptic problems independently of the regularity of the problem and of the degree of the finite element spaces used.

papers.title: Higher-order asymptotic formulae for periodic orbits of 3-dimensional volume-preserving Anosov flows and the Foulon conjecture
papers.abstract:
Let $X^t$ be a volume-preserving Anosov flow of class $C^7$ on a closed $3$-manifold. We consider a sequence of periodic orbits which shadow a homoclinic loop of a fixed periodic orbit $\gamma$, and derive higher-order asymptotic expansions for their periods $T_n$ and for the logarithms of their unstable multipliers $\log\lambda_n$. We give geometric interpretations of the coefficients in these expansions, in particular in terms of the Anosov cocycle (\`a la Hurder-Katok) and the longitudinal Anosov cocycle (\`a la Foulon-Hasselblatt), evaluated on $\gamma$. Following the idea of De Simoi-Leguil-Vinhage-Yang, we compare these asymptotics when volume is the measure of maximal entropy. In this case, the equilibrium-state characterizations of volume and the measure of maximal entropy synchronize periods and exponents: $\log\lambda_n=hT_n$. Matching the coefficients of the two asymptotic expansions forces the cohomology classes of both cocycles to vanish.
  Then the work of Foulon-Hasselblatt on the longitudinal Anosov cocycle, together with Foulon's work on the contact case, yields the Foulon Conjecture for flows of class $C^7$: if volume is the measure of maximal entropy, then, up to a finite cover, $X^t$ is smoothly conjugate either to a constant-roof suspension of a hyperbolic automorphism of the $2$-torus or to a finite cover of the constant-speed geodesic flow on a closed hyperbolic surface.

papers.title: Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson classes of symmetric powers and applications
papers.abstract: The Chern-Schwartz-MacPherson class $c_{SM}(X)$ is defined in the Chow group $A_*(X)$ of a scheme $X$, and generalizes $c(T_X)\cap [X]$ if $X$ is smooth. In this paper we independently compute $c_{SM}(S^nX)\in A_*(S^nX)$ modulo $n!$ torsion; we use this result to compute the pushforward to $S^nX$ of $c_{SM}(Quot^n_X(E))$ (and in particular $c_{SM}(Hilb^n X)$) when $X$ is smooth and $E$ is a vector bundle on $X$. Finally, when $X$ is smooth and complete of dimension $3$ we propose a refined version of the the MNOP conjecture that computes the image of the pushforward of $[Hilb^n X]^{vir}$ to $A_0(S^nX)$ and prove it modulo $n!$ torsion when $X$ is Calabi-Yau.

papers.title: Divisor Sums with Spacing Constraints
papers.abstract: For $x,y>0$ let $S(x,y)$ denote the largest value of $\sum_{n\in A}\tau(n)$ over subsets $A$ of $[1,x]\cap\N$ whose elements are pairwise separated by more than $y$ (here $\tau$ is the divisor function). We determine the order of magnitude, and in a subrange the precise asymptotic, of $S(x,y)$ when the spacing parameter $y$ ranges over a polylogarithmic scale $y=(\log x)^{1+\lambda(\log\lambda-1)}$, $\lambda>1$. We show that for every fixed $\lambda>2$ the spacing constraint costs a computable power of $\log x$ in the exponent, while for every fixed $1<\lambda<2$ it costs nothing at all: $S(x,y)\sim x\log x$, the same asymptotic as the unconstrained sum $\sum_{n\le x}\tau(n)$. Near the threshold $\lambda=2$ the two regimes meet, and we show that for any fixed $\kappa>0,$ $S(x,y)\asymp_{\kappa} x\log x$ uniformly as long as $\lambda\le 2+2\kappa/\sqrt{\log\log x}$. The proof combines the Sathe-Selberg distribution of the number of prime factors, a smooth squarefree estimate obtained from a generating function together with Cauchy's formula, a sieve estimate for correlations among the squarefree parts of the integers that contribute most heavily to $\sum_{n\le x}\tau(n)$, and two combinatorial devices (the Caro-Wei bound and a concentration inequality on the symmetric group) used to extract a well-spaced independent set from a sparse auxiliary graph.

papers.title: Presheaf structures governed by oriented matroids and pseudohyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: We study higher complements of pseudohyperplane arrangements and the specialization maps between them, induced by degenerations. We develop a presheaf formalism on oriented matroids and weak maps, which model degenerations. Our main constructions are the posets of weighted and weightwise topes, which provide functorial combinatorial models for higher complements and their specialization morphisms. Their presheaf structure yields a deletion-contraction homotopy pushout, from which we derive a uniform combinatorial proof of the integral cohomology presentation for all $n \geq 2$. This presentation is natural with respect to weak maps and identifies cohomology rings with higher Orlik-Solomon algebras extending the known formulas for linear arrangements to non-realizable oriented matroids. Finally, we equip Deligne groupoids with a presheaf structure and identify them functorially with the fundamental groupoids of the complexified complements.

papers.title: The Calabi-Yau and Sullivan conjectures for minimal surfaces with symmetries
papers.abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite group acting on a connected open Riemann surface \(X\) by holomorphic automorphisms and acting on a Euclidean space \(\mathbb R^n\), \(n\ge 3\), by orthogonal transformations. In a previous paper, the second author gave a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a \(G\)-equivariant conformal minimal immersion \(F:X\to\mathbb R^n\), and he asked whether such \(F\) can be chosen to be a proper map. Assuming that this condition holds, we give an affirmative answer when \(X\) is a bordered Riemann surface and \(G\) acts freely on the boundary of \(X\). This contributes to the Sullivan conjecture concerning the existence of proper hyperbolic minimal surfaces in \(\mathbb R^3\) of finite topology. Under the same conditions, we also construct a \(G\)-equivariant proper conformal minimal immersion of \(X\) to the unit ball of \(\mathbb R^n\) which is complete in the induced metric, thereby opening a new direction in the Calabi--Yau theory regarding the study of complete bounded minimal surfaces. Analogous results hold for null curves in \(\mathbb C^n\).

papers.title: Positive Planar Measures for Spectral Pinching and the Corrected BMV Conjecture
papers.authors: Trung Hoa Dinh, Cong Trinh Le, Trung Dung Vuong
papers.abstract: We prove the corrected Bessis--Moussa--Villani pinching conjecture for all symmetrized word averages. For Hermitian matrices $A,B$ and $D=E_A(B)$, we construct a positive compactly supported measure $\zeta_{A,B}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ such that \[ \Tr f(xA+yB)-\Tr f(xA+yD) =y^2\int_{\mathbb R^2}f''(xa+yb)\,d\zeta_{A,B}(a,b). \] Its total mass is $\frac12\|B-D\|_2^2$. This representation proves the corrected conjecture, including its equality cases, and gives a positive bivariate moment representation for the coefficient differences. We also derive complete monotonicity of normalized exponential pinching defects and a comparison with Lie--Trotter approximations. A one-dimensional second-order loss measure is obtained for trace-preserving conditional expectations on finite tracial von Neumann algebras. Finally, we relate $\zeta_{A,B}$ to Hein\"avaara's tracial joint spectral measure by an explicit positive radial transform.

papers.title: The $d$-invariant of surgeries on $2$-component L-space links
papers.abstract: Gorsky, B. Liu and Moore provided a formula for the $d$-invariants of integral surgeries on $2$-component $L$-space links with linking number $0$. This paper generalizes these results to the nonzero linking number case. We describe how the $d$-invariant depends on the definiteness of the framing matrix and provide formulae for certain families of positive definite framings, as well as a skein relation for non-algebraically split links.

papers.title: Quantitative nodal domain count for Maass forms
papers.abstract: We consider a real even Hecke-Maass cusp form $\phi$ on the modular surface, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. We prove that its restriction to any fixed compact segment $\beta$ of the vertical geodesic above $i$ has $\gg_{\beta,\varepsilon} T^{1/6-\varepsilon}$ sign changes, yielding the same lower bound for the number of distinct inert nodal domains meeting the segment. Building on ideas of Jang-Jung and Jung-Young, we study correlations between values at points on the vertical geodesic separated by distances of order $T^{-1}$. Using arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity and Dirichlet-polynomial estimates, we show that the correlation is negative for a suitable choice of separation. An elementary counting argument and the Iwaniec-Sarnak supremum bound then give the claimed lower bound.

papers.title: The permutation and automorphism groups of univariate multiplicity codes
papers.authors: Eduardo Camps Moreno, Hiram H. L\'opez, Umberto Mart\'inez-Pe\~{n}as, Rodrigo San-Jos\'e
papers.abstract: We give explicit characterizations of the permutations and linear isometries that leave (univariate) multiplicity codes invariant. We consider any evaluation subset of the finite field, any multiplicity and dimension, and the automorphisms are with respect to the Niederreiter-Rosenblom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric. For multiplicity one, we recover the permutation and automorphism groups of classical Reed--Solomon codes in the classical Hamming metric. In the main dimension range, automorphisms are uniquely determined by a projectivity that permutes the evaluation subset, up to multiplication by a nonzero scalar. For multiplicity one, permutations are given by affine maps that permute the evaluation subset. In contrast, for multiplicity at least two, permutations are only given by translations that permute the evaluation subset. Finally, we give an algebraic characterization of automorphisms of multiplicity codes for the folded Hamming metric.

papers.title: Multilevel Monte Carlo for Polytopic DG Discretisations with Spatially Represented Random Coefficients
papers.authors: Veronika Chronholm, Matt Evans, Emmanuil H. Georgoulis, Tristan Pryer
papers.abstract: We develop a multilevel Monte Carlo framework for coercive elliptic problems with random diffusion and reaction coefficients on polytopic meshes, with particular emphasis on the approximation and inter-level coupling of random coefficients generated from spatially represented latent fields. The main analytical contribution is a Strang-type error decomposition in a DG norm that separates the forward discretisation error from the error introduced by approximating the random coefficients. On this basis, we study two coefficient-generation and multilevel-coupling strategies, a spectral sampler based on a stationary Gaussian latent field defined on a fixed Cartesian reference grid, and an SPDE-based Mat\'ern sampler in which levels are coupled through projected white-noise loads on agglomerated hierarchies. Both fit into the same coefficient-aware analytical framework and couple adjacent levels directly through a common latent random input. The theory is supported by numerical experiments on general Voronoi and agglomerated polytopic meshes, demonstrating the predicted forward and coefficient-representation errors, decay of multilevel corrections, strong inter-level coupling, and the resulting work-accuracy behaviour relative to single-level Monte Carlo.

papers.title: Bounded compositions and products of chains, or bi(s)nomials everywhere from de Moivre's formula to spin multiplicities and constant-sum codes
papers.authors: Hac\`{e}ne Belbachir, Jos\'{e} Ricardo G. Mendon\c{c}a
papers.abstract: How many ways are there to select $k$ objects from $n$ types when type $i$ is available in only $s_{i}$ copies? For equal bounds, this is de Moivre's problem of obtaining a prescribed total with $n$ dice, now a textbook application of the principle of inclusion-exclusion. For arbitrary bounds, the answer is encoded by the rank polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1+x+\cdots+x^{s_{i}})$. Its coefficients enumerate bounded compositions and submultisets, give, after normalization, the probability mass function of a sum of independent discrete uniform random variables, and are the weight multiplicities of a tensor product of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ representations. Most of these interpretations are classical but dispersed; here we place them in a common notation and document their provenance. A complement involution proves symmetry and boundary identities. For arbitrary bounds, lower-half first differences give both symmetric-chain starts and mixed-spin multiplicities, and the chain-length and irreducible-dimension profiles agree. Convolution gives log-concavity and the central mode. For equal bounds with fixed $s \geq 1$ and even $ns$, local expansions give central asymptotics with explicit $1/n$ and $1/n^{2}$ corrections for the coefficient and its first difference. A Poisson limit gives the first boundary crossover of these differences at scale $k \sim \lambda n^{s/(s+1)}$, with factor $e^{-\alpha\lambda^{s+1}}$ when the proportion of bounds equal to the fixed minimum $s \geq 1$ tends to $\alpha>0$. Central first differences include the $s$-Catalan numbers, themselves Littlewood-Richardson coefficients; central layers yield maximum-size constant-sum codebooks for hash-based signatures. Under the polynomial binomial convention, the full inclusion-exclusion transform vanishes, and the omitted terms sum to the negative of the number of bounded compositions.

papers.title: A generalization of Gordon's Theorem to arbitrary winding number
papers.abstract: We study minimizers of the Keplerian action functional with homogeneous potential of type $1/|u|^\alpha$ on periodic loops with fixed winding number $k \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. This extends the classical theorems of Gordon and Venturelli, closing the previously open case $\alpha \in (1,2)$, $|k|\geq 2$. We show that the $k$-circular solution loses local minimality below the threshold $\alpha = 2-1/|k|^2$, and that minimizers are collision-free above $\alpha = 2-1/|k|$. Combining these results with the existence of precessing periodic orbits in between, we obtain a full classification of the minimizer in terms of $\alpha$ and $k$, which we also verify numerically for $k=2$.

papers.title: Observability from measurable sets for strongly coupled parabolic systems
papers.abstract: We characterize observability of strongly coupled parabolic systems from arbitrary space-time measurable sets of positive measure. For constant coercive diffusion matrices and arbitrary constant zeroth-order coupling and observation matrices, observability holds if and only if the generalized Kalman rank condition is satisfied at every Dirichlet eigenvalue. The diffusion matrix need not be diagonalizable, and the number of components is arbitrary. The observation is measured in $L^1$, yielding null controllability with bounded controls by duality. The proof combines a Remez-type inequality for exponential polynomials with a quantitative analysis of the mode-dependent Kalman condition. The resulting finite-dimensional observability estimate is uniform over the spatial modes up to a polynomial frequency loss. A spectral inequality and the Lebeau--Robbiano strategy then give observability of the full system.

papers.title: Profinite groups whose closed subgroups are subnormal of defect at most two
papers.authors: A. L. P. Porto, I. Lima, M. Silva
papers.abstract: In this paper, we classify profinite groups whose closed subgroups are subnormal of defect at most two, providing profinite versions of theorems due to Heineken and to Mahdavianary. We also establish that if G is a finitely generated periodic pro-{\pi} group, where {\pi} is a finite set of odd primes, and all its procyclic subgroups are subnormal of defect at most 2, then G is a finite {\pi}-group in which every abelian subgroup is subnormal of defect at most 2.

papers.title: Comparison of Logarithmic Hochschild Homologies
papers.abstract: We construct a comparison morphism $\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Rog}}\to\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Ols}}$ between Rognes' logarithmic Hochschild homology and Olsson's logarithmic Hochschild homology which generalizes the comparison between Gabber's log cotangent complex $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{Gab}}$ and Olsson's log cotangent complex $\mathbb{L}^{\mathrm{Ols}}.$ In particular, Olsson's comparison is recovered as the first associated graded piece of our comparison morphism $\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Rog}}\to\operatorname{HH}^{\mathrm{Ols}}.$ In the development of this comparison, we also prove a descent result for the cotangent complex generalizing a result of Bhatt, and construct a notion of HKR completed Hochschild homology for a general morphism of derived stacks which is functorial in the morphism and generalizes existing constructions of Hochschild homology when the base is affine.

papers.title: A frame-indifferent rank-one convex function in three dimensions which is not quasiconvex
papers.authors: Sergio Conti, Georg Dolzmann, Patrick Dondl
papers.abstract: We construct a function $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times3}\to\mathbb{R}$ which is frame-indifferent, $W(QF)=W(F)$ for all $Q\in\mathrm{SO}(3)$, rank-one convex, but not quasiconvex. In a neighbourhood of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ the function is an explicit polynomial of degree four in the strain $F^TF-\mathrm{Id}$; the failure of quasiconvexity occurs at $F=\mathrm{Id}$ through a third-order mechanism of \v{S}ver\'ak type, with test functions whose gradients are arbitrarily close to $\mathrm{Id}$. The polynomial is obtained from a geometrically linear example, a rank-one convex, non-quasiconvex quartic polynomial of the symmetric part of the gradient, by evaluating it at the strain $\frac12(F^TF-\mathrm{Id})$, adding a uniaxial prestress and a cubic correction, and enlarging the quartic term. The local function is extended to all of $\mathbb{R}^{3\times3}$ by adding a frame-indifferent polyconvex function which vanishes near $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. This work was carried out with the assistance of the AI model Claude Opus 5.5; the proofs of the main results have been formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Pointwise Riesz potential bounds for rough singular integrals
papers.abstract: We give a complete characterization of the kernels $\Omega\in \Lup^1(\Sp)$ for which the rough singular integral $\T_\Omega$ and the associated maximal operator $\M_\Omega$ satisfy pointwise bounds by $\Int_1(|\nabla \cdot|)$ and $\M_1(|\nabla \cdot|)$, respectively, where $\Int_1$ is the Riesz potential and $\M_1$ is the fractional maximal operator. These bounds hold if and only if $\Omega$ belongs to the homogeneous dual Sobolev space $\dot \W^{-1,\infty}(\Sp)$. Equivalently, $\Omega=\text{div}_\Sp \mathbf{V}$ for some bounded vector field $\mathbf{V}$ on the sphere, or $\big|\int_E\Omega\big|\leq C\,\mathcal H^{d-2}(\partial E)$ for every open set $E\subseteq\Sp$ with smooth boundary. On the Lebesgue scale, we show that for $d\geq3$ the condition $\Omega\in\Lup^{d-1,\infty}(\Sp)$, together with mean zero, suffices, and that the exponent $d-1$ is sharp. Finally, in dimension $d=2$, we use complex-analytic methods to prove a new pointwise bound in terms of the complex derivative $\bar\partial f$ that is valid for every mean-zero $\Omega\in\Lup^1(\mathbb S^1)$. As a consequence, we obtain new Sobolev bounds for rough singular integrals in the plane.

papers.title: Geometric Quantities in Spray Geometry and Their Applications to Finsler Geometry
papers.abstract: In this paper we give an overview of several developments in spray geometry and provide some further interpretations of the geometric quantities that arise naturally in this subject. We discuss, in particular, the $S$-curvature, the $\chi$-curvature, and several notions of Ricci curvature for sprays. We rederive a number of identities relating these quantities and explain their applications to locally projectively flat sprays and to projectively related sprays. We also discuss applications to Finsler geometry, with emphasis on the $\chi$-curvature of a Finsler metric and on the inverse problem of determining whether a given spray is induced by a Finsler metric.

papers.title: Associated primes and v-numbers of integral closures of powers of edge ideals
papers.authors: Trung Chau, Tai Huy Ha, Thanh Vu
papers.abstract: Let $I = I(G)$ be the edge ideal of a finite simple graph $G$. We investigate the relationship between the associated primes and $v$-numbers of powers $I^t$ and their integral closures $\overline{I^t}$. For the third power, we establish the associated prime containment $\operatorname{Ass}(S/\overline{I^3}) \subseteq \operatorname{Ass}(S/I^3)$, which yields $v(I^3) \le v(\overline{I^3})$. In contrast, for $t \ge 4$, we show that $\operatorname{Ass}(S/\overline{I^t})$ and $\operatorname{Ass}(S/I^t)$ are in general incomparable. Furthermore, for every fixed $t \ge 3$ and $r\ge 4$, we construct families of graphs for which the discrepancies $v(\overline{I^t}) - v(I^t)$ and $v(I^r)-v(\overline{I^r})$ are arbitrarily large.

papers.title: On Parameterization of Some Problems in Number Theory
papers.abstract: The article is devoted to the parametric solution of some Diophantine equations with two variables. In essence, we find an additional parametric relationship between the solution of the original equation and the simpler linear equation ax - by = 1. The method of hidden parameters helps to obtain a parametric representation of integer solutions for a number of problems in number theory. The method consists in that, first, instead of each quantity included in the original equation, we introduce an additional number of parameters using a linear or non-linear function, which allows us to find both connections between the parameters and some parametric solution of the desired equation. Then we reset (nullify) the introduced linear or non-linear functional dependence (hidden parameters), which in the original formulation of the problem would mean just changing the letter designation of the parameters. However, as a result of these actions, a simplified parametric solution is obtained and the found relationship between the parameters remains. In this paper, the method is discussed in detail using the example of parametric solving such Diophantine equation as the Pell equation. The method of such parameterization is also applied to problems related to Pell's equation. The methods of parameterization are discussed for the Delaunay equation, the Nagell equation and similar equations of higher powers.

papers.title: The Pu inequality and the Viterbo conjecture with finite symmetry
papers.abstract: We study a construction for producing Finsler metrics on the sphere from convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^4$ using the quaternions. Among several applications, we prove the weak Viterbo conjecture for convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^4$ that are invariant under the natural action of the quaternion group $Q$. This is the first instance where Viterbo's systolic inequality is established for convex bodies with a finite group symmetry, addressing a question of Haim-Kislev-Ostrover. Moreover, a smooth $Q$-symmetric convex domain that achieves equality is symplectomorphic to the ball, without any assumption of strict or uniform convexity. Finally, we show that any link of minimal Reeb orbits on the boundary of a uniformly convex $Q$-symmetric convex body is transversely isotopic to a union of Hopf fibers, strengthening a result of Abbondandolo-Edtmair-Kang in the $Q$-symmetric setting.

papers.title: Polarized Ensemble Kalman Inversion: A Derivative-Free Method for Multimodal Inverse Problems with Non-asymptotic Analysis
papers.abstract: Inverse problems often admit multiple solutions consistent with the same noisy, indirect observations, especially with sparse data and/or strongly nonlinear forward models. Ensemble Kalman inversion (EKI) provides a robust, derivative-free framework to solve inverse problems, but its global empirical covariances couple all ensemble members across distinct solution modes, limiting its effectiveness for multimodal problems. We introduce polarized ensemble Kalman inversion (PEKI), which constructs distance-weighted local covariances for each ensemble member. This localization weakens contributions from distant, data-consistent regions and enables different clusters of ensemble members to evolve toward distinct solution modes. For the practical algorithm with finite ensemble size and polarization radius, we also establish non-asymptotic bounds and perform numerical studies, showing that cross-cluster effects decay exponentially with cluster separation relative to the polarization radius. For linear forward maps, we further establish particle-wise residual contraction and derive an exact cluster-mean decomposition that separates cross-cluster leakage, within-cluster gain variation, and observation perturbations. These results further motivate a one-step procedure for choosing the polarization radius by reusing stored forward-model evaluations. We studied the performance of PEKI on several numerical experiments, including low-dimensional nonconvex benchmarks, a problem equipped with many-mode landscape, and a high-dimensional inverse problem governed by Navier--Stokes equations. The results confirm the theoretical exponential decay of cross-cluster effects and show that PEKI can serve as a robust and derivative-free method for inverse problems with multiple solution modes.

papers.title: Effective Multiplicative Ergodic Theorems for Banach Space Cocycles
papers.abstract: The multiplicative ergodic theorem (MET) describes the asymptotic growth rates of $q$-volumes under the iterates of an operator cocycle, i.e., compositions of operators driven by a stationary process, organizing the underlying space into equivariant filtrations or splittings into so called Oseledets subspaces. For operator cocycles in finite dimensions, and more generally in Hilbert spaces, one can control the geometry of the Oseledets subspaces given by the MET via the convergence rates of finite-time volume growth data. This makes the MET "effective" for matrix and Hilbert-space operator cocycles. We extend this effective theory to cocycles of Banach-space operators, obtaining quantitative angle estimates that are new even in the finite-dimensional setting. We take a sequential approach \`{a} la Raghunathan and Ruelle, allowing us to separate the geometric argument of the MET from measure-theoretic considerations. This permits weaker cocycle measurability hypotheses for the non-invertible and semi-invertible METs on a broad class of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones. As an application, we establish the MET for transfer operator cocycles on $\operatorname{BV}[0,1]$ associated with jointly measurable random Lasota-Yorke maps.

papers.title: Elliptic curve rank growth in multi-quadratic extensions
papers.abstract: In this article we give an algorithm to produce infinitely many explicit quadratic twists of a given elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with a rational point and fixed root number. Moreover, under the Parity Conjecture (or other technical hypotheses), for each $n\geq 1$, we produce explicit multi-quadratic extensions $L_n$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, of degree $2^n$, such that the growth in rank from $\mathbb{Q}$ to $L_n$ is at least $\max\{2n+2^{n-1}-1,\,2^n-1\}$ when the root number of $E$ is $-1$, and at least $\max\{2n,\,2^{n-1}\}$ when it is $+1$. As a result, assuming Parity, we exhibit elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ and extensions of degree $2^n$ where the rank after base-extension is greater than or equal to $34$ or $30+\max\{2n+2^{n-1},\,2^n\}$.

papers.title: Flexibility of topological entropy and factor persistence in the $C^0$-Gromov Hausdorff topology
papers.abstract: We prove that every surjective topological dynamical system on a compact metric space can be approximated in the $C^0$-Gromov--Hausdorff topology by homeomorphisms with any prescribed topological entropy in $[0,+\infty]$, even when simultaneous approximation of its sets of invariant and ergodic measures is required. We also establish a rigidity result under uniform geometric bounds in a fixed dimension: for a homeomorphism of a closed, connected Riemannian manifold, topological stability in the sense of Gromov--Hausdorff guarantees its persistence as a factor of sufficiently close perturbations within the same geometric class. This persistence prevents topological entropy from decreasing and ensures that every invariant or ergodic measure of the original system admits a lift of the same type to the perturbed system.

papers.title: The space of equators has infinite Hofer's diameter
papers.abstract: We settle several questions about Hofer's geometry of the two-sphere. We prove that the space of equators has infinite Hofer diameter, construct simple commutators of arbitrarily large Hofer norm, and exhibit a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism whose iterates escape to infinity in Hofer distance from the set of autonomous diffeomorphisms. Finally, we construct a bi-Lipschitz group monomorphism from the free group of rank two, equipped with its conjugation-invariant generator norm, into the Hamiltonian group equipped with Hofer's metric. The proof rests on an interplay between Lagrangian Floer theory in the fourth symmetric product of the sphere and combinatorial group theory. This paper was written with substantial assistance from AI.

papers.title: Probabilistic representation and Monte Carlo method for nonlinear Dirac equations
papers.authors: Jean-Pierre Fouque, Tomoyuki Ichiba, Ka Lok Lam
papers.abstract: Dirac equations describe the relativistic evolution of quantum particles. Using the point-process stochastic calculus of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMPs) on general state spaces, which naturally allows additional Feynman-Kac potentials, we develop a probabilistic representation for the nonlinear Dirac equations in $1+1$ spacetime dimension with cubic nonlinearity and $L_\infty$-type problem data using a multi-type branching telegraph process together with both continuous and jump-type multiplicative functionals. Our main theorem leads to a classification result which, when applied to the specific Soler model, gives a sharp finite-time admissibility of the probabilistic representation. By extending the one-step representation to a multi-step, time-marching representation using an analytically-derived a priori $L_\infty$ estimate, we observe a ``local probabilistic representation, but global PDE well-posedness" phenomenon. We proceed to propose a time-marching Monte Carlo algorithm as a global numerical solver for the Soler system with a rigorous convergence proof and establish an additional stability result on the PDE side. Finally, while the underlying process parameters do not affect the validity of the probabilistic representation, we observe their potential for variance reduction in the Monte Carlo methods.

papers.title: Mean estimation in spatial functional data
papers.abstract: Functional mean estimation exhibits a sparse-to-dense phase transition as the number of measurements per curve increases. For spatially indexed functional data, however, dependence between nearby curves and increasing spatial sampling density fundamentally alter this transition. We investigate this phenomenon under a unified framework allowing both increasing-domain and infill asymptotics, with irregular temporal observations. Our analysis identifies two distinct sources of estimation error: an observation-level component governed by the total number of measurements and a curve-level component governed by a spatial dependence-adjusted effective sample size. The resulting uniform convergence rates reveal how spatial dependence shifts the temporal phase-transition boundary and how spatial infill can improve estimation through additional measurements without a corresponding increase in effective curve-level information. We establish these results for three spline-based estimators: a pooled estimator of a stationary mean curve, a local-kernel estimator, and a tensor-product estimator of a spatially varying mean surface. The effects of spatial localization on the phase transition are characterized explicitly. Simulations illustrate the interplay between spatial dependence and temporal sampling density, and environmental data applications demonstrate the proposed estimation methods.

papers.title: Perturbed Exponential Systems, Pattern-Dependent Shifted-Sinc Operators, and Matrix Symbols on Finite Unions of Intervals
papers.abstract:
We study perturbed exponential systems and unions of shifted frequency lattices through shifted-sinc operators and finite-dimensional fiberizations. For the auxiliary binary local-shift model, we identify the exact pattern-dependent invariant $$ \rho_{\delta,s}=\|P_-T_{2\delta}P_+\|, $$ which gives the optimal squared synthesis bounds $1\pm\rho_{\delta,s}$. For periodic patterns, the synthesis operator reduces exactly to a single constant Vandermonde-type matrix, yielding finite-dimensional basis criteria and optimal bounds. We further prove that the worst binary lower bound is the infimum of its periodic counterparts; at the critical value $\delta=1/4$, a step pattern is governed by a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has vanishing lower bound, although every fixed periodic pattern remains invertible.
  We also combine exact bounds for structured patterns with a support-independent perturbation estimate, obtaining explicit stability neighborhoods. For finite unions of bounded intervals and finitely many shifted lattices, folding modulo one yields finitely many rectangular phase matrices whose singular values and ranks give the exact bounds and complete Riesz-sequence, frame, and Riesz-basis criteria. This framework also yields finite Hadamard constraints for periodic spectra and an exact reduction of rationally commensurate multirate sampling.

papers.title: Spectrum of the basilica group and the associated real and complex 2D dynamics
papers.authors: Eric Bedford, Rostislav Grigorchuk, Nguyen-Bac Dang, Mikhail Lyubich
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the iteration over the real and complex loci of a specific rational map, found by Grigorchuk and Zuk. This two dimensional map arises as the renormalization map which yields the density of states measure associated with the iterated monodromy group of the Basilica Julia set. It admits two natural complex currents, and we construct their real analogs and show that they are laminar. Finally, this yields some consequences on the properties of the density of states measures and its support.

papers.title: On perfectoid ideals
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study perfectoid ideals using the reduction modulo $p$ of perfectoid rings. We show that perfectoid ideals correspond to ideals in the reduction modulo $p$ on which Frobenius is surjective. We establish the existence of universal $p$-adic power series whose evaluations, together with their compatible $p$-power roots, generate perfectoidizations of ideals. In the special case of the perfectoidization of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/p^{\infty}}\rangle/(t-1)$, we describe a linear algebra algorithm for computing finite approximations of such generators. We illustrate this by an explicit approximation modulo $8$ of an element $\sigma\in (t-1)_{\mathrm{perfd}}\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_2^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/2^{\infty}}\rangle$ which admits compatible sequences of $2$-power roots and satisfies $\sigma\equiv t-1\pmod{2}$.

papers.title: Trivial Iwasawa modules and arithmetic linking numbers
papers.abstract: We give a computable criterion of the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa module over the maximal multiple $\mathbb Z_p$-extension of a number filed in which an odd prime number $p$ splits completely. This criterion is obtained from the description of the presentation matrix of the Galois coinvariant of the Iwasawa module by arithmetic linking numbers. The description is based on the Koch type presentation of a pro-$p$ Galois group with restricted ramification, which is analogous to the Milnor presentation of a link group from a viewpoint of arithmetic topology.

papers.title: Swapping Compatible Words
papers.abstract: In 1981 Guibas and Odlyzko showed that the set $A$ of all words of a given length $n$ that avoid a given word $p$, and the set $B$ of all words of length $n$ that avoid a given word $q$, have the same cardinality iff $p$ and $q$ have the same self-border lengths. In 2024 Carrigan et. al. asked if there is a "natural" bijection between $A$ and $B$. This paper makes partial progress toward answering that question. We provide such a bijection by imposing additional conditions on $p$ and $q$, but we also obtain a stronger conclusion: there is a "natural" bijection $\Phi$ from the set of all finite words to itself such that a word $\Omega$ has a $p$ or $q$ at a given position iff $\Phi(\Omega)$ has, repectively, a $q$ or a $p$ at that same position. An algorithm is given for converting $\Omega$ into $\Phi(\Omega)$.

papers.title: Closed-form Optimal Solutions for Propulsive-Differential Drag Control of Spacecraft Swarms
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel optimal control approach for Distributed Space Systems (DSS) to minimize the total delta-v cost for large, time-constrained reconfigurations. Reconfiguration cost is decreased by blending differential drag and propulsive control within the same control window. By parameterizing the problem with Relative Orbital Elements (ROE) and leveraging reachable set theory, a maneuver planning methodology is derived to produce provably-optimal, full roto-translational control solutions in closed-form, such that they can be implemented on hardware-limited spacecraft.

papers.title: Closed-form Optimal Propulsive-Differential Drag Control for Large Reconfigurations of Spacecraft Swarms
papers.abstract: Distributed Space Systems offer unique capabilities but have significant hardware limitations on computational processing and fuel when employing small satellites. These constraints drive interest in deterministic maneuver planning that incorporates orbital perturbations to improve final state accuracy and decrease reconfiguration delta-v cost. This paper proposes a novel closed-form, provably optimal framework to generate complete roto-translational solutions for propulsive-differential drag control of multiple satellites. The approach leverages relative orbit elements and reachable set theory to characterize all control with a single methodology that can be readily generalized to generic impulsive-continuous control. The algorithm is robust to large reconfigurations and extended control windows where differential drag is most effective.

papers.title: Optimal Graphon Control of Collective Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study optimal control of non-linear graphon dynamics in which the interaction kernel itself is the control. Motivated by opinion formation in social networks, we ask how changing who influences whom can steer a population toward a desired outcome. We develop a framework using interaction kernels with bounded variation in the receiver label, providing compactness while accommodating finite networks. We prove existence of an optimal pair and show that finite-agent approximations recover the continuum optimal value under successive refinement of the network and initial data, with subsequential convergence of suitably chosen discrete optimizers. Numerical experiments use neural networks to approximate optimal controls for bounded-confidence and graphon Kuramoto dynamics, illustrating how changes in interactions can prevent fragmentation and promote synchronization.

papers.title: Coefficient Positivity for Arborescence Ratios of Covering Digraphs
papers.authors: Muchen Ju, Junjie Ni, Kaixin Wang, Yihan Xiao
papers.abstract:
For a directed graph with a chosen root, the arborescence polynomial sums the products of edge weights over all spanning trees directed toward that root. In a finite graph cover, each lifted edge inherits the variable of its base edge. At corresponding roots, the ratio of the cover's arborescence polynomial to the base polynomial is known to be an integer polynomial. We prove that every coefficient of this ratio is nonnegative, resolving the positivity conjecture of Pylyavskyy.
  The key to the proof is to allow fibers of unequal size and replace the permutations defining a cover by arbitrary maps. For these more general systems, we prove a stronger coefficient-positivity theorem for a determinant derived from the graph Laplacian. The enlarged class is closed under two reductions: contraction of an edge over a base loop and elimination of a base vertex. Both yield nonnegative recurrences for the relevant coefficients in terms of smaller systems, allowing an inductive proof. We also pose the problem of finding a direct combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients.

papers.title: A Novel Matrix-Free Approximate Elemental Inverse for Efficient Preconditioning of Discontinuous Galerkin Spectral Elements
papers.abstract: Efficient matrix-free preconditioning remains a challenge for discontinuous Galerkin spectral element discretisations of elliptic problems, particularly for general element shapes with collapsed-coordinate bases, such as prisms, tetrahedra and pyramids. Multigrid provides a promising framework, but its efficiency depends strongly on the effectiveness and computational cost of the smoother. For modal bases, point Jacobi can provide insufficient smoothing, whereas applying block Jacobi through stored dense inverses incurs substantial storage and computational costs. We propose a matrix-free approximate elemental inverse, an approximation to the inverse of each elemental diagonal block, constructed from inverse modal-to-nodal transforms and an element-dependent sparse matrix. Its application exploits generalised sum-factorisation and partial sum-factorisation in collapsed coordinates, avoiding the explicit storage and multiplication of large dense matrices. The method is evaluated as both a standalone preconditioner and a multigrid smoother on hexahedral, prismatic, tetrahedral and pyramidal elements. Although the proposed approximation generally increases iteration counts compared to exact block Jacobi, the cost per iteration is far lower. This trade-off yields substantial reductions in total solution time for hexahedral and prismatic elements, while achieving comparable performance for tetrahedral and pyramidal elements. This study can also serve as a practical guide for tuning the convergence of the discontinuous Galerkin interior-penalty Poisson solver.

papers.title: Reflected BSDEs under random horizons: Sharp support criteria, irregular reflection, and Cox reconstruction
papers.abstract: We study reduction and reconstruction of reflected backward stochastic differential equations (RBSDEs) across random horizons. We establish optional and predictable contact-measure transfer criteria by dual projection, prove a Cox survival identity for arbitrary integrable reflection measures (including atoms), and give a Brownian Cox reconstruction theorem with continuous obstacles and a converse within a specified reduction class. We also isolate componentwise minimality criteria for irregular obstacles and predictable reflection. The unresolved semimartingale and obstacle transport problems for general non-Cox invariance times are formulated as open questions rather than asserted as theorems. The paper distinguishes established results from conditional constructions.

papers.title: A Globally Convergent Newton Method for Nonsmooth Optimization in the absence of Smooth Surrogates
papers.authors: Tran T. A. Nghia, Nghia V. Vo, Khoa V. H. Vu
papers.abstract: We propose a globally convergent Newton method for convex composite optimization problems with polyhedral regularizers. The method rests on the observation that the proximal gradient step yields not only a new point but also a subgradient, which determines the face on which the linearization of the regularizer is exact. Minimizing a second-order model of the objective over this face produces a Newton direction that involves no generalized second-order information about the regularizer and is a descent direction for the objective itself. The method is therefore globalized by an Armijo line search on the original objective which, unlike forward-backward envelope techniques, requires only evaluations of the smooth component. We establish global convergence and local quadratic convergence to tilt-stable minimizers without any nondegeneracy condition, and show that the unit step is always accepted when the smooth component is quadratic, which yields a line-search-free method. The subproblems require only projections onto faces, which are explicit for the Lasso and nonnegative least squares and computable in linear time for the fused Lasso. Numerical experiments show that the method compares favorably with state-of-the-art solvers.

papers.title: Sobolev Orthogonal Polynomials on the unit circle with varying inner product
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the validity of the Szeg\"o type strong asymptotic formula for the Sobolev orthogonal polynomials associated with a Sobolev-type inner product depending on a parameter $s$, which is defined as \begin{equation*} \langle f,g\rangle _{\frac{\lambda}{n^s}}:= \int_{\mathbb{T}} f(z)\overline{g(z)} d\mu_1(z)+ \dfrac{\lambda}{n^s} \int_{\mathbb{T}} f^{\prime}(z)\overline{g^{\prime}(z)} d\mu_2(z), \quad \text{where $s$ is fixed and } \quad s\geq 2, \end{equation*} and $\lambda >0$. Here, $\mu_1$, $\mu_2$ are absolutely continuous with respect to the normalized lebesgue measure and $\int_{\mathbb{T}} \mu^{\prime}_i(z) dm=1$, where $\mu_i^{\prime}(z)= \dfrac{d\mu_i}{dm} >0$ for $i=1,2$. Further, $\mu_1, \mu_2$ belongs to the Szeg\"o class and also has non-zero bounded Radon-Nikodym derivatives on the unit circle. %satisfies $ 0 <m \leq \dfrac{\mu^{\prime}_1(e^{\iota \theta})}{\mu^{\prime}_2(e^{\iota \theta})}\leq M < \infty $. We observe that the measure appearing in the Szeg\"o function of the strong asymptotic limit depends on $s$. As a specific case, we consider the Bernstein-Christoffel Sobolev orthogonal polynomials and study their properties, including the asymptotic distribution and location of their zeros for different values of $s$. We further establish a spectral characterization of their zeros as the eigenvalue of an explicitly constructed modification of the associated Hessenberg matrix and provide numerical evidence supporting the obtained asymptotic and zeros results.

papers.title: Polychromatic blocks and explicit lower bounds for multicolour van der Waerden numbers
papers.abstract: Let $W(r,k)$ be the least $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ contains a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression. Many of the best lower bounds for $W(r,k)$ with $r\ge3$ come from blow-up recurrences of Blankenship, Cummings and Taranchuk and of Xu, in which a known colouring is lengthened by a periodic block. Call an $h$-colouring of $Z_q$ $k$-polychromatic if every $k$-term progression with nonzero common difference meets each of the $h$ colours. The argument behind these recurrences shows that such a colouring gives $W(r,k)>q(W(r-\lceil r/h\rceil,k)-1)$ for all $r\ge h$. We show that cubic, quartic, quintic and sextic residue colourings give $k$-polychromatic blocks with $q$ much larger than $k$ (e.g. $q=1,376,317$ for $h=3$ and $k=28$), and use them to get explicit lower bounds. For three colours and $9\le k\le28$ we improve on every published bound we know of, among them $W(3,9)>4,002,705$ and $W(3,28)>159,594,201,561,100,726$. For $3\le r\le6$ and $9\le k\le28$, $77$ of the $80$ cases improve on what the published bounds give under these recurrences and the other three tie. For $r=5$ and $12\le k\le15$ the best values come from palettes that are cyclic intervals of colours indexed by quintic residues. We checked every block by exhaustive enumeration and every base colouring by computer. We also prove that the block modulus is at most $(W(2,k)-1)/(k-1)$, so the method does not improve the asymptotics. For large $k$ the largest cubic block modulus lies between $k^{4-\varepsilon}$ and $k^2 4^k$.

papers.title: Kashiwara's Lemma for Potent D-modules
papers.abstract: On stacks there is a richer version of $\mathcal{D}$-modules---called $\textit{potent }\mathcal{D}\textit{-modules}$---which decompletes at equivariant parameters, in the same sense that genuine equivariant $K$-theory decompletes equivariant cohomology. In this paper, we prove a ``genuine'' version of Kashiwara's lemma for $\mathcal{D}$-modules. Namely, we show that for a broad class of geometric stacks $X$, if $Z \subset X$ is a closed substack, the category $\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{pot}}(Z)$ of potent $\mathcal{D}$-modules on $Z$ is equivalent under pushforward to the category $\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{pot}} _Z(X)$ of potent $\mathcal{D}$-modules on $X$ with support contained in $Z$.

papers.title: Strengthening AC optimal power flow relaxation through offline bound tightening and linear approximations
papers.authors: Xiangxin An, Constance Crozier, Santanu S. Dey
papers.abstract: The alternating-current optimal power flow (ACOPF) problem is fundamental to power system operation and planning, but its nonconvexity makes globally optimal solutions of large-scale instances computationally challenging. Convex relaxations provide tractable lower bounds for assessing solution quality and supporting global optimization, although their effectiveness depends strongly on relaxation strength. This paper proposes an offline convexification and bound tightening framework for constructing strong linear programming (LP) relaxations for families of related ACOPF instances. Rather than repeating the tightening procedure for each instance, we compute variable bounds and second-order cone outer-approximation (SOC-OA) cuts offline using a demand-slack model and reuse them for subsequent instances with the same topology and admissible demand variations. Computational results on PGLib instances show that the fully offline approach achieves an average gap of $4.32\%$, compared with $3.80\%$ for the fully online approach, while achieving an average speedup of approximately $272\times$. The results demonstrate that offline convexification and bound tightening can recover most of the relaxation improvement of online tightening while significantly reducing the computational burden for repeated ACOPF evaluations.

papers.title: An explicit bound on $|\zeta_K(1+it)|$
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n$ and discriminant $\Delta$. The estimate $|\zeta_K(1+it)|\le C_K\log{t}$, where $C_K$ is an unspecified constant depending on $K$, is a well--known result in the literature. We obtain an explicit upper bound for $|\zeta_K(1+it)|$, depending only on $n$ and $\Delta$. We also show how improvements on the bound depend on improvements on estimates of the ideal counting function $I_K$ and the residue of $\zeta_K$ at $s=1$.

papers.title: Tropical cohomology for band schemes over the tropical hyperfield
papers.abstract: We define tropical band varieties as $\mathbf{T}$-reductions of separated finitely presented $\mathbf{T}$-band schemes. We construct a faithful functor from the category of tropical band varieties to the category of extended polyhedral spaces in the sense of Gross--Shokrieh. As a byproduct, we show that tropical cohomology can be defined functorially on tropical band varieties.

papers.title: Fisher Information and the Minimum Mean-Square Error for Locating Closely Spaced Point Sources
papers.authors: Chuling Wen, Jian Lu, Qingtang Jiang, Charles K. Chui
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal average error of locating closely spaced sources from noisy superpositions of a known smooth response with unknown complex coefficients. Relative phases control how changes in one location can be offset by the other unknowns, so local Fisher information alone does not determine the attainable error. For every fixed number $K\ge2$ of sources with independent uniform phases, we prove matching Bayes risk bounds jointly in separation and noise, for all sufficiently small separations and all noise levels. Odd source counts have two risk regimes; even counts have an intermediate regime in which mean squared error is linear in the noise standard deviation. A projected least-squares estimator attains these orders without knowing the phases or the prior density. Bounded nonuniform phase laws preserve the orders under stated support conditions, whereas priors concentrated near poorly identified configurations can change the exponents. A common finite comparison yields both a global inverse bound and paths controlled by the original prior. These give sufficient conditions under which the risk has the order of the pointwise capped Cram\'er--Rao bound, and a lower-tail calculation explains the power and logarithmic regimes. We also give conditional guarantees when the cluster center, separation, and source count are unknown, with an additional low-noise requirement for count selection. A calibrated covariance factor model illustrates the same criterion beyond source localization.

papers.title: A Kallin's lemma for polynomials with exponents in a compact convex set and local approximation
papers.authors: Kieu Phuong Chi, Duong Thi Thuy Van
papers.abstract: Let $S\subset\Bbb R_+^n$ be compact and convex with $0\in S$, and let $\mathcal{P}^S$ be the algebra spanned by monomials with exponents in $\bigcup_{m\ge0}(mS\cap\Bbb N_0^n)$. We define the associated polynomial hull and prove a Kallin lemma for the union of two sets convex with respect to this algebra. A weighted approximation lemma then shows that, under a sector or ray condition, two admissible monomials generate exactly the functions of the unrestricted algebra that are constant on a specified zero fibre. Applications include an exact density criterion for mixed monomials, a transfer principle for relative perturbations, and density and hull computations on stars of totally real discs.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Jordan structure of $C^*$-algebras from the metric on positive unit spheres
papers.authors: Chi-Wai Leung, Chi-Keung Ng, Ngai-Ching Wong
papers.abstract:
Let $A$ and $B$ be unital $C^*$-algebras, and let $\mathrm{S}_{A^+}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{B^+}$ denote their positive unit spheres. We first show that the diametral relation on the positive unit sphere already determines Jordan structure. More precisely, suppose that $\Lambda:\mathrm{S}_{A^+}\to\mathrm{S}_{B^+}$ is a bijection satisfying \[ \|\Lambda(u)-\Lambda(v)\|=1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \|u-v\|=1 \qquad (u,v\in\mathrm{S}_{A^+}). \] If $A$ has no two-dimensional irreducible $^*$-representation, then $A$ and $B$ are Jordan $^*$-isomorphic. Moreover, the Jordan $^*$-isomorphism can be chosen to be compatible with $\Lambda$ on the peak and zero projections of positive norm-one elements. The proof is based on recovering the order and orthogonality structure of Akemann closed projections in the bidual.
  As a main application, we give an affirmative answer to the positive-sphere extension problem for unital $C^*$-algebras of real rank zero. Namely, if $A$ has real rank zero (but could has two-dimensional irreducible $^*$-representations) and $\Lambda:\mathrm{S}_{A^+}\to\mathrm{S}_{B^+}$ is a surjective isometry, then $\Lambda$ extends to a Jordan $^*$-isomorphism from $A$ onto $B$.

papers.title: Equifacetted polytopes whose facets are products of simplices: The simplicial prism case
papers.authors: Federico Castillo, Guillermo Pi\~neda-Villavicencio, Jos\'e Alejandro Samper
papers.abstract: We study \emph{prismatical} polytopes, those all of whose facets are combinatorially isomorphic to the simplicial prism $\Delta^{d-2}\times\Delta^1$. In dimension three these are exactly the cubical polytopes, so the class sits naturally between simplicial and cubical polytopes. In dimension four, $\Delta^2\times\Delta^2$ is the simplest prismatical polytope and we can construct infinitely many by using connected sums. By fibreing a triangle over a triangulated polygon we construct infinitely many connected-sum-prime prismatical $4$-polytopes. Finally, we show that there are no prismatical $d$-polytopes for $d\ge5$, answering a question of Perles and Shephard.

papers.title: On polarizations of affine Calabi--Yau varieties
papers.abstract: Let $(X, \Omega)$ be an affine Calabi--Yau variety, by which we mean a klt affine variety $X$ with a non-vanishing algebraic volume form $\Omega$. In connection with complete Calabi--Yau metrics of Euclidean volume growth on $(X, \Omega)$, we study algebraic aspects of polarizations of $X$ given by a negative valuation. We show that such a valuation is finitely generated with a klt degeneration if and only if $X$ admits a dlt log Fano type compactification, generalizing a compactification considered by Tian--Yau. We further give a valuative criterion detecting K-semistability of the degeneration by a negative valuation.

papers.title: Amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations and applications to anti-treeability
papers.abstract: We study the structure of amenable subrelations of treeable measure-class-preserving equivalence relations, applying the Radon--Nikodym topography perspective initiated in our companion paper [TTD25]. For a nowhere smooth amenable subrelation, we show that the ends selected by each class in Adams's end selection theorem are precisely those which are nonvanishing along that class. From this, we derive a number of structure results about nowhere smooth amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations. For example, we show that every nowhere smooth amenable subrelation is contained in an essentially unique maximal amenable subrelation. This yields an anti-treeability criterion, which we use to show that every nonamenable locally compact second countable group with noncompact amenable radical is not treeable, and that every nonamenable nonunimodular treeable group has a compact open subgroup.

papers.title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary.
