For incompressible flow, NBM yields a velocity-only formulation whose residual provides an a posteriori velocity-error estimate, establishing a certified, data-free training objective for coefficient learning. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, generalization, and scalability of NBM, with substantial improvements over baselines.

papers.title: An exploration of plug-and-play flow matching for full-waveform inversion on breast imaging
papers.authors: Cristina Garcia-Cardona, Siting Liu, Fatma Terzioglu, Shanyin Tong, Lu Zhang
papers.abstract: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) reconstructs sound-speed fields from measured waveforms, by solving an optimization problem that minimizes the discrepancy between measured waveforms and those predicted by a numerical wave-propagation model. However, choosing suitable regularization for this optimization is challenging because it must stabilize the inversion while preserving relevant structures, prompting us to investigate whether priors learned from representative sound-speed images can improve reconstruction. In this work, we adapt plug-and-play flow matching (PnP-Flow) to FWI by alternating waveform-misfit updates with updates from a pretrained flow prior. We explore the effectiveness of PnP-Flow reconstruction by comparing it with total-variation (TV) regularization using noiseless transmission-only plane-wave data. Separate flow priors are trained on two circular-inclusion model families with constant and spatially varying backgrounds. We evaluate the method both on these in-distribution circle models and under substantial distribution shift by transferring the Gaussian-circle prior and reconstruction settings to breast phantom patches without retraining or retuning. Using the same number of waveform-misfit updates, the proposed PnP-Flow framework generally improves circle reconstruction accuracy and recovers breast lesion contrast more accurately than TV baselines.

papers.title: Freeform Programmable Liquid Crystal Elastomers via Monolithic Integration of Co-Optimization and 4D-Printing
papers.authors: Yibo Wang, Asad Farooq Ahmed, Weichen Li, Weiyun Xu, Xiaojia Shelly Zhang
papers.abstract: Liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) are active materials capable of large, reversible thermally induced actuation, offering significant potential for applications such as artificial muscles and soft robotics. However, their broader deployment is hindered by the lack of a unified design-to-fabrication framework, the strong coupling among geometry, director fields, and manufacturing constraints, and the difficulty of reliably translating complex designs into physically realizable architectures. Here, we present an autonomous and monolithic integration of co-optimization and 4D printing that enables the end-to-end design-to-realization of versatile programmable LCE architectures with superior precision, complexity, and versatility. The proposed framework establishes a unified design strategy that co-optimizes the freeform multilayer geometry and fully continuous layer-specific director distributions, and subsequently translates the optimized fields into fabrication-ready DIW toolpaths through an automated manufacturing-aware pipeline. To bridge computation and realization, we develop an optimization-centered 4D printing approach with automated, fabrication-aware toolpath generation tailored for direct ink writing of LCEs. With the proposed design-to-fabrication paradigm, we experimentally realize architectures that exhibit complex, non-intuitive thermo-mechanical behaviors. Experiments achieve highly challenging prescribed functionalities beyond the reach of intuition-based approaches and show excellent agreement with numerical simulations across all samples. This work establishes a generalizable inverse design and physical realization of freeform programmable LCE systems, enabling function-oriented and optimization-driven intelligent LCE applications for next-generation soft robotic and responsive material engineering.

papers.title: Performing a Quantum Subroutine Using Cluster States
papers.authors: Sakibul Islam Rayhan, Karima Hassan, Md Rasedujjaman, Md Mohsinur Rahman Adnan
papers.abstract: Quantum subroutines, like their classical counterparts, serve as essential components of larger algorithms. They can be realized using gate based architectures or measurement based quantum computation (MBQC), where computation proceeds through adaptive measurements on highly entangled cluster states. In this work, we implement a phase oracle as a reusable subroutine within the MBQC framework using experimentally feasible cluster states. Unlike prior demonstrations of Grover's algorithm in MBQC that omit explicit oracle construction, our approach provides a transparent formulation of the oracle subroutine, including its measurement patterns, byproduct correlations, density-matrix simulations, and corresponding MBQC measurement circuits.

papers.title: Empirically Calibrated Differential Games for Simulating Driver Interactions
papers.authors: Amirmohammad Khakpour (Marco), Nachuan Li (Marco), Pedram Beigi (Marco),  Yu (Marco),  Nie
papers.abstract: Game-theoretic models can resolve vehicle interactions without hand-written priority rules, but whether they describe human drivers once calibrated has rarely been tested. This study formulates a general-sum differential game of vehicle interactions at urban intersections, calibrates it to observed driving, and evaluates it on data not used for calibration. Each vehicle minimizes a cost that combines speed tracking, adherence to a map-derived lane route, control effort, gap keeping based on the intelligent driver model, a predictive conflict term, and a contact barrier, while perceiving the other vehicles with a delay. The game is solved with a feedback iterative linear-quadratic algorithm, and ten behavioral parameters per vehicle are calibrated by Bayesian optimization on trajectories recorded at four intersections in Washington, D.C. The calibrated game reproduces the trajectories of 819 vehicles with a mean position error of 1.00 m. When only each vehicle's route is known, as in a simulator, it is the most accurate of the compared models on 96 held-out vehicles (7.42 m), and ten-fold cross-validation shows that it is significantly more accurate than calibrated SUMO (by 3.61 m), an inverse reinforcement learning model (by 0.93 m), and independent and cooperative variants of the same model (by 0.33 and 0.32 m). The solutions, computed in 2.1 s for a typical interaction, are verified approximate equilibria. Finally, the conflict and steering weights, which the data do not identify, can be set from safety and comfort targets; together with a stiffer contact barrier, this removes the collisions that otherwise occur in 43% of tight closed-loop conflicts.

papers.title: Regret-Based Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control under Uncertain Traffic States
papers.authors: Chaopeng Tan, Qiongdan Hu, Meng Wang
papers.abstract: Max-pressure (MP) traffic signal control selects phases using pressure scores computed from estimated traffic states, but these states are uncertain and their consequences depend on whether they alter phase ranking and how much pressure is lost. This paper develops a decision-oriented Regret-Based Max-Pressure framework that represents uncertainty through phase-selection regret, defined as the pressure loss of a candidate phase relative to the pressure-maximizing phase under each plausible latent state. We propose Stochastic Regret MP, which minimizes expected regret under a calibrated residual distribution, and Distributionally Robust (DR) Regret MP, which minimizes worst-case expected regret over a Wasserstein ambiguity set. Robustifying regret rather than absolute pressure makes the formulation invariant to state-dependent pressure components shared by all candidate phases, thereby focusing robustness on relative phase quality. We further derive an explicit queue-linear pressure-loss bound and establish strong queue stability when the net-service reserve exceeds the resulting loss coefficient. Numerical experiments show that both methods reduce normalized true-state pressure regret by about 70% relative to Point-estimate MP, while DR Regret MP yields lower network queues than direct robustification of absolute pressure. In microscopic SUMO experiments on a 28-intersection real-world network, Stochastic Regret MP and DR Regret MP reduce mean delay by 18.9% and 14.9%, respectively, and retain benefits under detector undercount and failure. The results show that representing uncertainty through its decision consequences can improve reliable traffic control under imperfect state information.

papers.title: Existence and Absence of Spin-Glass Phases on Migdal--Kadanoff Hierarchical Lattices: A Complete Classification
papers.abstract: We consider the Ising spin-glass model on Migdal--Kadanoff (MK) hierarchical lattices, characterized by the fractal dimension $d=1+\log s/\log b$, where $s$ and $b$ denote the number of parallel branches and the number of bonds in series within each branch, respectively. For independent Gaussian couplings, we rigorously establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for arbitrary integers $b,s\ge2$. We prove that a finite-temperature spin-glass phase exists whenever \[ \frac{b}{\sqrt{s}} \left( \frac{b\sqrt{s(s-1)}}{bs-1} \right)^{s-1}<1. \] In particular, this condition holds for all three-dimensional MK hierarchical lattices ($d=3$, or equivalently $s=b^2$), regardless of the choice of $b$. Conversely, we prove the absence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for fractal dimensions $d<1+\log17/\log6\approx2.58$, as well as in the large-$b$ limit for any fixed $d<3$. In the intermediate regime $1+\log17/\log6\le d<3$, we provide a finite-step procedure to determine the presence or absence of spin-glass order, which depends on $b$ and $s$. Our results provide a complete characterization of finite-temperature spin-glass order on MK hierarchical lattices.

papers.title: CoPiT: A conditional Position-induced Transformer for aerodynamic field prediction on unstructured meshes
papers.authors: Junfeng Chen, Yongchen Fan, Zhonghua Qiao, Kailiang Wu
papers.abstract: High-fidelity Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) simulations remain a standard tool for aerodynamic analysis, yet each solve on an unstructured mesh is computationally expensive, making many-query tasks such as design exploration, optimization, and multi-condition evaluation costly. Neural operators provide mesh-flexible surrogates for mapping geometry and operating conditions to flow fields; however, in many existing architectures, global parameters such as the freestream state and design variables are concatenated with pointwise inputs, leaving their influence on intermediate features implicit. This paper proposes CoPiT, a \textbf{Co}nditional \textbf{P}osition-induced \textbf{T}ransformer that builds on the Position-induced Transformer (PiT) as its geometric backbone and injects a global condition vector through multi-stage feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), thereby making parametric modulation explicit while preserving geometry-based attention weights. The model is evaluated on two-dimensional AirfRANS airfoil fields, including scarce-data and extrapolation regimes, and on three-dimensional BlendedNet++ blended-wing-body surfaces. On the AirfRANS full-data test set, CoPiT reduces surface and volume losses by approximately 54\% and 24\% relative to Transolver, respectively, and achieves the lowest overall normalized test MSE among the compared baselines on BlendedNet++. Matched ablations show that FiLM conditioning generally improves upon input concatenation, while the preferred placement is task-dependent. CoPiT thus provides a practical operator-learning surrogate for parametric aerodynamics on unstructured meshes.

papers.title: Dynamics of a Harvested Predator-Prey Model with a Generalized Holling Type~III Response Capturing Group Defense
papers.authors: Wael El Khateeb, Farjana Akter, Chanaka Kottegoda, Muner Mustafa Abou Hasan
papers.abstract: We investigate a predator-prey model with constant prey harvesting and a generalized Holling type III functional response, focusing on the biological and dynamical consequences of allowing the parameter $b$ to be negative. In this regime, predation efficiency declines at high prey densities, potentially reflecting group defense. This change permits an additional coexistence equilibrium and introduces new bifurcation mechanisms affecting population persistence. We establish the existence of a codimension-three Bogdanov--Takens bifurcation, derive a codimension-three nilpotent-saddle unfolding, and investigate a codimension-two generalized Hopf bifurcation and the emergence of multiple limit cycles. Our analysis show that moderate harvesting weakens the protection conferred by high prey abundance; excessive harvesting leaves too few prey to sustain predator growth; and low harvesting preserves strong group defense, requiring high predator density for population persistence.

papers.title: Mapping Academic Sports Analytics: A Content Analysis of JQAS and JSA
papers.abstract: Sports analytics has expanded rapidly in professional sports and mainstream culture, yet defining its academic core remains a challenge. In this paper, we provide an empirical map of the academic sports analytics landscape based on a systematic content analysis of approximately 700 papers published in two leading dedicated journals, the Journal of Quantitative Analysis in Sports (JQAS) and the Journal of Sports Analytics (JSA), between the years 2005 and 2024. We classify each paper by sport discipline, mathematical method, and core research area, identify recurring themes, and examine macro trends. We find game tactics, player evaluation, team ranking, result forecasting, and tournament design to be the most studied research areas in sports analytics. We highlight selected papers in each area, illustrating the wide range of mathematical methods used and sports disciplines analyzed. Our work offers a comprehensive overview of the questions, methods, and disciplines that characterize the field, serving as a foundational reference for practitioners and researchers in sports analytics.

papers.title: A Robust Control Architecture for Multirate Systems and their Interconnections
papers.abstract: We introduce a framework for analyzing and designing linear multirate control systems and their interconnections through the lens of robust control. The proposed approach models multirate systems as impulsive systems with multiple independent jump maps and corresponding jump-time sequences. We tackle analysis and design problems with stability, dissipativity, and robustness objectives, relying on a multi-clock-dependent Lyapunov function parameterization. Further, we develop a compositional approach for analyzing interconnections of multirate systems based on individual dissipativity properties. The theoretical conditions can be verified via linear matrix inequalities and they require weak assumptions on the sampling rates, allowing for asynchronous and time-varying sampling rates with or without separated time scales. The practicality of the framework is demonstrated with numerical examples.

papers.title: Stable Set Reconfiguration in Dense Digraphs
papers.authors: Sarah Houdaigoui, Nacim Oijid, Matthieu Petiteau, Alexandre Vigny
papers.abstract:
In a directed graph, a stable (or acyclic) set is a set which does not induce a directed cycle. Given a directed graph and two acyclic sets of the same size, the Acyclic-Set-Reconfiguration with Directed Token Sliding (ASR) problem asks whether one can, by iteratively replacing a vertex by an adjacent one, transform the first set into the second one, while maintaining acyclicity during the transformation.
  In this work, we present a study of the complexity of ASR and provide an FPT algorithm for semi-complete digraphs, when parametrized by the size of the sets being reconfigured, the directed pathwidth (or equivalently, the directed treewidth) of the instance, and a newly introduced parameter called the iteration of the reconfiguration sequence.
  To the best of our knowledge, the reconfiguration of stable sets has only been studied on undirected graphs, or (more recently) on sparse directed graphs.

papers.title: Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithms
papers.authors: Geetika, Shivani Singh Chauhan, Gauranshi Gupta, Anant Jain, Kaushik Kalyanaraman, Bapi Chatterjee
papers.abstract: Adversarial sharpness penalty per iteration of a base optimizer, known as sharpness-aware minimization (SAM), is an accepted technique to improve generalization in deep learning. Recently, Muon has emerged as a dominant optimization algorithm for training large language models (LLMs). It achieves lower sample complexity for heavy-tailed gradient updates - a phenomenon common in LLM training. However, sharpness penalties with Muon updates are yet largely unexplored in the literature. Moreover, the behavior of SAM under heavy-tailed noise is unknown both theoretically and empirically. A potential reason for this gap is the additional cost of extra gradient computation per iteration for penalty perturbations in SAM, which becomes prohibitive for LLMs. This paper introduces Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithm (SOMA) to combine a computationally efficient and theoretically grounded perturbation scheme with the Muon algorithm. The key idea is to use stale (purely) stochastic gradient noise for adversarial perturbations. Theoretically, we show that SOMA's sample complexity is invariant to the perturbation direction. We provide explorations and insights into SOMA's robustness to heavy-tailed gradient noise. We extensively explore SOMA's efficacy in (a) mitigating quality degradation due to post-training quantization, and (b) catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning of LLMs.

papers.title: L0-Norm-Based CycleGAN for Unpaired Brain CT-to-MR Synthesis
papers.authors: Yunxiao Zhang, Shouqiang Du, Zexian Xu, Chuanlong Xu
papers.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance (MR) imaging provide complementary information for the brain, but acquiring both modalities is not always possible. The cycle-consistent adversarial network (CycleGAN) enables unpaired CT-to-MR synthesis, but because the standard L1-norm cycle?consistency penalty grows linearly with the residual magnitude, the network tends to focus on large residuals. This paper introduces an L0-norm-based cycle?consistency term, in which the L0-norm is approximated by a smooth and bounded function. This approximation not only increases sensitivity to small residuals but also effectively suppresses the influence of large residuals. The proposed model and an otherwise identical L1-norm baseline were trained on 102 images and evaluated on 9 test images. The proposed model achieves a lower mean squared error (0.02746 versus 0.03464, a 20.7% reduction), a higher mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (15.80 versus 14.77 dB), and a higher mean structural similarity index (0.5689 versus 0.5407). It also has a lower maximum MSE and higher minimum PSNR and SSIM than the baseline. These results indicate that modifying the cycle-consistency penalty can improve reconstruction accuracy on this dataset.

papers.title: Deterministic Root-Finding over Finite Fields with Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract:
Finding the roots of a polynomial over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ in deterministic polynomial time is a long-standing open problem. Classical deterministic methods work in the multiplicative group $\mathbb F_q^\times$ and are efficient only when $q-1$ is smooth, which is rarely the case.
  We propose a method that replaces $\mathbb F_q^\times$ by the groups of rational points of an elliptic curve $E$ and of its quadratic twist $\widetilde E$. The computation splits into an offline phase, which depends only on $\mathbb F_q$ and outputs a short \emph{elliptic preprocessing datum} $\mathcal D$, and an online phase, which processes the input polynomial. Writing $\Xi(\mathcal D)$ for the largest prime factor of $\lvert E(\mathbb F_q)\rvert\cdot\lvert\widetilde E(\mathbb F_q)\rvert$, the online phase is deterministic and finds the roots of any $f\in\mathbb F_q[X]$ of degree $n$ within $\widetilde O(\Xi(\mathcal D)^2\,n\log^2 q+n^\omega\log q+n\log^3 q)$ operations in $\mathbb F_q$. A precursor of our method is an algorithm by R\'onyai, which recovers the roots through Galois computations over number fields, relies on GRH, and comes with a polynomial bound of unspecified degree; in contrast, our online phase works entirely over $\mathbb F_q$ and is unconditional. Moreover, $\mathcal D$ can be certified deterministically and unconditionally in time polynomial in $\log q$ and $\Xi(\mathcal D)$.
  We conjecture that every $\mathbb F_q$ of large enough characteristic admits a datum with $\Xi(\mathcal D)\leq(\log q)^{O(1)}$, and support this with a heuristic and with experiments. Constructing such a datum in polynomial time remains open.

papers.title: Commuting Families of Flag Quasideterminants in Reflection Equation Algebras of Type A
papers.abstract: We consider a family of northeastern antidiagonal quasideterminants associated with the successive blocks of the generating matrix of a reflection equation (RE) algebra of type $A_{n-1}$. Our main result proves the conjecture on their pairwise commutativity formulated earlier. The proof uses the triangular realization of the RE algebra in a quantum enveloping algebra and the flag property of quasideterminants. We also discuss the interpretation of these elements in terms of quantum cluster coordinates and their possible connection with generalized Toda systems.

papers.title: Stochastic predator-prey compartment model with cyclic and non-cyclic transition pathways and mortality
papers.authors: Thomas M. Michelitsch, Ayten D. Baher, Michael Bestehorn, Andrzej F. Nowakowski, Alejandro P. Riascos, Bernard A. Collet
papers.abstract: We study variants of a stochastic SEIRS-SEID compartmental model incorporating presymptomatic infectiousness and disease-related mortality, with independent compartmental sojourn times drawn from arbitrary distributions, in particular Weibull distributions. We consider a large population of agents that occupy the states (compartments) S (susceptible to infection), E (exposed: infected but asymptomatic during the latency period and already infectious, including diseases with presymptomatic infections), I (infected and infectious, with symptoms), R (recovered, immune, and non-infectious), or D (dead). We consider (i) cyclic transmission pathways, where compartmental sojourn times are finite and immunity is temporary, and (ii) non-cyclic pathways, where immunity is permanent. In the absence of mortality, cyclic transmission pathways support an endemic equilibrium above the spreading threshold which is either globally stable or oscillatory (Hopf) unstable, whereas for non-cyclic pathways a stationary disease-free state is emerging. From a stochastic perspective, we elucidate the connection between compartmental sojourn-time distributions and the appearance of fractional operators in the evolution equations: fat-tailed compartment waiting-time distributions necessarily lead to fractional derivatives. For cyclic transition pathways we obtain an explicit expression for the expected number of infection cycles that an agent survives. Our model is validated by a combined Monte Carlo -- Runge -- Kutta simulation scheme and random-walk simulations on Barabasi-Albert networks. It has cross-disciplinary applications beyond epidemiology, including wildfire spreading, certain classes of chemical reactions, population dynamics, finance, economics, and biology.

papers.title: Exact Global Minimax Risk near Nonidentification
papers.abstract: We study squared-error estimation when a nuisance parameter is unidentified on a submodel but affects a target that vanishes there. For models with higher-order profile expansions, we give sufficient conditions under which the largest critical-path minimax risk is the exact asymptotic minimax risk over the full parameter space. An efficient observable feature, negligible calibration error and stable recovery yield one estimator attaining the leading constant uniformly, with the profile coordinates unknown. The estimator uses calibration estimates, a local feature mean and an empirical recovery feature. The constant is expressed through a bounded-normal decision problem. We verify the conditions in two models. In centered Gaussian logistic errors-in-variables regression with one surrogate and two unknown variances, we determine the fifth-order global coefficient risk and its exact constant. A sparse extension separates variance-decomposition uncertainty from direction estimation and specifies when the scalar constant is preserved. In a degree-balanced replicated-network model, we determine the sixth-order global edge-contrast risk when block proportions are unknown. Triangles identify a parameter combination; a bowtie supplies the additional information needed for the contrast.

papers.title: Contextual Decision Making: Predictive or Generative
papers.authors: L. Jeff Hong, Weihuan Huang, Xinyao Li
papers.abstract: Contextual decision making uses observed covariates to guide decisions under uncertainty. Two natural approaches are predict-then-optimize (PtO), which learns the conditional expected objective, and generate-then-optimize (GtO), which learns conditional uncertainty and optimizes using generated scenarios. We study when each approach is preferable by examining how the choice of learning target affects statistical accuracy and optimization tractability. Although PtO learns a narrower target, our regret bounds show how differences in smoothness can offset GtO's additional dimensional burden. Exploiting smoothness also raises an optimization tradeoff: within the class of nonnegative-weight PtO methods studied, a lower bound limits the gains from additional smoothness, while more flexible methods may introduce signed weights and lose the guarantee of preserving convexity. GtO preserves scenario-wise convexity, but requires learning a richer object and generating scenarios for optimization. Synthetic experiments and a real case study illustrate how these tradeoffs vary with data availability and problem structure. Together with the scope for reusing a model across tasks, our findings provide practical guidance for choosing between the approaches without identifying a universal winner.

papers.title: An Invitation to Algebraic Methods in Quantum Theory
papers.authors: Peter T. J. Bradshaw, Jonte R. Hance
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present various well-studied examples of quantum systems, and discuss how they might be analysed algebraically. We analyse the harmonic oscillator, hydrogenic atom, optical components, and particle spin using multiple algebraic methods, and highlight the central importance of algebraic relationships between operators in determining the physical character of the system. In particular, we show: the ubiquity of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)\cong\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ as the ``spectrum generating algebra''; the role of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ in determining the action of optical components; that an elementary algebraic approach to particle spin offers novel insights into its nature versus the usual approaches; and how understanding the full (often hidden) symmetry of a problem enables it to be solved immediately without the need to solve differential equations. We hope this work will serve as a gentle introduction to algebraic methods in quantum mechanics for the interested reader --- we therefore signpost active areas of research within the community.

papers.title: Sensitivity-Guided Parameter Estimation of Bubbly Liquid via a Nonlinear Wave Equation and Physics-InformedNeuralNetworks
papers.authors: Takeru Hasegawa, Naoto Mitsume, Shota Deguchi, Mitsuteru Asai, Tetsuya Kanagawa
papers.abstract: Interactions between ultrasound and microbubbles underlie a range of biomedical and industrial applications, yet predicting how the physical parameters of the medium and bubbles govern nonlinear wave propagation remains difficult. This study proposes a parameter estimation framework that combines a Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers (KdVB) equation, describing weakly nonlinear wave propagation in a bubbly liquid, with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The contributions are threefold. First, the PINN reproduces the reference solution of the governing equation in the forward problem, with a near-zero prediction error at the initial time that confirms the initial condition is enforced exactly as intended. Second, prior to inverse estimation, a sensitivity analysis is introduced that quantifies, at both the coefficient and solution levels, how each of eight physical parameters influences the KdVB equation, allowing the expected difficulty of estimating each parameter to be assessed in advance. Third, based on this assessment, single-parameter inverse estimation is performed for seven of the eight parameters using the PINN. Liquid viscosity, bubble initial radius, liquid density, sound speed, and liquid pressure are estimated with errors of 0.8-2.1%, the polytropic exponent converges only partially, and the surface tension coefficient cannot be estimated at all, consistent with the sensitivity analysis. These results establish a general framework for identifying and estimating the physical parameters governing nonlinear wave propagation in bubbly liquids from observed waveform data.

papers.title: A Linear Lower Bound for Convex Body Chasing in Every $\ell_p$ Norm
papers.abstract: We establish an $\Omega(d)$ lower bound on the competitive ratio of convex body chasing in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\ell_p$ movement costs for any $p \in [1, \infty)$. Previously, the best known lower bound for general $p$ was $\Omega(\max\{\sqrt{d}, d^{1-1/p}\})$, established by Bubeck et al. (2019); a linear lower bound was known only for $p = \infty$, realized by the standard construction of chasing faces of a hypercube. Our lower bound strictly improves on the prior bound for every fixed $p \in [1, \infty)$ and shows that the functional Steiner point algorithm of Sellke (2023) - which has competitive ratio $O(d)$ - is asymptotically optimal for every $\ell_p$ norm. Our lower bound is based on the recursive construction of Bubeck, Coester, and Rabani (2023) for metrical service systems, which gives a lower bound of $\Omega(r^2)$ for requests of size $O(r)$ in that setting. We show that requests in their construction, each comprising a set of discrete points in a graph metric, can be mapped to the vertices of convex requests in a $(2r+1)$-dimensional vector space while approximately preserving movement costs up to a factor of $O(r)$, which establishes the lower bound.

papers.title: Score-Preserving Continual Lasso under Task Shift
papers.authors: Jingyi Guo, Runze Li, Lingzhou Xue
papers.abstract: Continual learning (CL) aims to learn from sequential tasks while mitigating catastrophic forgetting when historical data are no longer accessible. We study continual learning for high-dimensional sparse linear regression, where $\ell_1$ regularization creates a difficulty absent from continual ridge regression: that recursively reusing an $\ell_1$-penalized estimator can propagate earlier shrinkage and accumulate regularization bias across tasks. We propose score-preserving continual Lasso (SP-CL), which separates sparse estimation from state transmission by preserving the historical squared-loss score. Under squared loss, its cumulative estimator exactly recovers a full-history Lasso minimizer. When task coefficients coincide, it inherits the full-history sparse rate. For related task-specific coefficients, SP-CL uses a regularized current-task correction that leaves the transmitted state unchanged and attains the offline source-assisted rate under an oracle related-task condition. We also derive Overall/BWT/FWT decompositions that distinguish historical information loss, task conflict, and current-task specialization, and validate the resulting regimes in simulation.

papers.title: Discrete WKB approach to density profiles in inhomogeneous two-band free-fermion chains
papers.authors: Federico Finkel, Artemio Gonz\'alez-L\'opez, Mart\'in Zapata
papers.abstract: We extend the discrete WKB method to one-dimensional bipartite tight-binding chains of free fermions with slowly varying hopping amplitudes and on-site potentials. We focus on the inhomogeneous Rice-Mele model, suggesting possible experimental realizations thereof in optical superlattices. We derive explicit semiclassical expressions for the single-particle wave functions and density of states, as well as the sublattice-resolved local particle densities and filling fraction at arbitrary Fermi energy. In particular, we show that the WKB density profiles agree with those obtained from the local-density approximation. We analyze the spatial dependence of the local band edges and its consequences for the global spectral structure, and clarify the role played by the phase-space topology in determining the Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization conditions. Finally, we illustrate our results with two representative examples: a homogeneous Rice-Mele chain subject to a harmonic trap and a fully inhomogeneous chain containing a domain wall.

papers.title: Structure and Exact Certification of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions
papers.abstract: We study the structure and exact certification of nonnegative tensor decompositions supplied through rational factor matrices. Every failure of minimality or essential uniqueness contains an irreducible positive exchange between $p$ supplied terms and $q$ competing terms. A dimension count based on the Lovitz--Petrov splitting theorem bounds the effective order of such an exchange, the sum over the modes of the joint factor-span dimension minus one, by $p+q-2$, and this bound is attained at every supplied length $R\ge2$. After eliminating ambient-row variables by the Farkas lemma, the resulting semialgebraic systems have fewer than $2R^2$ real variables. For input bit length $L$, this gives a deterministic $G(R)L^{O(R^2)}$-time algorithm that computes the nonnegative rank and an exact minimum-length decomposition, decides minimality and essential uniqueness, and returns exact witnesses when either property fails. The exponent is independent of the tensor order and the mode dimensions. For Lebesgue moment tensors, positive quadrature determines the nonnegative rank and the uniqueness behavior, and some rational length-$R$ inputs force a common field of degree at least $\lfloor R/2\rfloor!$ for any exact minimum-length output. As an illustration, an implementation resolves all 114 instances left inconclusive by earlier positive-scattering criteria, of which 95 are minimal and essentially unique and 19 are minimal but nonunique.

papers.title: Multiplicative vs. Additive State Coupling in Learned Optimizer Schedules
papers.authors: M. Harper Langston, Pierre-David Letourneau, Dalton Jones, Roland Memisevic, Peter Scott, Mingu Lee, Richard A. Lethin, Christopher Lott, Fatih Porikli, Harris Teague
papers.abstract: We learn schedules for a continuous penalty relaxation of MAX-CUT by backpropagating through an unrolled classical solver. A state-blind schedule generalizes to instances substantially larger than those used for training. A state-adaptive bilinear schedule also generalizes out of distribution, outperforming its untrained baseline across 15 seeds ($t=4.1$). By contrast, an additive ablation with identical inputs and output heads is statistically indistinguishable from the bilinear model in distribution but performs worse than its own baseline out of distribution ($t=-11.7$). This separation appears without regularization and persists across a $30$ round weight-decay sweep: the bilinear advantage remains significant at every tested value, whereas the additive model never recovers. The results in this setting isolate how solver state enters the schedule, rather than state adaptivity alone, as the architectural distinction associated with out-of-distribution transfer.

papers.title: Non-singlets and the phase diagram of Matrix Quantum Mechanics
papers.authors: Igor R. Klebanov, Henry W. Lin, Pavel Meshcheriakov, Jessica Yeh
papers.abstract: The quantum mechanics of one $N\times N$ Hermitian matrix in the infinite $N$ limit is well known to define a two-dimensional string theory when the quartic coupling constant $g$ is tuned to a special negative value $g_*$. We study the thermodynamics of this Matrix Quantum Mechanics (MQM), treating the SU$(N)$ symmetry as a global symmetry. Crucially, the non-singlets, i.e. states in non-trivial representations of SU$(N)$, implement the effects of vortices on the discretized worldsheets. This random lattice model has the low-temperature $c=1$ and high-temperature $c=0$ phases, with the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition separating them. We map out the phase diagram in the coupling--temperature plane, which is separated by the critical stability curve $T_c(g)$ extending from $g_*< g <0$. We study this curve using the non-perturbative matrix bootstrap and low- and high-temperature perturbation theory, which explain the thermal instability. At low temperatures, thermally excited non-singlets backreact on the Fermi sea of matrix eigenvalues, causing it to spill over. At high temperatures, the theory is described by an effective matrix integral obtained by dimensional reduction on the thermal circle; the eigenvalue distribution of the zero mode becomes unstable at the critical coupling. We conjecture that the BKT transition occurs at a special point on the critical curve and estimate its position. Finally, we switch to the regular square lattice and study the MQM-inspired Villain model, where the link factor is the one-dimensional propagator on a circle. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we map out the BKT transition in this model.

papers.title: Acyclic 2-edge-coloured graphs: polynomial-time linkages and colouring hardness
papers.authors: J{\o}rgen Bang-Jensen, St\'ephane Bessy, Amadeus Reinald
papers.abstract:
A path or cycle in a $2$-edge-coloured graph is alternating if consecutive edges have different colours. These objects are natural analogues of paths and cycles in graphs, and even more so in digraphs. A well-studied class is that of acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs, that is, those forbidding alternating cycles. In particular, (acyclic) $2$-edge-coloured graphs generalize directed (acyclic) graphs (DAGs), but the complexity of problems on DAGs is much better understood than that of the corresponding problems on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs. We investigate the complexity of two such problems, whose directed counterparts are well-known.
  Our first result is an $n^{O(k)}$-time algorithm for the alternating $k$-linkage problem on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs. This problem asks for $k$ vertex-disjoint alternating paths joining $k$ prescribed pairs of vertices. This generalizes the directed $k$-linkage algorithm for DAGs. For every fixed $k$, this also yields a polynomial-time algorithm for finding $k$ internally vertex-disjoint alternating $(s,t)$-paths, solving an open problem by Abouelaoualim et al. from 2008.
  We then consider the alternating chromatic number of $2$-edge-coloured graphs, defined as the minimum number of parts in a vertex partition such that each part induces an acyclic subgraph. This notion is analogous to the dichromatic number of digraphs, where it is known that deciding dichromatic number $2$ is NP-complete even on tournaments. Our second result is that deciding alternating chromatic number $2$ is NP-complete on complete $2$-edge-coloured graphs. Equivalently, deciding whether a graph can be partitioned into two induced threshold graphs is NP-complete.

papers.title: On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing
papers.abstract: Stratification can reduce the estimator variance in Monte Carlo simulations by partitioning the sample space according to a low-dimensional factor and sampling separately within the resulting strata, making it well suited to the valuation of path-dependent claims in high-dimensional financial models. Its performance, however, depends critically on the choice of the stratification factor, and effective low-dimensional factors are generally difficult to identify in complex continuous-time models. Neural networks provide a flexible approximation class for this purpose and have proved useful in related variance-reduction problems in quantitative finance. In this paper, we study the construction of neural stratification factors for derivative pricing under proportional allocation in continuous-time models. Since the numerical construction of a stratification factor typically involves approximation, we establish continuity results for the associated conditional expectations and, more generally, conditional distributions, and provide several counterexamples showing the limits of this continuity theory. Combined with density results for neural networks, our findings yield a universal approximation theorem for admissible stratification factors. We conclude with numerical experiments involving a constant-maturity-swap range accrual in a two-factor Gaussian short-rate model and a worst-of autocallable in a Wishart stochastic covariance model, where the learned factors outperform all considered benchmarks.

papers.title: A dynamical approach towards Collatz conjecture
papers.abstract:
The present work focuses on the study of the renowned Collatz conjecture, also known as the $3x+1$ problem. The analysis rests on the dynamics of an iterative map in binary form, defined on the dyadic rationals of $[1/2,\,1)$. We estimate how the length of the binary expansion of the iterated numbers changes, and we regard the iterative map as a perturbation of a circle map without periodic points, with an explicit bound for the error between both maps. A condition on the periods of periodic orbits is given; it is the classical argument of Crandall, and it recovers the lower bound of Eliahou for the length of nontrivial cycles.
  This version corrects several errors of the first one; they are listed in the Addendum.

papers.title: An Optimal Projection Framework for Structure-Preserving Model Reduction of Linear Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a model order reduction framework for linear systems where the $\mathcal{H}_2$ optimization is combined with the Petrov-Galerkin projection to preserve a wide range of system properties, including stability, bounded realness, sector boundedness, and dissipativity. The model reduction problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem on a generalized Stiefel manifold, aiming to minimize the $\mathcal{H}_2$ norm of the pproximation error between the full-order and reduced-order models. An explicit expression for the Euclidean gradient of the objective function is derived, and a Riemannian gradient procedure with an efficient generalized Cayley update is applied to seek a (locally) optimal projection, followed by a theoretical analysis of the algorithm. Finally, the performance of the proposed method is demonstrated by a numerical example.

papers.title: Positivity for toric Kac polynomials in higher depth
papers.abstract: We prove that the polynomials counting locally free, absolutely indecomposable, rank 1 representations of quivers over rings of truncated power series have non-negative coefficients. This generalizes the positivity of toric Kac polynomials to higher depth. The proof goes by inductively contracting/deleting arrows of the quiver and is inspired by a previous work of Abdelgadir, Mellit and Rodriguez-Villegas on toric Kac polynomials. We also relate counts of absolutely indecomposable quiver representations in higher depth and counts of jets over fibres of quiver moment maps. This is expressed as a plethystic identity involving generating series of these counts. In rank 1, we prove a cohomological upgrade of this identity, by computing the compactly supported cohomology of jet spaces over preprojective stacks. This is reminiscent of PBW isomorphisms for preprojective cohomological Hall algebras. Finally, our plethystic identity allows us to prove two conjectures by Wyss on the asymptotic behavior of both counts, when depth goes to infinity.

papers.title: Box Order and Dominance Order on Standard Young Tableaux
papers.abstract: We generalize results of [1] concerning two partial orders on Standard Young Tableaux: the dominance order and the box order. Extending their definitions from tableaux of a fixed shape to the set Tr of all Standard Young Tableaux of a fixed size r, we prove that these orders coincide in this more general setting. We also investigate basic properties of these orders. We further show that this result extends to Littlewood-Richardson tableaux whose skew shapes are rook strips. We briefly mention applications to invariant subspaces of nilpotent linear operators.

papers.title: Envelopes of Horospheres and Weingarten Surfaces in Hyperbolic 3-Space
papers.abstract:
We derive basic differential geometric formulae for surfaces in hyperbolic space represented as envelopes of horospheres. The dual notion of parallel hypersurfaces is also studied. The representation is applied to prove existence and regularity theorems for Weingarten surfaces in H^3, which satisfy (1-a)K = a(2-H), for an a < 0, and have a specified boundary curve at infinity. These surfaces are shown to be closely connected to conformal mappings of domains in S^2 into the unit disk and provide Riemannian interpretations for some conformal invariants associated to such mappings.
  This paper was originally written in 1984, before I learned to use TeX, and was typed by one of the secretaries in the Princeton Math Department. It was more or less, my first original work after my dissertation. For some reason, I was not able to get this paper published in a timely manner. The results and perspective in this paper have proved to be useful to a variety of people, some of whom asked me to render the article into TeX and post it to the arXiv. I had been seriously thinking about doing this, when Martin Bridgeman sent me a transcription of my original article into TeX. I am extremely grateful to him for the effort he has put into this project.
  The paper is now formatted in a more or less modern AMS-article style, but for lots of additional punctuation, a few corrections and some minor stylistic changes, the content has been largely reproduced as it originally was. Remarks about the 'state-of-the-art' in hyperbolic geometry are obviously way out of date, as there has been enormous progress in many aspects of this still rich subject.

papers.title: Source reconstruction algorithms for coupled parabolic systems from internal measurements of one scalar state
papers.authors: Cristhian Montoya, Ignacio Brevis, David Bolivar
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of source reconstruction algorithms for coupled systems of heat equations, with either constant or spatially dependent coupling terms, where internal measurements are available from a reduced number of observed states. Two classes of systems are considered. The first comprises parabolic equations with constant zero-order coupling terms (through a matrix potential term or via the diffusion matrix). The second type considers parabolic equations coupled by a matrix potential that depends on spatial variables, which leads to the analysis of a non-self-adjoint operator. In all configurations, the source is assumed to be of separate variables, the temporal part is a known scalar function, and the spatial dependence is an unknown vector field. Several numerical examples using the finite element method in 1D and 2D are presented to show the reconstruction of space-dependent sources.

papers.title: Simple Tilings of Riemannian Homogeneous Spaces
papers.abstract: We define simple tilings in the general context of a $G$-tiling on a Riemannian homogeneous space $M$ to be tilings by Riemannian simplices. As evidence that this definition is natural, we prove that a large class of tilings of $M$ are MLD to simple ones. We further show that there is an isomorphism between \u{C}ech cohomology and pattern-equivariant cohomology of simple tilings of homogeneous Riemannian Spaces. This demonstrates the utility of our definition by generalizing an established result on the topology of tiling spaces of Euclidean space.

papers.title: Atiyah duality for motivic spectra
papers.authors: Toni Annala, Marc Hoyois, Ryomei Iwasa
papers.abstract: We prove that Atiyah duality holds in the $\infty$-category of non-$\mathbb A^1$-invariant motivic spectra over arbitrary derived schemes: every smooth projective scheme is dualizable with dual given by the Thom spectrum of its negative tangent bundle. The Gysin maps recently constructed by L. Tang are a key ingredient in the proof. We then present several applications. First, we study $\mathbb A^1$-colocalization, which transforms any module over the $\mathbb A^1$-invariant sphere into an $\mathbb A^1$-invariant motivic spectrum without changing its values on smooth projective schemes. This can be applied to all known $p$-adic cohomology theories and gives a new elementary approach to "logarithmic" or "tame" cohomology theories; it recovers for instance the logarithmic crystalline cohomology of strict normal crossings compactifications over perfect fields and shows that the latter is independent of the choice of compactification. Second, we prove a motivic Landweber exact functor theorem, associating a motivic spectrum to any graded formal group law classified by a flat map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Using this theorem, we compute the ring of $\mathbb P^1$-stable cohomology operations on the algebraic K-theory of qcqs derived schemes, and we prove that rational motivic cohomology is an idempotent motivic spectrum.

papers.title: Metaplectic cusp forms and the large sieve
papers.abstract:
We prove a power saving upper bound for the sum of Fourier coefficients $\rho_f(\cdot)$ of a fixed cubic metaplectic cusp form $f$ over primes. Our result is the cubic analogue of a celebrated 1990 Theorem of Duke and Iwaniec, and the cuspidal analogue of a Theorem due to the author and Radziwill for the bias in cubic Gauss sums.
  The proof has two main inputs, both of independent interest. Firstly, we prove a new large sieve estimate for a bilinear form whose kernel function is $\rho_f(\cdot)$. The proof of the bilinear estimate uses a number field version of circle method due to Browning and Vishe, Voronoi summation, and Gauss-Ramanujan sums. Secondly, we use Voronoi summation and the cubic large sieve of Heath-Brown to prove an estimate for a linear form involving $\rho_f(\cdot)$. Our linear estimate overcomes a bottleneck occurring at level of distribution $2/3$.

papers.title: A direct proof of the existence of MME for finite horizon Sinai billiards
papers.abstract: The Sinai billiard map $T$ on the two-torus, i.e., the periodic Lorentz gas, is a discontinuous map. We provide two separate conditions for a finite horizon billiard to admit equilibrium states. The first one -- namely \emph{negligible singularities} -- only concerns the billiard table and implies upper semi-continuity for the metric pressure map of $T$. The condition of negligible singularities is shown to be generic (dense $G_\delta$) among billiard tables with $C^{3+\alpha}$ boundaries, in the $C^{3+\alpha}$ topology, and implies the sparse recurrence condition for the null potential. Compactness of the set of $T$-invariant measures is proved. For finite horizon Sinai billiards, we provide a bound on the defect of upper semi-continuity of the metric pressure map. From it, a condition of existence of equilibrium states only involving potentials is deduced. In both situations, for the potentials $g \equiv 0$ and $g = -h_{\rm top}(\Phi^1) \tau$, we recover and extend the recent results of the existence of measures of maximal entropy (MME) for both the map $T$ and the flow $\Phi^t$, due to Baladi and Demers for $T$, jointly with Carrand for $\Phi^t$. Upper semi-continuity of the metric entropy is shown. Assuming negligible singularities, equidistribution of the periodic orbits with respect to the unique MME is proved. A bound on the topological tail entropy is given.

papers.title: Variational principles and aplications to symmetric PDEs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we explore various equivalences of Ekeland's variational principle within the framework of group-invariant mappings. We introduce and analyze several key theorems, including the Drop theorem, the Petal theorem, Caristi-Kirk fxed-point theorem, and Takahashi's theorem, all of them within this context. Moreover, we extend the classical Drop theorem and Petal theorem to a more generalized setting. We also demonstrate the practical signifcance of these findings through numerous applications to diverse areas of mathematics. In particular, in the context of partial differential equations, we explore their implications on the solution of the Plateau problem, and in control theory. We also extend the classical Pontyargin maximum principle.

papers.title: Puzzle Game: Prediction and Classification of Wordle Solution Words
papers.authors: Haidong Xin, Fang Wu, Zhitong Zhou
papers.abstract: Wordle result prediction involves both daily participation and the difficulty of the solution word. We model these quantities with ARIMA forecasts of report counts, XGBoost regressors using word frequency, letter entropy, and repetition, and a decision tree trained on K-means difficulty tiers. Experiments use 355 daily outcome distributions, with a 107-word chronological holdout and four expanding-window tests. XGBoost reduces holdout mean absolute error from 4.08 to 3.84 percentage points and improves over the training mean in every temporal window. Ridge and random forests remain competitive. XGBoost systematically underestimates failure rates on difficult words. The lexical decision tree achieves 54.2% tier accuracy, compared with 40.2% when predicted histograms are assigned to the same training centroids. Bootstrap analysis shows that cluster stability does not imply that tiers are predictable from lexical attributes. For report counts, comparisons at matched horizons reveal substantial overdispersion in full-history ARIMA intervals. These results characterize the predictive value and limitations of a compact lexical model of reported Wordle performance.

papers.title: The evolution of random subgraphs of the permutahedron
papers.authors: Maur\'icio Collares, Joseph Doolittle, Joshua Erde
papers.abstract:
In their seminal paper introducing the theory of random graphs, Erd\H{o}s and R\'{e}nyi considered the evolution of the structure of a random subgraph of $K_n$ as the density increases from $0$ to $1$, identifying two key points in this evolution -- the percolation threshold, where the order of the largest component seemingly jumps from logarithmic to linear in size, and the connectivity threshold, where the subgraph becomes connected. Similar phenomena have been observed in many other random graph models, and in particular, works of Ajtai, Koml\'{o}s and Szemer\'{e}di and of Erd\H{o}s and Spencer determine corresponding thresholds for random subgraphs of the hypercube.
  The permutahedron, like the hypercube, has many equivalent representations, and arises as a natural object of study in many areas of combinatorics. In particular, as a highly-symmetric simple polytope, like the $n$-simplex and $n$-cube, percolation on the permutahedron arises naturally as an analogue to the Erd\H{o}s-R\'{e}nyi random graph and the percolated hypercube.
  We determine the percolation threshold and the connectivity threshold for random subgraphs of the permutahedron. Along the way we develop a novel graph exploration technique which can be used to find exponentially large clusters after percolation in high-dimensional geometric graphs, and we initiate the study of the isoperimetric properties of the permutahedron.

papers.title: Minimal finite models of wedges of spheres with at most eight points
papers.abstract: A minimal finite model of a topological space is a finite $T_0$-space of least cardinality that is weak homotopy equivalent to it. We determine, up to homeomorphism, the minimal finite models of eight wedges of one- and two-dimensional spheres. The spaces $S^{2}\vee S^{1}$ and $S^{2}\vee S^{2}$ have exactly two and three minimal finite models, respectively, all with seven points, whereas $S^{1}\vee S^{1}\vee S^{2}$ has exactly seven minimal finite models, $S^{1}\vee S^{1}\vee S^{1}\vee S^{2}$ has one, $S^{1}\vee S^{2}\vee S^{2}$ has six, $S^{2}\vee S^{2}\vee S^{2}$ has five, $S^{2}\vee S^{2}\vee S^{2}\vee S^{2}$ has three, and $S^{1}\vee S^{1}\vee S^{2}\vee S^{2}$ has two, all with eight points. To prove this we classify the connected finite $T_0$-spaces of height $2$ without beat points that have seven or eight points, and we identify their weak homotopy types by means of McCord's theorem and explicit collapse and suspension arguments for their two-dimensional order complexes. Together with the known results for spheres and wedges of circles, this determines, up to weak homotopy equivalence, all path-connected spaces whose minimal finite models have at most eight points.

papers.title: Series expansions by generalized Bessel functions for functions related to the lattice point problems for the $p$-circle
papers.abstract: The lattice point problems of the $p$-circle (for example, the astroid), which a generalized circle for positive real numbers $p$, have been solved for approximately $p$ more than 3, based on the series representation of the error term using the generalized Bessel functions by E. Kr\"{a}tzel and the results of G. Kuba. On the other hand, for the cases $0<p<2$, the method via this series representation cannot make progress. Therefore, in such cases, it is necessary to consider another method. In this paper, we prove that certain functions closely related to the problems can be displayed as series by newly generalized Bessel functions based on the property $p$-radial, generalization of spherical symmetry, and highlight the possibility that attempts to solve the problems via this display are suitable especially for the cases $0<p\leq1$. This study is based on the harmonic-analytic method by S. Kuratsubo and E. Nakai, using certain functions generalizing the error term of the circle problem by variables and series representation of the functions by the Bessel functions.

papers.title: Monotonicity properties of Hadamard weighted geometric means of bounded sets of positive kernel operators
papers.abstract: We prove new monotonicity properties for joint and generalized spectral radius and their essential versions, operator norm, Hausdorff measure of non-compactness and numerical radius of products and sums of Hadamard weighted geometric means of positive kernel operators on appropriate Banach function spaces. Our results extend recent results on weighted geometric symmetrizations of bounded sets of such operators defined on $L^2$. To our knowledge, several proved properties in this generality are new even in the finite dimensional case and also in the case of singelton sets.

papers.title: A multi-objective mixed integer linear programming model for supply chain planning of 3D printing
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) printing makes customized parts in small batches, but 3D printers are expensive and slow, so the grouping, orientation, and sequencing of parts decide both delivery times and printer use. We study the allocation of parts with due dates to jobs on identical powder bed 3D printers, where the orientation of a part sets its height and the plate area it occupies. We formulate a bi-objective mixed integer linear programming model that minimizes the weighted earliness and tardiness of the parts and the unused plate area of the jobs, and we show that the optimal timing of a fixed job sequence is an isotonic regression. The Pareto front is computed with the epsilon-constraint method, and a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm built on this timing result handles larger instances. On random instances, choosing the orientation lowers the earliness and tardiness by 63\% on average compared with the orientation given in the data. For 15 to 40 parts, the genetic algorithm keeps 98\% to 99\% of the hypervolume of the best known fronts in less than a minute per run on average, whereas a time-limited epsilon-constraint method keeps about half of it with 30 and 40 parts.

papers.title: Chromatic Ramsey numbers and two-color Tur\'an densities
papers.authors: Maria Axenovich, Simon Gaa, Dingyuan Liu
papers.abstract: Given a graph $G$, its $2$-color Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}^{(2)}(n,G)$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph, such that the edges can be colored with two colors avoiding a monochromatic copy of $G$. Let $\pi^{(2)}(G)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{ex}^{(2)}(n,G)/\binom{n}{2}$ be the $2$-color Tur\'{a}n density of $G$. What real numbers in the interval $(0,1)$ are realized as the $2$-color Tur\'{a}n density of some graph? It is known that $\pi^{(2)}(G)=1-(R_{\chi}(G)-1)^{-1}$, where $R_{\chi}(G)$ is the chromatic Ramsey number of $G$. Burr, Erd\H{o}s, and Lov\'{a}sz showed that $(k-1)^2+1\leq{R_{\chi}(G)}\leq{R(k)}$, for any $k$-chromatic graph $G$, where $R(k)$ is the classical Ramsey number. However, it is an open problem to determine how many distinct values between $(k-1)^{2}+1$ and $R(k)$ can be realized as $R_{\chi}(G)$ of some $k$-chromatic graph $G$ for general $k$. In this paper, among others, we prove that there are $\Omega(k)$ different values of $R_{\chi}(G)$ among $k$-chromatic graphs $G$. This sheds more light onto the possible $2$-color Tur\'{a}n densities of graphs.

papers.title: A note on quasi-elementary sub-Hopf algebras of the polynomial part of the odd primary Steenrod algebra
papers.abstract: We prove that every quasi-elementary sub-Hopf algebra of the polynomial part of the odd primary Steenrod algebra must lie in a certain sub-Hopf algebra called $D$.

papers.title: Distinction of the Steinberg representation with respect to a symmetric pair
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a non-archimedean local field of residual characteristic $p\neq 2$. Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over $K$, let $\theta$ be an involution of $G$ over $K$, and let $H$ be the connected component of $\theta$-fixed subgroup of $G$ over $K$. By realizing the Steinberg representation of $G$ as the $G$-space of complex smooth harmonic cochains following the idea of Broussous--Court\`es, we study its space of distinction by $H$ as a finite dimensional complex vector space. We give an upper bound of the dimension, and under certain conditions, we show that the upper bound is sharp by explicitly constructing a basis using the technique of Poincar\'e series. Finally, we apply our general theory to the case where $G$ is a general linear group and $H$ a special orthogonal subgroup, which leads to a complete classification result.

papers.title: K\"unneth and extension theorems for Morita invariants of non-commutative schemes
papers.abstract: In this article, we apply the derived Morita theory of dg-categories to show how to extend the domain of validity of many identities relating Morita invariants from associative dg-algebras toward non-commutative scheme. Doing so, we obtain that the dg-category of associative algebras can be used to test the exactness of any sequence and the commutativity of any diagram involving Morita invariants depending multilinearly on their arguments, under a mild condition of stability by cofibrant replacement. This gives a simple picture of how the underlying algebra of a non-commutative scheme captures its Morita invariant properties. As an application, we use a K\"unneth formula on non-commutative schemes to factorise the Hochschild cohomology of a product of quasi-phantom categories such as built by Orlov and Gorshinsky in [GO13]. This is an occasion to explore how the derived Morita theory interacts with the \v{C}ech dg-enhancement of a projective scheme and to shed an unifying light upon the landscape of dg-modules over dg-categories.

papers.title: Subset selection problems in planar point sets
papers.authors: J\'ozsef Balogh, Felix Christian Clemen, Adrian Dumitrescu, Dingyuan Liu
papers.abstract:
Given a finite point set satisfying condition $\mathcal{A}$, the subset selection problem asks, how large of a subset satisfying condition $\mathcal{B}$ can be extracted? In this paper, we make progress on three instances of subset selection problems in planar point sets. Let $n,s\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\geq s$, and let $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points, where at most $s$ points lie on the same line.
  Firstly, we select a general position subset of $P$. This problem was proposed by Erd\H{o}s under the regime when $s$ is a constant. For $s$ being non-constant, we give new lower and upper bounds on the maximum size of such a subset. In particular, we show that in the worst case such a set can have size at most $O(n^{5/6+o(1)}/\sqrt{s})$ when $3\leq s\leq n^{1/3}$ and $O(n/s)$ when $n^{1/3}\leq s\leq n$.
  Secondly, we select a monotone general position subset of $P$, that is, a subset in general position where the points are ordered from left to right and their $y$-coordinates are either non-decreasing or non-increasing. We present bounds on the maximum size of such a subset. In particular, when $s=\Omega(\sqrt{n})$, our upper and lower bounds differ at most by a logarithmic factor.
  Lastly, we select a subset of $P$ with pairwise distinct slopes. This problem was initially studied by Erd\H{o}s, Graham, Ruzsa, and Taylor on the grid. We show that for $s=O(\sqrt{n})$ such a subset of size $\Omega((n/\log{s})^{1/3})$ can always be found in $P$. When $s=\Theta(\sqrt{n})$, this matches a lower bound given by Zhang on the grid. As for the upper bound, we show that in the worst case such a subset has size at most $O(\sqrt{n})$ for $2\leq s\leq n^{3/8}$ and $O((n/s)^{4/5})$ for $n^{3/8}\leq s=O(\sqrt{n})$.
  The proofs use a wide range of tools such as incidence geometry, probabilistic methods, the hypergraph container method, and additive combinatorics.

papers.title: Long Time Behavior and Stabilization for Displacement Monotone Mean Field Games
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of the long time behavior of Nash equilibria in Mean Field Games within the framework of displacement monotonicity. We first show that any two equilibria defined on the time horizon $[0,T]$ must be close as $T \to \infty$, in a suitable sense, independently of initial/terminal conditions. The way this stability property is made quantitative involves the $L^2$ distance between solutions of the associated Pontryagin system of FBSDEs that characterizes the equilibria. Therefore, this implies in particular the stability in the 2-Wasserstein distance for the two flows of probability measures describing the agent population density and the $L^2$ distance between the co-states of agents, that are related to the optimal feedback controls. We then prove that the value function of a typical agent converges as $T \to \infty$, and we describe this limit via an infinite horizon MFG system, involving an ergodic constant. All of our convergence results hold true in a unified way for deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven Mean Field Games, in the case of strongly displacement monotone non-separable Hamiltonians. All these are quantitative at exponential rates.

papers.title: Ideal transition systems
papers.abstract: We study an inductive method of computing initial ideals and Gr\"obner bases for families of ideals in a polynomial ring. This method starts from a given set of pairs $(I,J)$ where $I$ is any ideal and $J$ is a monomial ideal contained in the initial ideal of $I$. These containments become a system of equalities if one can establish a particular transition recurrence among the chosen ideals. We describe explicit constructions of such systems in two motivating cases -- namely, for the ideals of matrix Schubert varieties and their skew-symmetric analogues. Despite many formal similarities with these examples, for the symmetric versions of matrix Schubert varieties, it is an open problem to construct the same kind of transition system. We present several conjectures that would follow from such a construction, while also discussing the special obstructions arising in the symmetric case.

papers.title: Construction and sample path properties of diffusion house-moving between two curves
papers.abstract: This study aims to construct a stochastic process called ``diffusion house-moving,'' which is a diffusion bridge conditioned to stay between its starting point and its ending point. To construct this process, statements are prepared on the weak convergence of conditioned diffusion processes, and conditioned diffusion bridges. Moreover, the sample path properties of diffusion house-moving are studied as well.

papers.title: Singularity of the spectrum of typical minimal smooth area-preserving flows in any genus
papers.authors: Krzysztof Fr\k{a}czek, Adam Kanigowski, Corinna Ulcigrai
papers.abstract: We consider smooth flows preserving a smooth invariant measure, or, equivalently, locally Hamiltonian flows on compact orientable surfaces, and show that almost every such locally Hamiltonian flow with only simple saddles has singular spectrum. Furthermore, we prove that for almost every pair of such flows, the elements of the pair are spectrally disjoint. More generally, the results from which these statements are deduced are singularity of the spectrum and pairwise spectral disjointness for special flows over full measure sets of interval exchange transformations under a roof with symmetric logarithmic singularities. Spectral singularity is proved using a criterion based on tightness of Birkhoff sums with exponential tail decay. The assumptions of the criterion are verified exploiting the cancellations proved by the last author to prove the absence of mixing in this class of flows, by showing that the latter can be combined with rigidity by exploiting the local product structure of Rauzy-Veech induction. Pairwise spectral disjointness then follows by producing mixing times (for the second flow), using a new mechanism for shearing based on what we call resonant rigidity times.

papers.title: Nonexistence results for the semilinear wave equation on graphs
papers.authors: Dario Daniele Monticelli, Fabio Punzo, Jacopo Somaglia
papers.abstract: We investigate the semilinear wave equation with potential on weighted graphs. We establish sufficient conditions for the nonexistence of global-in-time solutions. Both nonnegative and sign-changing solutions are considered. In particular, the proof for sign-changing solutions relies on a novel technique for this type of result.

papers.title: Intersections of Schubert varieties and smooth $T$-stable subvarieties of flag varieties
papers.authors: Jaehyun Hong, Eunjeong Lee, Seonjeong Park
papers.abstract: A smooth projective variety equipped with a suitable torus action admits a cell decomposition, called the Bia{\l}ynicki-Birula decomposition. The singularities of the closures of these cells are not well understood in general. Schubert varieties in a flag variety~\(G/B\) are classical examples of such closures, and several criteria for their smoothness are known. In this paper, we study the closures of Bia{\l}ynicki-Birula cells in regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties~\(\mathrm{Hess}(s,h)\), called Hessenberg Schubert varieties. We first investigate the smoothness of intersections of Schubert varieties with \(\mathrm{Hess}(s,h)\), obtaining a sufficient condition for a Hessenberg Schubert variety to be smooth. We also establish several combinatorial sufficient conditions for the smoothness of Hessenberg Schubert varieties in type \(A\).

papers.title: A note on the class of sober rings
papers.abstract: We study sober rings, a class of commutative rings in which every prime non-maximal ideal is not the intersection of the prime ideals strictly containing it. We establish basic structural properties of sober rings and investigate connections to other known classes of rings. We show that sobriety is preserved under quotients and localizations and we examine the behavior of sobriety for polynomial extensions.

papers.title: Hausdorff dimension of the graph of the unweighted error-sum function of continued fractions
papers.abstract: We study the unweighted error-sum function $\mathcal{E}(x) \coloneqq \sum_{n \geq 0} (x - p_n(x)/q_n(x))$, where $p_n(x)/q_n(x)$ denotes the $n$th convergent of the continued fraction expansion of $x \in \mathbb{R}$, and we prove that the graph of $\mathcal{E}$ has Hausdorff dimension $1$. The key ingredient is an exact formula for the oscillation of $\mathcal{E}$ on fundamental intervals, which we obtain in a symbolic space of continued fraction sequences containing non-realizable sequences. Using the same framework, we also give a new derivation of the upper bound $3/2$ of Ridley and Petruska (2000) for the Hausdorff dimension of the graph of the relative error-sum function $P(x) \coloneqq \sum_{n \geq 0} (q_n(x)x - p_n(x))$. Moreover, we present an alternative argument based on M\"obius inversion and summation over coprime convergent denominators, and we explain why the square coverings used for $P$ cannot yield an upper bound smaller than $3/2$.

papers.title: The number of regular simplices in higher dimensions
papers.authors: Felix Christian Clemen, Adrian Dumitrescu, Dingyuan Liu
papers.abstract: We study the extremal function $S^k_d(n)$, defined as the maximum number of regular $(k-1)$-simplices spanned by $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$. For any fixed $d\geq2k\geq6$, we determine the asymptotic behavior of $S^k_d(n)$ up to a lower-order term. In particular, when $k=3$, we determine the exact value of $S^3_d(n)$, for all even dimensions $d\geq6$ and sufficiently large $n$. This resolves a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s in a stronger form. The proof leverages techniques from hypergraph Tur\'an theory and linear algebra.

papers.title: Comparing the face rings of a boolean complex and its barycentric subdivision
papers.abstract: We consider the relationship between the Stanley--Reisner ring (a.k.a. face ring) of a simplicial or boolean complex $\Delta$ and that of its barycentric subdivision. These rings share a distinguished parameter subring. S. Murai asked if they are isomorphic, equivariantly with respect to the automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(\Delta)$, as modules over this parameter subring. We show that, in general, the answer is no, but for Cohen--Macaulay complexes in characteristic coprime to $|\operatorname{Aut}(\Delta)|$, it is yes, and we give an explicit construction of an isomorphism. To give this construction, we adapt a pair of tools introduced by A. Garsia in 1980. The first one transfers bases from a Stanley--Reisner ring to closely related rings of which it is a Gr\"obner degeneration, and the second identifies bases to transfer.

papers.title: Recent perspectives on the Invariant Subspace Problem
papers.abstract: We review recent work connected with the invariant subspace problem for operators, in particular new developments in the last 15 years. In particular, we include discussions of almost-invariant subspaces, universal operators, specific classes of operators and new results in the framework of Banach spaces.

papers.title: General diffusions on metric graphs as limits of space-time Markov chains
papers.abstract: We introduce the Space-Time Markov Chain Approximation (STMCA) for a general diffusion process on a finite metric graph $\Gamma$. The STMCA is a doubly asymmetric (in both time and space) random walk defined on subdivisions of $\Gamma$, with transition probabilities and conditional transition times that match, in expectation, those of the target diffusion. We derive bounds on the $p$-Wasserstein distances between a non-explosive diffusion and its STMCA in terms of a thinness quantifier of the subdivision. An extension to absorbed diffusions uses a boundary-adapted Green-kernel thinness that remains finite even at certain singular exit boundaries. Under the stated regularity and subdivision hypotheses, this gives convergence at any rate strictly less than $\frac14\wedge\frac1p$ in the appropriate thinness quantifier. For suitably adapted subdivisions satisfying a quadratic thinness bound, we show that the rate is doubled: we achieve any rate strictly less than $\frac12\wedge\frac2p$ in terms of the maximum cell size. Additionally, we provide explicit analytical formulas for transition probabilities and times, enabling practical implementation of the STMCA, as well as easily verifiable sufficient non-explosion conditions for the bounds to hold. Numerical experiments illustrate our results.

papers.title: Relative braid group symmetries on modified iquantum groups and their modules
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive generalization of Lusztig's braid group symmetries for quasi-split iquantum groups. Specifically, we give 3 explicit rank one formulas for symmetries acting on integrable modules over a quasi-split iquantum group of arbitrary Kac-Moody type with general parameters. These symmetries are formulated in terms of idivided powers and iweights of the vectors being acted upon. We show that these symmetries are consistent with the relative braid group symmetries on iquantum groups, and they are also related to Lusztig's symmetries via quasi $K$-matrices. Furthermore, through appropriate rescaling, we obtain compatible symmetries for the integral forms of modified iquantum groups and their integrable modules. We verify that these symmetries satisfy the relative braid group relations.

papers.title: The Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^{p}_{FIO}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ for Fourier integral operators for $p<1$
papers.authors: Naijia Liu, Jan Rozendaal, Liang Song
papers.abstract: We introduce the Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^{p}_{FIO}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ for Fourier integral operators for $0<p<1$, thereby extending earlier constructions for $1\leq p\leq \infty$. We then establish various properties of these spaces, including their behavior under complex interpolation and duality, and their invariance under Fourier integral operators. We also obtain Sobolev embeddings, equivalent characterizations, and a molecular decomposition. These spaces are used in the companion article arXiv:2502.02511 to determine the sharp $\mathcal{H}^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ and $\mathrm{bmo}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ regularity of wave equations with rough coefficients.

papers.title: Bistatic Target Detection by Exploiting Both Deterministic Pilots and Unknown Random Data Payloads
papers.authors: Lei Xie, Fan Liu, Shenghui Song, Shi Jin
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) plays a crucial role in 6G, enabling innovative applications such as drone surveillance, urban air mobility, and low-altitude logistics.
