However, the hybrid ISAC signal, which comprises deterministic pilot and random data payload components, poses challenges for target detection due to two reasons: 1) these two components cause coupled shifts in both the mean and variance of the received signal, and 2) the random data payloads are typically unknown to the sensing receiver in the bistatic setting. Unfortunately, these challenges could not be tackled by existing target detection algorithms. In this paper, a generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT)-based detector is derived by leveraging the known deterministic pilots and the statistical characteristics of the unknown random data payloads. Due to the analytical intractability of exact performance characterization, we perform an asymptotic analysis for the false alarm probability and detection probability of the proposed detector. The results reveal a deterministic-random trade-off: the deterministic pilots enhance detection through a target-induced mean shift, while the random data payloads provide an additional covariance-domain target signature but simultaneously introduce statistical uncertainty due to their unknown realizations. Simulations validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed detector, which highlights the necessity of designing a dedicated detector to fully exploit the signaling resources assigned to random data payloads.

papers.title: Geodesic clustering of zeros of Eisenstein series for congruence groups
papers.authors: Sebasti\'an Carrillo Santana, Gunther Cornelissen, Berend Ringeling
papers.abstract: We consider a set of generators for the space of Eisenstein series of varying even weight $k$ for any fixed congruence group $\Gamma$ and study the set of all of their zeros taken for all $\Gamma(1)$-conjugates of $\Gamma$ in the standard fundamental domain for $\Gamma(1)$. We describe (a) an upper bound $\kappa_\Gamma + O(1/k)$ for their imaginary part; (b) a finite configuration of geodesics segments to which all zeros converge in Hausdorff distance as $k \rightarrow \infty$; (c) a finite set containing all algebraic zeros for all weights. The bound in (a) depends on the (non-)vanishing of a new generalization of Ramanujan sums. The proof of (b) originates in a method used to study phase transitions in statistical physics. The proof of (c) relies on the theory of complex multiplication. The results can be made quantitative for specific groups. For $\Gamma=\Gamma(N)$ with $4 \nmid N$, $\kappa_\Gamma=1$ and the zeros tend to the unit circle, whereas if $4 \mid N$, $\kappa_\Gamma=2$ and the limit configuration includes parts of vertical geodesics and circles of radius $2$. In both cases, for sufficiently large $k$, the only algebraic zeros are at $\mathrm{i}$ and $\exp(2\pi \mathrm{i}/3)$, and, for $4 \mid N$, at $2\mathrm{i}$. For $\Gamma(N)$ with $N$ odd, we use finer estimates to prove a trichotomy for the exact `convergence speed' of the zeros to the unit circle, as well as angular equidistribution of the zeros as $k \rightarrow + \infty$, implying weak convergence of the normalized zero counting measure on $Y(1)$ to the image of the argument measure on the lower arc of the fundamental domain.

papers.title: Perfect t-Embeddings of Uniformly Weighted Generalized Tower Graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study sequences of perfect t-embeddings of a uniformly weighted family of graphs we call generalized tower graphs. We show that the embeddings of these graphs satisfy certain technical assumptions, in particular, the rigidity assumption of Berggren-Nicoletti-Russkikh. As a result, we confirm the convergence of the gradients of the height function fluctuations of these graphs to those of the Gaussian free field.

papers.title: Application of Onsager's Variational Principle to the Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: In this note we propose a basic $L^2$-based approach for studying the global and local energy equalities of the incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes equations in the standard energy class on $\mathbb{T}^3 \times (0,T]$. Motivated by L. Onsager's principle of least dissipation of energy (1931), we give a new sufficient condition for the energy equalities in terms of the limit of a sequence of minimizers. In particular, we show that the equalities are attained if this limit is non-vanishing. We observe that the indeterminacy in the vanishing case is reminiscent of turbulence-driven energy transfer dominating other transport processes.

papers.title: Hyperbolic Monge-Amp\`ere Equation on a Cylinder: Well-Posedness and Stability
papers.abstract: This paper develops a rigorous analytic framework for the hyperbolic Monge-Amp\`ere equation on strip-like domains, which model wrinkled patterns in thin elastic sheets. Our work addresses the rigid side of the classical rigidity-flexibility dichotomy by defining this regime not by high smoothness, but by the more fundamental property of partial convexity. The hodograph transformation is the natural tool for this setting, as its validity is predicated on partial convexity. It converts the nonlinear Monge-Amp\`ere equation into a linear damped wave equation, allowing us to formulate a well-posed Cauchy-Goursat problem. A key challenge is the corner singularity that arises where characteristic and non-characteristic boundary data meet. To resolve this, we develop a parametrix-corrector decomposition that captures the solution's inherent singular behavior. This method recasts the problem as a singular Volterra integral equation, for which we prove the existence and uniqueness of a new class of hodograph weak solutions. Finally, we derive energy estimates to establish the quantitative stability of these rigid solutions under perturbations of the underlying curvature function.

papers.title: Approximate Bregman proximal gradient algorithm with variable metric Armijo line search
papers.authors: Kiwamu Fujiki, Shota Takahashi, Akiko Takeda
papers.abstract: We propose a variant of the approximate Bregman proximal gradient (ABPG) algorithm for minimizing the sum of a smooth nonconvex function and a nonsmooth convex function. ABPG is known to converge globally to a stationary point even when the smooth part of the objective function does not have a globally Lipschitz continuous gradient, and its iterates can often be expressed in closed form. However, ABPG relies on an Armijo line search to guarantee global convergence, which can slow down its practical performance. To address this issue, we propose a variant of ABPG with a variable metric Armijo line search, which relaxes the Armijo condition. We prove that the line search terminates in finitely many steps for a general nonsmooth convex function. Under the variable metric Armijo condition, we establish global subsequential convergence of the algorithm. Moreover, assuming the Kurdyka--\L{}ojasiewicz property, we also prove that the algorithm globally converges to a stationary point. Numerical experiments on $\ell_p$-regularized least squares problems, nonnegative linear inverse problems and phase retrieval demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing algorithms.

papers.title: Corrections and additions to "A note on the hit problem for the polynomial algebra in the case of odd primes and its application" [Rev. R. Acad. Cienc. Exactas F\'is. Nat. Ser. A Mat. 118 (2024), article 22]
papers.abstract: In this work, we correct results in the published paper [Rev. R. Acad. Cienc. Exactas F\'is. Nat. Ser. A Mat. 118 (2024), article 22]. We determine the non-hit kernel of the first reduced power in polynomial degree $p+1$, identify the published Frobenius construction as zero on indecomposables, and replace the multiplier assertion by a theorem with explicit degree hypotheses. We also classify the monomial multipliers of Frobenius that preserve hits in one variable. For the third algebraic transfer, we correct the target dimensions and establish surjectivity throughout the four principal degree families. Explicit invariant calculations and Minami's degree reduction give isomorphisms in seven infinite families at $p=3$ and $p=5$, including a family with an initial change from dimension one to dimension two. For every odd prime, compatibility with the Frobenius operation on $\operatorname{Ext}$ gives an exact sequence comparing successive transfer kernels and forces a nonzero invariant extraction kernel at every second-family dimension jump. We compute the first cohomology of a nonzero extraction kernel and determine the exact obstruction to injectivity from rank-two products in the first and fourth families. Coefficient extraction and changes of coordinates give an additional infinite isomorphism family and a spanning result for annihilated polynomial homology. At each extraction isomorphism, the quotient by all rank-two products is preserved as a general linear group module. We distinguish these results from the unresolved invariant dimensions at arbitrary normalized index differences, and give the precise limitations of composition-factor counts and Dickson multiplication. An appendix supplies explicit representatives for all the nonzero rank-two invariant lines in Crossley's dimension classification.

papers.title: Eventually periodic resolutions with applications to integral group rings
papers.abstract: We present a general construction of eventually periodic projective resolutions for modules over the quotient of a ring by a regular central element. Our approach combines the iterated mapping cone technique with the higher homotopies of Shamash. The periodic part of each resolution comes from a matrix factorization of the central element. The construction is applied to the integral group rings of quotients of groups of finite cohomological dimension by infinite cyclic central subgroups. We give explicit calculations for several families of groups, including hyperbolic triangle groups and the mapping class group of the plane with four punctures.

papers.title: Individual Minima-Informed Multi-Objective Model Predictive Control for Fixed Point Stabilization
papers.abstract: In multi-objective model predictive control (MOMPC), a single Pareto-optimal solution has to be selected at each sampling instant by an automated a priori decision-making (DM) mechanism, since real-time constraints do not permit a human decision-maker to be involved. This paper considers MOMPC for fixed point stabilization, where the DM translates a high-level preference into the solution to be implemented, while closed-loop stability has to be preserved. To this end, an approach called individual minima-informed DM is introduced. These methods leverage the individual minima, which are characteristic Pareto-optimal points, to facilitate the translation of a high-level preference to a point on the Pareto front. They can be implemented through two sequential optimizations, regardless of the number of objectives, thereby facilitating a real-time implementation of MOMPC. Two novel methods are proposed and compared with four established ones. These methods are embedded into a stabilizing MOMPC scheme that builds on a quasi-infinite horizon framework from the literature. Closed-loop stability is proven under a descent condition that is less restrictive than the one in the original framework and retains the largest DM space among all descent conditions that prevent any objective from increasing. The required terminal ingredients can be constructed with a practical procedure. In a numerical case study, the resulting scheme stabilizes the fixed point and illustrates the potential benefit of adapting the preference online.

papers.title: The iterates of FISTA converge even under inexact computations and stochastic gradients
papers.abstract: Very recently, the papers "Point Convergence of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Method: An AI-Assisted Proof" by Jang and Ryu, and "The Iterates of Nesterov's Accelerated Algorithm Converge in the Critical Regimes" by Bot, Fadili, and Nguyen have simultaneously resolved a long-standing open problem concerning Nesterov's accelerated gradient method. These works show that the iterates of the algorithm (known in its composite form as FISTA) indeed converge to an optimal solution. In this work, we extend these results and prove that, in infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces, the iterates of such an algorithm still converge (in the weak sense) even when the proximity operator and the gradient are computed inexactly, with the latter possibly stochastic. Our framework covers both absolute and relative errors in proximal computations. In the stochastic setting, it allows for uniformly bounded variance as well as proximal counterparts of strong growth conditions, under which iterate convergence can be established while retaining accelerated objective-value rates.

papers.title: Palindromic switching rook polynomials and domino-stable collections of cells
papers.authors: Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, Giancarlo Rinaldo
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a finite collection of cells. Two non-attacking rook configurations on $\mathcal{P}$ are switching-equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of switches inside rectangles contained in $\mathcal{P}$. The switching rook polynomial of $\mathcal{P}$ enumerates the resulting equivalence classes according to the number of rooks. We characterize the collections of cells whose switching rook polynomial is palindromic. More precisely, we introduce a new combinatorial property, called domino-stability, and we prove that the switching rook polynomial of $\mathcal{P}$ is palindromic if and only if $\mathcal{P}$ is domino-stable.

papers.title: Weinstein Handlebodies for the Painlev\'e Betti Spaces
papers.authors: Jo\"el D. Beimler, William E. Olsen
papers.abstract: We prove that the generic fibre of the Betti moduli space associated to any of the ten Painlev\'e equations coincides with the result of attaching Weinstein handles along the Stokes Legendrian, and provide Weinstein handlebody diagrams for each of them in the process. We moreover extend the procedure for obtaining presentations in Gompf normal form of Weinstein manifolds obtained by attaching handles to Legendrian lifts of cooriented curves in surfaces to their unit cotangent bundle to the case where the surface may have nonempty boundary.

papers.title: Homogenization of a thin linear elastic plate reinforced with a periodic mosaic of small rigid plates
papers.authors: Amartya Chakrabortty, Georges Griso, Julia Orlik
papers.abstract: In the framework of linearized elasticity, we study thin elastic composite plates with thickness $\delta$. The plates contain small, rigid rectangular plates distributed periodically along $\varepsilon$. Between two neighboring rigid plates is an elastic beam with thickness $\delta < \varepsilon/3 < 1$. Through a simultaneous process of homogenization and dimension reduction, we obtain the limit model. Our analysis yields Korn-type inequalities adapted to the rigid-elastic geometry of the structure and provides a precise characterization of the limit deformation and displacement fields. In the $2$D limit problem, the bending is the sum of two functions, each depending on only one variable. This is due to the fact that the mixed derivatives of the outer-plane displacement vanish. Finally, the limiting 2D problem is two decoupled plates or strips, each one with just three degrees of freedom: shear along the strip axis, the cross-contraction (-extension), and the cross-bending. The corresponding correctors are defined in the same way in the periodicity cell. In the linearized setting, all the correctors are decomposed.

papers.title: Expansivity of algebraic semigroup actions
papers.abstract: For a semigroup $S$ and a right $\mathbb{Z}[S]$-submodule $J\leq \mathbb{Z}[S]^n$, we study expansivity of the algebraic action of $S$ induced on the Pontryagin dual of $\mathbb{Z}[S]^n/J$. We completely determine the class of semigroups for which expansivity of this action is characterized by the triviality of $J^\perp$, in terms of the existence of a finite subset $K\subseteq S$ such that $S=KS$. This condition is satisfied in particular by every monoid, and more generally by every semigroup with a left unital convolution Banach algebra, in which case we are able to extend the characterization of expansivity in terms of an invertibility condition when $J$ is finitely generated. We also exhibit examples of non-unital semigroups satisfying the hypotheses of our results.

papers.title: Adversarial Problems and the Limits of Uniform Resolution
papers.abstract: A general method of resolution can take part in forming problems once their language represents the method itself. A fixed formation rule gives each sound resolver a presentation it cannot answer. Admitting the diagnosis yields a sound successor with an instance of its own. For standard arithmetical theories $\mathrm{T}$, the instance is $\mathsf{HA}$-provably equivalent to $\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{T})$. A theory that decides its own instance asserts a false sentence. The $m$-th iterated independence question is equivalent to the instance $m$ stages later. No effective admission policy with consistent union closes the regress. A noncomputable answer function resolves all program indices, while a false assertion of resolution supplies no warrant. At feasible scale, bounded self-consistency is cheap. A clocked G\"odel sentence gives an unconditional gap relative to its short binary description, but no superpolynomial lower bound in the window size. The arithmetic identity motivates studying bounded consistency of the successor theory, as in a conjecture of Pudl\'ak. We state its finitely axiomatized case and prove that it implies $\mathcal{NP}\ne\mathrm{co}\mathcal{NP}$. The conjecture motivates a feasible analogue, but does not establish all clauses of the unbounded barrier.

papers.title: A Li-Yau and Aronson-B\'enilan approach for the Keller-Segel system with critical exponent
papers.authors: Charles Elbar, Alejandro Fern\'andez-Jim\'enez, Filippo Santambrogio
papers.abstract:
The Li-Yau and Aronson-B\'enilan estimates are fundamental differential inequalities for heat and porous-medium equations, yielding differential Harnack inequalities and sharp smoothing and decay rates. We develop analogues for the critical parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where diffusion and aggregation act at the same scale. Our main tool is the effective pressure $v=p-u$, with $p=\log\rho$ in $d=2$ and $p=\frac{m}{m-1}\rho^{m-1}$ for $d>2$, $m=2-\frac{2}{d}$. We prove quantitative lower bounds on $\Delta v$, showing that classical pressure estimates subsist in a suitable form despite the nonlocal interaction.
  These estimates unify previous results and yield new regularity. For nonnegative finite-measure initial data of sufficiently small mass, assuming only a logarithmic moment in $d=2$, we construct global solutions smooth for positive times and satisfying $\|\rho_t\|_{L^\infty}\le C/t$. For finite-free-energy data, we obtain global $L^\infty$ bounds of order $1+t^{-1}$ in the subcritical and critical mass regimes.
  We also introduce a new characterization of the critical mass as the minimal mass $M_c^{\mathrm{sub}}(d)$ of subsolutions of the elliptic Lane-Emden equation (Liouville in $d=2$). We prove that it equals $8\pi$ in dimension $2$ and, for $d\ge3$, coincides with the Keller-Segel critical mass given by the HLS inequality, by reducing the problem to a one-dimensional optimal-control problem.
  Along the way we prove tools of independent interest: $L^\infty$ estimates from lower bounds on $\Delta v$, critical log-HLS/HLS estimates away from Dirac masses, Hessian bounds for Newtonian potentials, and Lipschitz and Hessian estimates for bounded porous-medium solutions with drifts on the whole space.

papers.title: Classical elliptic ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model: relation to Zhukovsky-Volterra gyrostat and 1-site classical XYZ model with boundaries
papers.abstract: We present a description of the classical elliptic ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model with 8 independent coupling constants through a pair of ${\rm BC}_1$ type classical Sklyanin algebras generated by the (classical) quadratic reflection equation with non-dynamical XYZ $r$-matrix. For this purpose, we consider the classical version of the $L$-operator for the Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model proposed by O. Chalykh. In ${\rm BC}_1$ case it is factorized to the product of two Lax matrices depending on 4 constants. Then we apply an IRF-Vertex type gauge transformation and obtain a product of the Lax matrices for the Zhukovsky-Volterra gyrostats. Each of them is described by the ${\rm BC}_1$ version of the classical Sklyanin algebra. In particular case, when 4 pairs of constants coincide, the ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model exactly coincides with the relativistic Zhukovsky-Volterra gyrostat. Explicit change of variables is obtained. We also consider another special case of the ${\rm BC}_1$ Ruijsenaars-van Diejen model with 7 independent constants. We show that it can be reproduced by considering the transfer matrix of the classical 1-site XYZ chain with boundaries. In the end of the paper, using another gauge transformation we represent the Chalykh's Lax matrix in a form depending on the Sklyanin's generators.

papers.title: Second-Order Schalkwijk-Kailath Coding for Autoregressive Gaussian Channels
papers.authors: Jun Su (Shitz), Guangyue Han (Shitz), Shlomo Shamai (Shitz)
papers.abstract: We study noiseless-feedback communication over Gaussian channels with stationary autoregressive (AR) noise of arbitrary finite order. We introduce a class of Gaussian linear-feedback coding schemes based on the celebrated Schalkwijk--Kailath (SK) coding scheme, called SK(2), whose message process follows a second-order deterministic recursion, and derive a closed-form characterization of its maximal achievable rate under average power constraint $P$. As a first-order benchmark, we formulate SK(1) as a sign-consistent, branch-complete version of the real constant signed-ratio specialization of Butman's linear-feedback construction. For stationary AR($p$) Gaussian channels, optimizing over recursions with both characteristic roots outside the unit circle gives the same rate supremum as optimizing over all SK(2) recursions and yields a rate no smaller than the maximal SK(1) rate. The SK(2) scheme achieves feedback capacity for the AWGN channel, stationary AR(1) Gaussian channels, and a subclass of stationary AR(2) Gaussian channels obtained by interleaving two independent AR(1) noise processes. For the interleaved subclass, we show that a genuine SK(2) scheme strictly outperforms SK(1). Numerical comparisons illustrate further strict rate gains over a broader range of AR(2) parameters. These results show that the SK(1) scheme is not universally optimal beyond AR(1) noise and disprove a corrected form of Butman's conjecture.

papers.title: Polar decompositions of complex varieties and tropical homotopy theory
papers.abstract:
We take the first steps towards developing a tropical homotopy theory, which we use to construct explicit finite CW complex structures on smooth complex varieties. Our approach decomposes a variety into a set of radial and angular parts, a construction we call polar decomposition. We derive a combinatorial formula for the $f$-vector of the resulting CW complex in terms of a weighted sum of local angle $f$-vectors, and we determine these $f$-vectors explicitly for toric varieties and complete intersections in terms of Stirling numbers.
  To construct these decompositions, we introduce the notion of a rational tropical manifold, which we view as a tropical manifold with a non-reduced structure. The local topology of these is dictated by Kummer coverings of affine linear spaces in a complex torus, as opposed to the affine linear spaces in the theory of tropical manifolds. Examples of such manifolds include the Fermat and Dwork hypersurfaces.
  Using Kato-Nakayama spaces, we associate a diagram of topological spaces to any rational tropical manifold. We then construct a cofibrant replacement of this diagram using sealed Kato-Nakayama spaces to show that the homotopy colimit is homotopy equivalent to a general nearby fiber. To construct CW complex structures, we then show that the spaces in the diagram can be replaced by their angle sets. More precisely, for any Kummer covering of a very affine linear space, we prove that the angle map is a homotopy equivalence, extending earlier work of Salvetti and Bj\"{o}rner--Ziegler. We construct compatible cellulations for these angle spaces and show that these give rise to an explicit CW complex structure on the nearby fibers. For complete intersections, we make these spaces and all the CW complex structures completely explicit using refined Coxeter arrangements.

papers.title: Generalizations of tropical Tevelev degrees
papers.abstract: We study tropical Tevelev degrees arising from maps between certain tropical moduli spaces of curves. Building on work of Dawson and Cavalieri, who defined and computed tropical Tevelev degrees in the case of degree $d = g+1$ and $n = g+3$ marked points, we extend the theory by introducing an additional integer parameter $\ell$. In our framework the curve degree and number of marked points vary as $d = g + 1 + \ell$ and $n = g + 3 + 2\ell$, and we analyze the resulting tropical Tevelev degrees for both positive and negative values of $\ell$. This tropicalizes results of Cela, Pandharipande, and Schmitt on algebraic Tevelev degrees. We then further broaden the framework by introducing generalized tropical Tevelev degrees, providing the tropical counterpart to the generalized Tevelev degrees studied by Cela and Lian. These results establish a wider set of computational and structural patterns for intersection calculations on tropical moduli spaces and reveal new behavior beyond the classical setting.

papers.title: Symmetries and Higher-Form Connections in Derived Differential Geometry
papers.authors: Severin Bunk, Lukas M\"uller, Joost Nuiten, Richard J. Szabo
papers.abstract: We introduce a general definition of higher-form connections on principal $\infty$-bundles in differential geometry. These connections are built as infinitesimal parallel transports and thus satisfy the fake-curvature condition. We achieve this by developing the formal differentiation and integration of maps from smooth manifolds to derived stacks with sufficient deformation theory. That allows us to introduce the Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid of a principal $\infty$-bundle and establish its global sections as the $L_\infty$-algebra of the derived higher symmetry group of the bundle. We define the space of $p$-form connections on an $\infty$-bundle as the space of order $p$ splittings of its Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid. This can be cast equivalently as lifting the classifying map of a bundle on a manifold to the order $p$ truncation of the de Rham stack of the manifold. We demonstrate that our new concept of derived geometric $p$-form connections recovers the known notion of connections on higher U(1)-bundles defined via \v{C}ech-Deligne differential cocycles. We further relate the $L_\infty$-algebras of derived higher symmetries of higher U(1)-bundles and higher Courant algebroids. Some applications in higher gauge theory and in supergravity are mentioned.

papers.title: On the $q$-integrability of $p$-Wasserstein barycenters
papers.abstract: We study the $L^q$-regularity of the density of barycenters of $N$ probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to the $p$-Wasserstein metric ($1<p<\infty$). According to a previous result by the first author and collaborators, if one marginal is absolutely continuous, so is the $W_p$-barycenter. The next natural question is whether the $L^q$- regularity on the marginals is also preserved for any $q > 1$, as in the classical case ($p=2$) of Agueh--Carlier, or for $W_p$-geodesics ($N=2$). Here we prove that this is the case if one marginal belongs to $L^q$ and the supports of all the marginals satisfy suitable geometric assumptions. However, we show that, as soon as $N>2$, it is possible to find examples of $W_p$-barycenters which are not $q$-integrable, even if one marginal is compactly supported and bounded, thus highlighting the role played by the geometry of the supports. Furthermore, we provide a general estimate of the $L^q$-norm, including a detailed study of the sources of singularities, and a characterization of the $W_p$-barycenters \`a la Agueh--Carlier in terms of the associated Kantorovich potentials. Finally, we explicitly compute the $W_p$-barycenters of measures obtained as push-forward of special affine transformations. In this case, regularity holds without any additional requirement on the supports.

papers.title: Generalized fluctuation bounds for stochastic algorithms in the presence of compactness
papers.authors: Morenikeji Neri, Nicholas Pischke, Thomas Powell
papers.abstract: We provide a convergence result for sequences of random variables taking values in a metric space that satisfy a stochastic quasi-Fej\'er monotonicity condition, in the context of a (local) compactness assumption. Our result is quantitative in that we derive an explicit and effective construction which, in terms of only a few moduli representing quantitative witnesses to key properties of the sequence of random variables and the underlying metric space involved, provides a metastable rate of pointwise convergence, a type of generalized fluctuation bound. That quantitative result in particular relies on the development of a finitary theory of martingales, culminating in a fully finitary Robbins-Siegmund theorem. We outline how this result particularises to the circumstances of the seminal work of Combettes and Pesquet on stochastic quasi-Fej\'er monotone sequences in separable Hilbert spaces, and we provide an initial application by illustrating how these results can be used to provide a metastable rate of pointwise convergence for a stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann scheme solving a stochastic common fixed point problem for nonexpansive maps over proper Hadamard spaces. This work is set in the context of recent applications of the logic-based methodology of proof mining to probability theory, and represents its most sophisticated case study to date.

papers.title: Nodal Coarsening and Approximate Ideal Interpolation for H(curl) in Algebraic Multigrid
papers.authors: Taoli Shen, James Brannick, Robert Falgout, Karsten Kahl, Jacob Schroder
papers.abstract: We propose an approximate interpolation construction and a practical coarsening algorithm for algebraic multigrid (AMG) method when applied to H(curl) problems. Building on the generalized AMG framework, we introduce an interior/exterior splitting that yields both a refinement-based and a fully algebraic construction of the interpolation. The refinement-based approach follows a geometric hierarchy, while the purely algebraic interpolation is constructed through a coarsening process that first coarsens a nodal dual problem and then builds coarse and fine variables using a matching algorithm. Under a uniform fine-space smoothing assumption, we prove a jump-independent two-grid convergence bound for canonical finite-element spaces. We also establish an exact commuting relation for the unshifted construction. Two-dimensional numerical experiments demonstrate sparse multilevel hierarchies and robust convergence under strong coefficient jumps in the curl--curl term. Three-dimensional experiments provide a two-level proof of concept, although the interpolation operators remain dense. Developing a practical sparse three-dimensional multilevel method is left to future work.

papers.title: Online Order Fulfillment with Replenishment
papers.authors: Zi Ling, Jiashuo Jiang, Linwei Xin
papers.abstract:
In modern e-commerce and service operations, firms jointly manage inventory replenishment and real-time order fulfillment under demand uncertainty. We study their interaction in a single-resource lost-sales system with heterogeneous rewards, positive lead times, and replenishment cycles of length $T$. A central difficulty is that low regret in one fulfillment cycle need not imply a small profit gap under repeated replenishment, since fulfillment decisions change inventory and, under base-stock replenishment, subsequent orders.
  We consider base-stock and constant-order replenishment and compare online fulfillment with a myopic offline benchmark that knows current-cycle demand but not future demand. We give conditions under which $O(T^\alpha)$ one-cycle regret yields an $O(T^\alpha)$ upper bound on the expected average profit gap, uniformly over all finite horizons $N$. For base stock, the bound remains valid when the online and offline targets are optimized separately. For constant orders, a uniform quadratic count-loss bound gives an unrestricted two-sided comparison between separately optimized systems. For the cycle-restarted Bayes Selector, the finite-horizon bounds are $O(1)$. The optimized long-run constant-order profit gap is also $O(1)$.
  We use these results to compare optimized base stock with greedy fulfillment against optimized constant order with the Bayes Selector and decompose the profit difference into replenishment and fulfillment components. A representative finite-horizon simulation shows that the ranking of the two policy combinations can change with cycle length. We also extend the transfer analysis to multiple resources. Under single-resource base-stock replenishment, a mean-LP quota policy has uniform $O(\sqrt T)$ regret against full-information benchmark.

papers.title: Optimization with Parametric Variational Inequality Constraints on a Moving Set Based on a Smoothing Method
papers.authors: Xiaojun Chen, Jin Zhang, Yixuan Zhang
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on optimization problems constrained by Parametric Variational Inequalities (PVI) defined on a moving set. Unlike most existing works on mathematical programs with equilibrium constraints, the equilibrium constraints have parameters not only in the function but also in the related set. We show that the solution function of the PVI is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the upper-level decision variables and the solution set of the optimization problem is nonempty and bounded. Moreover, we prove that the metric regularity of the constraints holds automatically, which allows us to characterize stationary points without any additional assumptions. A Smoothing Implicit Gradient Algorithm (SIGA) is proposed based on the smoothing approximation of the PVI with a novel scheme for updating the smoothing parameter. We prove the convergence of SIGA to a stationary point and validate the efficiency of SIGA by numerical examples from synthetic problems and portfolio management with real data.

papers.title: A new lower bound for the kissing number in 19 dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that the kissing number in 19 dimensions is at least 11948, improving the bound of Cohn and Li by 256. Their odd-sign construction reduces the problem to finding a binary code of length 19 and minimum distance 5 inside a 5-punctured extended binary Golay code. In an explicit model $D$ of this ambient code, the 21 words of weights 3 and 4 are exactly the pairwise differences that such a code must avoid. They span a 10-dimensional subcode $K$. We exhibit a 6-dimensional subcode $M\le K$ for which all 21 words lie in only five cosets of $M$. After identifying $K/M$ with $\mathbb F_2^4$, these five cosets are represented by $\Sigma=\{e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4,e_1+e_2+e_3+e_4\}$. In the graph on $\mathbb F_2^4$ in which $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $u+v\in\Sigma$, the set $\Sigma$ itself is independent. Lifting its five vertices gives 320 words in $K$, and translating this set through the four cosets of $K$ in $D$ gives a nonlinear code of size 1280 and minimum distance 5.

papers.title: Characteristic cycles of real and complex constructible sheaves, revisited
papers.authors: Ren Fernandes, Kazuki Kudomi, Kiyoshi Takeuchi
papers.abstract: For a smooth morphism $f: X \longrightarrow \Sigma$ of real analytic manifolds and an $\mathbb{R}$-constructible sheaf $F$ on $X$ satisfying some condition, we define a family of Lagrangian cycles parameterized by $\Sigma$ that we call the relative characteristic cycle of $F$ for $f$. In this way, the theory of characteristic cycles due to Kashiwara and Schapira is naturally extended to the relative setting. Based on it, we then prove a formula for the characteristic cycles of real nearby cycle sheaves. This leads us to obtain also formulas for the characteristic cycles of various constructible sheaves, such as specialization, microlocalization, and complex nearby and vanishing cycle sheaves, in a unified manner. In fact, our methods allow us to calculate not only their characteristic cycles but also their microlocal types in many situations. We will illustrate it by various examples.

papers.title: Density results for $r$-gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta-function
papers.abstract: Let $0<\gamma_1\leq \gamma_2\leq \ldots$ denote the positive ordinates of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta-function. A result first announced by Selberg states that there exist absolute constants $\Theta, \vartheta>0$ such that for each $r\in \mathbb{N}$, \[ \limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{\gamma_{n+r}-\gamma_n}{2\pi r/\log \gamma_n}\geq 1+\frac{\Theta}{r^\alpha} \qquad \text{and}\qquad \liminf_{n\to \infty}\frac{\gamma_{n+r}-\gamma_n}{2\pi r/\log \gamma_n}\leq 1-\frac{\vartheta}{r^\alpha} \] where $\alpha$ may be taken as $2/3$, or as $1/2$ if one assumes the Riemann hypothesis. This was recently proved by Conrey and Turnage-Butterbaugh under RH and by Inoue unconditionally. We prove that in fact a positive proportion of $r$-gaps are large (and small) to the above extent, and we provide explicit estimates for the sizes and proportions of these gaps. In the case $r=1$, this quantitatively improves an unconditional result of Simoni\v{c}, Trudgian and Turnage-Butterbaugh.

papers.title: Self-similar finite-time blowups with singular profiles of the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda model: theoretical and numerical investigations
papers.authors: De Huang, Jiajun Tong, Xiuyuan Wang
papers.abstract: For the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda model with a parameter $a$, we investigate novel scenarios of self-similar finite-time blowups that arise from a new setting where the smooth initial data satisfy a certain derivative degeneracy condition. In this setting, our numerical study reveals distinct self-similar blowup behaviors depending on the sign of $a$. For $a>0$, we observe one-scale self-similar blowups with regular profiles that have not been found in previous studies. In contrast, for $a\le 0$, we discover a novel two-scale self-similar blowup scenario where the outer profile converges to a singular function at the blowup time while the inner profile remains regular on a much smaller scale. Correspondingly, an $a$-parameterized family of singular self-similar profiles with explicit expressions are constructed for $a<0$ and shown to match nicely with the limiting profiles obtained in numerical simulation. In particular, for the specific case of $a=0$, we rigorously prove the convergence of the outer profile to an explicit singular function in self-similar coordinates. Furthermore, we demonstrate the two-scale nature of the blowup in this scenario by showing that the local inner profile behavior around the singularity point of the outer profile is governed by a traveling wave on a smaller scale. To support this observation, we rigorously establish the existence of such traveling wave solutions via a fixed-point method.

papers.title: On the optimal relaxation parameter of graph-based splitting methods for subspaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of the family of graph-based splitting algorithms specialized to the problem of finding a point in the intersection of linear subspaces. The algorithms in this family, which encompasses several classical methods such as the Douglas-Rachford algorithm, are defined by a connected graph and a subgraph. Our main result establishes that when the graph and subgraph coincide, the optimal relaxation parameter is exactly $1$, thereby extending known results for the Douglas-Rachford algorithm to a much broader class of methods. Our analysis hinges on some properties of iso-averaged linear operators, which are defined as the average of an isometry and the identity, and are characterized by a specific symmetry of the norm of their relaxation.

papers.title: Geometric singularities of regular surfaces with nef anti-canonical divisors over imperfect fields
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a regular projective surface over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, with $H^0(S,\mathcal{O}_S)=k$ and $-K_S$ nef. We prove that $S$ is geometrically integral over $k$ when $p\geq 7$, and we also find an example of $S$ that is not geometrically integral when $p=5$.

papers.title: Local discontinuous Galerkin FEM for convex minimization
papers.abstract:
The heart of the a priori and a posteriori error control in convex minimization problems is the sharp control of the differences of discrete and exact minimal energy. Conforming finite element discretizations for p-Laplace type minimization problems provide upper bounds of the energy difference with optimal convergence rates. Even for smooth solutions, known convergence rates for higher-order non-conforming finite element discretizations for the same problem class with $2 < p < \infty$, however, are exclusively suboptimal. Thus the popular a posteriori error control within the two-energy principle, that generalize hyper-circle identities, appears unbalanced.
  The innovative point of departure in a refined analysis of two discontinuous Galerkin (dG) schemes exploits duality relations between a discrete primal and a semi-discrete dual problem. The infinite-dimensional dual problem leads to a tiny duality gap that even vanishes for polynomial low-order terms. For a class of degenerated convex minimization problems with two-sided $p$ growth, the novel duality provides improved a priori convergence rates for the error in the minimal energies. This closes the misfit of convergence rates for the conforming and nonconforming schemes at least for the local discontinuous Galerkin schemes at hand. The motivating two-energy principle and some post-processing for a Raviart-Thomas dual variable provides an a posteriori error control, that also may drive adaptive mesh-refining. Computational benchmarks provide numerical evidence for improved convergence rates of the adaptive beyond uniform mesh-refining.

papers.title: Counterexamples to a dimension-free variant of Erd\H{o}s's diameter conjecture for separated distances
papers.abstract: Erd\H{o}s asked about the least possible diameter of an $n$-point set in Euclidean space when any two pairwise distances differ by at least $1$. We consider the uniform-in-dimension variant of his question, in which the dimension $d$ may grow with $n$ and the error term is independent of $d$, and answer it in the negative by an explicit construction. For every prime power $q$, we construct a set $\mathcal X_n$ of $n=q+1$ points in $\mathbb R^{q^2+q}=\mathbb R^{n^2-n}$ such that the $\binom{n}{2}$ pairwise distances are mutually at least $1$ apart, yet $$\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal X_n)\le \Bigl(1-\frac{1}{\pi^2}+o(1)\Bigr)n^2.$$ The construction combines a Singer cyclic difference set with a weighted product of $N=\binom n2$ regular $m$-gons, where $m=q^2+q+1$. The weights are chosen so that the resulting distances increase while the gaps between consecutive distances decrease. After normalizing the smallest gap to $1$, all distinct pairwise distances are separated by at least $1$, while the diameter has asymptotic constant $1-1/\pi^2<1$.

papers.title: Counterexamples for lacunary dilates via dyadic spike blocks
papers.abstract:
We construct counterexamples, along dyadic lacunary sequences, to two problems of Erd\H{o}s on the almost-everywhere behavior of sums $\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)$ on the circle. The main device is a dyadic spike block: rare positive spikes, each counted many times by a run of consecutive dilates, make the lacunary averages large, while a deterministic lower bound on every block prevents the rest of the series from cancelling them.
  We obtain a mean-zero $f\in\bigcap_{1\le q<\infty}L^q(\mathbb T)$ and a sequence $n_j=2^{m_j}$ with $n_{j+1}/n_j\ge2$ such that $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log N)^{-1/2}$ and $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)=+\infty$ for almost every $x$. This answers negatively a question of Erd\H{o}s on whether the condition $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log\log N)^{-C}$ suffices for almost-everywhere convergence, and shows that Matsuyama's condition $\|f-S_Nf\|_2\ll(\log\log N)^{-c}$, $c>1/2$, cannot be relaxed to $c=1/2$. A second choice of parameters gives, for every $2\le p<\infty$, functions $f\in L^p(\mathbb T)$ with $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\sum_{j\le N}f(n_jx)/(N(\log N)^{1/p-\varepsilon})=+\infty$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, almost everywhere. This is sharp up to $\varepsilon$, and the case $p=2$ answers negatively a second question of Erd\H{o}s. Finally, a bounded variant in the spirit of Marstrand's disproof of Khintchine's conjecture gives sets of arbitrarily small measure whose lacunary visiting frequencies have limsup $1$ almost everywhere.

papers.title: Minimizers for the Cahn-Hilliard energy functional with the Flory-Huggins potential under strong anchoring conditions
papers.authors: Shibin Dai, Abba Ramadan, Natasha Sharma
papers.abstract: In this paper, we theoretically and numerically study the minimizers for the Cahn-Hilliard energy with the Flory-Huggins potential under the strong anchoring condition, i.e., the Dirichlet boundary condition. We reveal bifurcation phenomena mediated by the boundary condition, the transition layer thickness, and the temperature of the system. Numerical simulations are also presented to approximate the minimizers of this energy by solving a gradient-flow equation, namely the Allen-Cahn equation constrained with strong anchoring conditions and random initial data. The effects of varying the transition layer thickness and temperature are presented to confirm the theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Correctness of Biot's model of in situ leaching for incompressible liquid and compressible solid components
papers.abstract: We study a mathematical model of in situ leaching of rare metals, in which the joint filtration of two liquids is governed by the microscopic model $\mathbb{A}^{\varepsilon}$. A key difficulty is the unknown (free) boundary $\Gamma(r)$ between solid and liquid components, determined by an additional condition on $\Gamma(r)$; no standard methods exist for this nonlinear problem. To resolve it, we apply the fixed point theorem. For a given function $r(\boldsymbol{x},t)$ from a set $\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}$ of sufficiently smooth functions describing the skeleton structure, we consider the auxiliary problem $\mathbb{B}^{\varepsilon}(r)$: an elliptic system for displacements of the liquid and solid components coupled with parabolic equations for the acid concentration. Selecting the weak solution of minimal smoothness, we apply the homogenization method to pass from the microscopic to the macroscopic description. The resulting macroscopic model $\mathbb{H}(r)$ contains a homogenized boundary condition that expresses the normal boundary velocity $V_{N}=\partial r/\partial t$ as a linear function of the acid concentration $c$. Since $c$ depends on $r$ via an operator $\mathbb{F}\colon\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}\to\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}$, we prove that $\mathbb{F}$ is Lipschitz continuous and, by Banach's theorem, possesses a unique fixed point $r^{*}$, which yields the unique solution $\mathbb{H}=\mathbb{H}(r^{*})$.

papers.title: Semi-discrete approximation of Ma\~n\'e, Aubry and Mather sets
papers.abstract:
We study a variational discretization in time of Aubry--Mather theory for
  Tonelli Lagrangians on the flat torus. We define discrete Ma\~n\'e, Aubry
  and Mather sets, establish their compactness and inclusion properties,
  and investigate their convergence as the time step tends to zero.
  We prove upper-limit results for the Ma\~n\'e sets and, when the continuous
  Aubry set has finitely many static classes, for the Aubry sets. We obtain
  full Kuratowski and Hausdorff convergence of the Aubry sets when this
  set is a single equilibrium or periodic orbit, and, under additional
  assumptions, a finite union of equilibria. Every weak limit of discrete
  Mather measures is a continuous Mather measure. For equilibrium Aubry
  sets, we give sufficient conditions for exact preservation of
  Mather sets and measure families at small time steps. A mechanical
  example illustrates these results and exhibits exact preservation
  of the Aubry set as well.

papers.title: Spanning Subdivisions in Robustly Expanding Digraphs
papers.authors: Zhilan Wang, Shuo Wei, Jin Yan
papers.abstract: K\"uhn, Osthus and Treglown [\emph{J. Combin. Theory Ser. B} \textbf{100} (2010)] proved that every sufficiently large robust outexpander with linear minimum semi-degree contains a Hamilton cycle. In this paper, we extend their result to spanning subdivisions of a digraph $F$ in a robust outexpander $D$, with prescribed branch vertices and arbitrarily specified path lengths. In particular, the digraph $F$ need not be fixed. For an $n$-vertex digraph $D$, $F$ may have as many as a constant multiple of $n/\log n$ arcs. This holds provided that $F$ has sufficiently few vertices and the prescribed lengths satisfy suitable conditions. We further establish a more general result for mixed prescribed path lengths, which allows $F$ to have linearly many arcs when the shorter replacement paths together use only a small proportion of the vertices of $D$. As applications, we obtain spanning subdivision extensions of the asymptotic Nash--Williams theorem for digraphs and an asymptotically sharp Ore-type theorem for oriented graphs.

papers.title: Stack Constructions and Equality Cases for Laffey's Bound for Maximal Commutative Matrix Algebras
papers.abstract:
We study equality cases in Laffey's lower bound for local maximal commutative subalgebras of matrix algebras with cube-zero radical.
  We introduce a stacking operation that combines algebras with common outer Loewy layers while preserving maximal commutativity. This yields standard equality bricks $B_{a,c}=(a,ac+1,c;a+c)$ for all $a,c\ge2$ and reduces further constructions to smaller building blocks.
  We establish the existence of all minimal equality bricks on the balanced branch and obtain sharp realizations throughout the $(4,5)$-sector. We also construct the first nontrivial nearly balanced root over arbitrary fields.
  We determine the balanced--nearly-balanced envelope of the numerical Laffey profile and give an arithmetic criterion for preservation of sharpness under stacking. As a consequence, the profile is attained in every matrix dimension $14\le n\le52$ and $93\le n\le114$, as well as along five infinite families over arbitrary fields.
  The main existence and interval results are proved in characteristic zero; the field-independent constructions are stated explicitly.

papers.title: Stochastic Riccati equations with jumps for indefinite linear-quadratic control: A stochastic value-flow approach
papers.authors: Kai Ding, Jiaqiang Wen, Jie Xiong, Xin Zhang
papers.abstract: This paper studies the nonlinear matrix-valued stochastic Riccati equation with jumps (SRE-J) arising from indefinite stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with random coefficients and Poisson jumps. We demonstrate that the presence of jumps may cause the matrix-valued optimal state process $\mathbf{X}$ to become singular, even under the standard condition. Consequently, the classical representation $P=\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{X}^{-1}$ used in the diffusion case is generally unavailable. To overcome this difficulty, we construct the Riccati process directly from the stochastic value flow under the uniform convexity condition on the cost functional, an approach that requires no invertibility condition on the jump coefficient. We then prove that the SRE-J admits a maximal strongly regular solution, which yields a closed-loop representation of the unique open-loop optimal control. Furthermore, we establish verifiable sufficient conditions for uniform convexity and provide examples of indefinite stochastic linear-quadratic problems with jumps.

papers.title: Classification of Double Saddle-Point Systems
papers.abstract: We offer a classification of a broad and practically relevant class of symmetric double saddle-point system. At the core of the paper is the division of the associated matrices into ``block-arrow'' and ``block-tridiagonal'' forms. We describe relevant applications, invertibility conditions, spectral properties, and block preconditioners. Our discussion is kept within a general framework rather than tailored to specific applications.

papers.title: A $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebraic Hoffman-Wielandt theorem
papers.abstract: We observe that the $2$-norm distance $d_{U,2}$ between the unitary orbits of normal elements in a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $\mathcal{M}$ is equal to the $2$-Wasserstein distance between the spectral measures induced by the trace $\tau_\mathcal{M}$. Using classification and optimal transport theory, we deduce an analogous $2$-norm equation for normal operators $x$ and $y$ in simple, separable, unital, nuclear, $\mathcal{Z}$-stable $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebras that are either monotracial, or real rank zero with finitely many extremal traces, provided that $\sigma(x)=\sigma(y)$ is convex. Consequently, $d_{U,2}$ equips the set of approximate unitary equivalence classes of contractive normal elements of $\mathcal{M}$ with the structure of a compact length space. The same is true of the set of equivalence classes of embeddings into the Jiang-Su algebra $\mathcal{Z}$ of classifiable tracial $2$-Wasserstein spaces over compact, convex planar domains.

papers.title: A unified approach to Penner, Ptolemy, and Casey's theorems in several dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove Penner's theorem on horocycles and theorems of Ptolemy and Casey, all with full converses, in hyperbolic space of several dimensions. Recently Waddle observed that the equations underpinning these three theorems are related, and it is this viewpoint that we advance, using the Lorentzian model of hyperbolic space. We show that all three theorems can be derived from a common Gram-matrix calculation applied to lightlike, timelike, and spacelike vectors. Remarkably, our approach gives a version of Casey's theorem in the plane with a full converse, involving three geometric alternatives, which to our knowledge has not previously been recorded.

papers.title: Amply regular graphs with $\mu$ close to half the valency and group divisible designs
papers.authors: Wei Jin, Jack H. Koolen, Chenhui Lv
papers.abstract: In this paper, we classify connected amply regular graphs with diameter $d \geq 4$ and parameters $(v, k, \lambda, \mu)$ satisfying $\mu = \frac{k-1}{2}$, where $k\geq 5$ is odd. We prove that such a graph must be exactly one of the following: the $5$-cube, the graph $\K_2 \square \Lambda$, where $\Lambda$ is the unique bipartite $(0,2)$-graph on $14$ vertices, or the point--block incidence graph of a group divisible design with the dual property, namely a $GDDDP\left(2, k+1;\, k;\, 0, \frac{k-1}{2}\right)$. For the last family, we give equivalent characterizations in terms of bipartite $Q$-regular graphs and relation graphs of symmetric association schemes with five classes. Furthermore, we present constructions of such amply regular graphs, yielding infinite families of examples derived from Paley graphs, Peisert graphs, and Paley digraphs.

papers.title: A path-following framework on fiber bundle for variational inequalities
papers.abstract: Developing general-purpose algorithms with global asymptotic convergence guarantees for variational inequalities (VIs) remains a longstanding challenge. This paper proposes a path-following framework for finite-dimensional VIs with arbitrary continuous mappings and polytope domains. The approach first transforms a general VI into a smooth VI on a simplex. Its key innovation is to formulate the resulting problem on a fiber bundle, called the fixed-point bundle, whose geometric structure enables the systematic integration of initialization, path-following, and singularity avoidance. Without imposing monotonicity or similar assumptions, the framework guarantees global linear convergence for nonsingular solutions and global linear convergence up to any prescribed precision for singular solutions. In numerical experiments, the algorithm attained a precision of $10^{-5}$ on all 6400 randomly generated instances, with dimensions up to 1024. Code and data are available at https://github.com/shb20tsinghua/FiberBundle_VI.

papers.title: Bounds on the F-Pure Threshold of Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: We obtain bounds for the $F$-pure threshold of isolated hypersurface singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic $p$ in terms of classical singularity invariants. For an irreducible plane curve whose value semigroup has first two generators $\beta_0,\beta_1$, we show that the $F$-pure threshold is at most $\frac{1}{\beta_0}+\frac{1}{\beta_1}$ and differs from it by less than $\frac{1}{\gcd(\beta_0,\beta_1)p}$, with equality when certain base-$p$ digits add without carrying, and we give an example showing that higher weighted-order terms can change the $F$-pure threshold. We also conjecture a lower bound in terms of the Milnor number, and prove it for semi-quasi-homogeneous singularities, for all plane curves, and whenever the number of variables exceeds $p$. In particular, it holds in characteristic $2$. As applications, we reprove Igusa's formula for the log canonical threshold of a complex plane branch (with integer coefficients), prove the conjecture of Musta\c{t}\u{a}, Takagi and Watanabe for such branches, and bound the log canonical threshold of complex isolated hypersurface singularities.

papers.title: The computable functional calculus
papers.authors: Christopher J. Eagle, Timothy H. McNicholl
papers.abstract: We show that the continuous functional calculus is computable. As consequences we obtain the computable compactness of the spectrum of any computable normal element of a computably presented $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra, the existence of effective approximate units for computably presented $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebras, and an effective version of the Spectral Theorem for compact operators on separable Hilbert spaces.

papers.title: The Size of the Intersection of $q$-ary Hamming Balls
papers.authors: Ville Junnila, Tero Laihonen, Tuomo Lehtil\"a, Pavan Padavu Devaraj
papers.abstract: The interest in studying the size of the intersection of multiple $q$-ary Hamming balls has grown due to the recent advances in DNA-based data storage systems. We present an exact formula for the cardinality of the intersection of $s$ Hamming balls of varying radii over a $q$-ary alphabet. It is known that the distances between the center points of the Hamming balls are not enough, in general, to determine the size of the intersection. Based on our formula, we are able to find more refined structural properties of the center points for determining the exact size of the intersection. Moreover, we also analyze the size of the intersection of Hamming balls with equal radii $t$ for sufficiently large $n$ when $t$ and $q$ are constants. When $s=3$, we give the necessary and sufficient conditions (for all $q\ge 2$, $q\neq 6$ and sufficiently large $n$) to obtain the maximum size of the intersection when the centers of the Hamming balls have a given minimum distance and demonstrate how to compute it using our general formula.

papers.title: Compensated Splitting For Generalized Lyapunov Equations
papers.abstract: The generalized Lyapunov equation has a natural splitting that leads to the standard fixed-point iteration (sFPI) for its numerical solution. sFPI is convergent, for an arbitrarily given initial guess, if and only if the spectral radius of the associated linear operator is smaller than $1$. This means that sFPI may diverge if the spectral radius is $1$ or bigger. In this paper, we propose a compensated splitting scheme that aims to reduce the spectral radius so that the resulting compensated fixed-point iteration (cFPI) has a better convergence property, namely, cFPI may still converge even if sFPI does not or cFPI converges faster than sFPI does when the latter is also convergent. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the superiority of cFPI to sFPI.

papers.title: Symmetry Breaking and Moduli for Ancient Yamabe Flows on the Sphere
papers.authors: Haixia Chen, Seunghyeok Kim, Monica Musso
papers.abstract: For every $n\ge3$, we construct compact Type II ancient Yamabe flows in the round conformal class of the unit $n$-sphere $\Ss^n$. After stereographic projection and rescaling of time and conformal factor, the solutions are asymptotic backward in time to finite superpositions of Aubin--Talenti bubbles with mutually comparable scales. For integers $h\ge1$ and $k\ge2$, the limiting centers form $h$ coaxial regular $k$-gons; when $h\ge2$, their distinct layer heights may be prescribed arbitrarily in the interval $(-1,1)$. If $hk\ge3$, the resulting flows are not geometrically equivalent to any rotationally symmetric ancient flow. For each flow, there is a fixed point of $\Ss^n$ at which the Ricci tensor has both positive and negative eigenvalues on every time slice. The corresponding volume-normalized Yamabe flows are also ancient. After rescaling each time slice to a fixed volume, the metrics converge to a wedge of $hk$ isometric round $n$-spheres in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology, as time tends to $-\infty$. For fixed $h,k\ge2$, the concentration configurations admit an explicit $(h-1)$-parameter description up to M\"obius transformations. Consequently, the construction yields geometrically inequivalent flows indexed by a nonempty open subset of $\R^{h-1}$, all with the same fixed-volume backward Gromov--Hausdorff limit. The proof uses inner--outer gluing for the quasilinear parabolic equation in $n$-dimensional space that exhibits Kelvin symmetry. Weighted Euclidean and spherical H\"older estimates control the nonlinear terms and, together with parabolic regularity, yield smooth extension of the conformal metrics across the north pole of $\Ss^n$.

papers.title: The contrast between real and $p$-adic integrability
papers.abstract: A fundamental question in $p$-adic symplectic geometry and $p$-adic Hamiltonian mechanics is to what extent we can learn new information about integrable systems with coefficients in the rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$, if we view them as $p$-adic systems instead of real ones. We combine geometric analytic estimates with Galois theory in order to show that at a local level, these real and $p$-adic viewpoints give completely different information. Then we focus on understanding this local behavior for the $p$-adic case by proving effective methods to compute local normal forms. Our results are motivated by a program outlined by Pelayo-Voevodsky-Warren a decade ago, to develop a $p$-adic theory of integrable systems and symplectic geometry.

papers.title: Hilbert transforms on graph products of finite von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: We study Hilbert transforms on graph products of finite von Neumann algebras, with particular interest in their boundedness on the associated noncommutative $L_p$-spaces for $1<p<\infty$. We establish a generalized Cotlar identity for Hilbert transforms, valid on operators whose lengths exceed a constant depending only on the underlying graph. We further prove that graph products of finite von Neumann algebras satisfying a Haagerup-type inequality admit $L_p$-bounded Hilbert transforms, therefore extending the corresponding result of Mei and Ricard for free products of finite von Neumann algebras. In addition, we obtain several equivalent characterizations of this Haagerup-type inequality. Our results apply, in particular, to graph products of finite groups, right-angled Hecke von Neumann algebras, and graph products of finite quantum groups. As an application, we provide a complete characterization of a compactness problem posed by Ozawa for graph products of finite groups and right-angled Hecke von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Weighted $H^p-L^q$ boundedness of integral operators with rough kernels
papers.authors: Andrea L. Gallo, M. Silvina Riveros, Lucas A. Vallejos
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study integral operators \begin{equation*} T_\alpha f(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}K(x,y) f(y)dy, \end{equation*} with kernels $K(x,y)= k_1( x- A_1y)...k_m( x-A_my),$ where $k_i(x)=\frac{\Omega_i(x)}{|x|^{n/q_i}}$ and $\Omega_i: \mathbb{R}^n\to \mathbb{R}$ are homogeneous functions of degree zero, satisfying a size and a Dini condition, $A_{i}$ are certain invertible matrices, and $\frac n{q_1}+\dots+\frac n{q_m}=n-\alpha,$ $0\leq \alpha <n.$ We obtain the $H^{p}_{w^p}(\mathbb{R}^{n})-L^{q}_{w^q}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ boundedness of these operators, for a class of Muckenhoupt weights $w$, satisfying the condition \begin{equation*} w(A_ix)\leq cw(x), \end{equation*} $a.e.x\in\mathbb{R} ^n $, $1\leq i\leq m$.

papers.title: Dissipativity properties of a class of nonlinear time-delay systems via Bessel-Legendre inequalities
papers.abstract: Time delays are inherent in many physical and engineered systems and can significantly affect their stability and performance. In this work, we investigate the dissipativity of a class of nonlinear time-delay systems with multiple discrete delays and derive sufficient conditions for both delay-dependent and delay-independent dissipativity using Bessel-Legendre inequalities. For linear systems, the resulting dissipativity conditions are expressed in terms of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) which can be solved numerically to obtain Lyapunov-Krasovskii-type storage functions.

papers.title: Classification of Smooth Minimal K\"ahler Fourfolds Without Effective Divisors and Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove the following two statements: (1) If $X$ is a compact K\"ahler fourfold with pseudo-effective canonical bundle and no subvarieties of codimension one or two, then $K_X$ is a torsion line bundle; (2) If $X$ is a compact K\"ahler fourfold with no subvarieties of codimension one or two, then $X$ is not uniruled. Using the Beauville-Bogomolov decomposition and a characterization of Uniruled manifolds by Wenhao Ou, we get that if $X$ is a compact K\"ahler fourfold with no subvarieties of codimension one or two, then either $X$ is a torus or an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold.

papers.title: Limit theorems for supercritical branching processes in Markovian environment with linear fractional offspring distributions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behaviour for distribution of supercritical branching process in a Markovian environment with linear fractional offspring distributions. Phase transitions in the behaviour of the process is discovered, through investigating the strongly, intermediately and weakly supercritical cases.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Transitive permutation groups with trivial four point stabilizers"
papers.authors: Paula H\"ahndel, Christoph M\"oller, Rebecca Waldecker
papers.abstract: This article revisits earlier work by the last author together with Kay Magaard. We correct mistakes in results about the Sylow 2- and 3-structure of groups that act with fixity 3 and one result about possible components, we improve some results and we add details.

papers.title: Stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of PDEs with Burgers-type nonlinearity
papers.abstract: Master--slave synchronization reconstructs the evolving state of a reference (or master) system by continuously correcting a second system, the slave, using observations of the master. In applications, the observations are often contaminated by noise, so the corrections injected into the slave are themselves uncertain. In this paper we aim at quantifying the effect of noisy observations on master--slave synchronization for a family of evolution equations that combine a quadratic transport term with a polynomial linear differential operator. The family includes the Burgers, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, Kawahara, Benney--Lin and Nikolaevskiy equations, among others. Under periodic boundary conditions, a Fourier--Galerkin approximation of order $K$ yields a finite-dimensional master--slave system in which white observation noise of intensity $\sigma$ is modeled through an It\^o stochastic differential equation. In this framework, we first establish local exponential stability of noiseless synchronization for sufficiently strong scalar coupling. Then we compare the stochastic synchronization error with its noiseless counterpart resulting from the same initial slave state, isolating in this way the effect of noise. Assuming bounded reference paths, the mean-square deviation between the noiseless and noisy synchronization errors is $\mathcal O(\sigma^2)$ on finite time intervals. Under additional regularity assumptions, we also bound the error between the finite-resolution stochastic slave model and the infinite-dimensional deterministic master field, explicitly separating spectral approximation error, deterministic synchronization error and observation noise. Numerical experiments for the Kawahara and Nikolaevskiy equations confirm the predicted noise scaling.

papers.title: Characterization of the boundedness of the segment multiplier on rearrangement-invariant spaces
papers.authors: Miguel F. Barea-Fern\'andez, Ron Kerman, Jan Lang, Javier Soria
papers.abstract: Given rearrangement-invariant (r.i.) spaces $X$ and $Y$, we show that the segment multiplier, the truncated Hilbert transform, and the discrete Hilbert transform (on the associated discretized space) are bounded from $X$ to $Y$ simultaneously. Moreover, when $X = Y$ this boundedness is characterized by a condition on a pair of Boyd-type indices. We also exhibit an r.i. space on which the segment multiplier is bounded while the (non-truncated) Hilbert transform fails to be bounded.

papers.title: Sharp Error Estimates for a Fully Discrete Approximation of Semilinear Stochastic Convection--Diffusion Equations with Additive Noise and Nonsmooth Initial Data
papers.authors: Jitendra Nath Naik, Lok Pati Tripathi
papers.abstract: We establish sharp strong error estimates for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear stochastic convection--diffusion equations driven by additive noise subject to nonsmooth initial data. The problem is discretized in space using a standard Galerkin finite element method and in time via the linearly implicit Euler scheme. By decoupling the noise regularity index $\beta \in (0, 2]$ from the initial data regularity index $\mu \in (0, 2]$, we derive time-weighted spatial and temporal regularity bounds that isolate the initial singularity at $t = 0$ into an integrable temporal weight. By allowing the drift operator $F$ to map into negative-order fractional spaces to incorporate the convection term, we prove sharp strong convergence rates of order $O(h^\beta + k^{\beta/2})$ for $\beta \in (0, 2)$ and $O\bigl(h^2 + k(1+\ln(t_n/k))^{1/2}\bigr)$ at the critical endpoint $\beta = 2$ for any fixed $t_n > 0$, without requiring the regularity of the initial data to match that of the noise. Furthermore, these convergence rates are achieved under a relaxed differentiability condition requiring only a Lipschitz continuous first G\^ateaux derivative of $F$. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results across both trace-class and space-time white noise regimes.

papers.title: Spherical Completeness, Coherence, and GCD Properties of Formal Power Series and Witt Vector Rings
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a complete nonarchimedean valued field with $v(K^\times)=\mathbf R$, and let $V=\mathcal O_K$. We prove that $K$ is spherically complete if and only if $V[[T]]$ is coherent, and that this is also equivalent to $V[[T]]$ being a GCD domain. If $K$ is perfect of characteristic $p$, the same characterization holds for the Witt vector ring $W(V)$. Thus, this settles the previously unresolved full-real-value-group case in the coherence problems for both formal power series and Witt vector rings. In particular, this result also gives affirmative answers to Questions~9 and~10 of Anderson--Kang--Park. The proof combines a coherence criterion for complete rings with a spherically complete valuation quotient and a uniform construction of non-finitely generated intersections of two principal ideals from an empty ball chain.

papers.title: On Sun's Conjectures for Truncated Jacobi-Symbol Determinants via Supersingular Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We study the truncated Jacobi-symbol determinants $$\{c,d\}_n=\det\!\left[\left(\frac{j^2+cjk+dk^2}{n}\right)\right]_{2\le j,k\le n-2}$$ proposed by Zhi-Wei Sun in \cite{ZWSun} and prove Conjectures 5.1(i), 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6(i), 5.7, 5.8, a case of 5.6(ii) of \cite{ZWSun}, Conjecture 4.8(i) of \cite{Sun2019} and some strengthened forms. All results follow from a single unified approach: for a prime $p$, we diagonalize the nonzero-residue matrix indexed by $\mathbb{F}_p^\times$ and reduce the vanishing of determinants to the supersingular reduction of certain CM elliptic curves. The same framework extends naturally to further families of parameters, suggesting a general mechanism behind identities of this type.

papers.title: Adaptive Schauder Stochastic Mirror Descent in Banach Spaces
papers.authors: Jinhui Bai, Shuai Lu, Lei Shi
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce an adaptive regularization strategy for stochastic mirror descent (SMD) to solve a class of risk functional minimization problems in infinite-dimensional Banach spaces. Using a Schauder basis, we construct nested finite-dimensional subspaces whose dimensions adapt to the sample size $n$ and balance approximation and optimization errors. We restrict each SMD subproblem to the corresponding subspace and project the stochastic gradient onto its dual space. This yields closed form solutions and coordinate-wise coefficient updates with low computational and storage complexity. For risk minimization in $\mathcal{L}^p$ spaces with $1<p<\infty$, we construct Bregman distances adapted to the underlying Banach space geometry using $\max\{2,p\}$-convex functionals induced by uniform convexity. At the $\mathcal{L}^1$ endpoint, we instead construct a locally strongly convex functional based on the entropy function. By developing a new analytical framework, we establish a convergence rate of $\mathcal O\left(n^{-\min\{\frac12,\frac1p\}}\right)$, up to logarithmic factors. In the misspecified setting, we prove convergence of the risk to its minimum under weaker regularity assumptions and derive explicit polynomial rates when the regularity exceeds a specified threshold. Finally, we apply the method to statistical inverse problems and illustrate its empirical performance through numerical experiments in both settings.

papers.title: Optimizing bounds for energy-constrained optimal cooling problems in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We study optimal control problems for incompressible fluids in two-dimensional domains with a cold boundary and internal heat sources and sinks. Given a kinetic energy budget, measured by the square of a nondimensional P\'eclet number $\mathrm{Pe}$, the goal is to maximize a cooling efficiency inversely proportional to the mean square gradient of the fluid's temperature. Using Lagrange duality, we formulate a well-posed dual problem whose solution yields an upper bound on the maximum cooling efficiency $\mathcal{E}(\mathrm{Pe})$. We then numerically approximate the dual problem using a convergent hierarchy of semidefinite programs obtained via discretization. We illustrate this computational approach on optimal cooling problems in a square and in an annulus, explaining also how problem symmetries can be exploited to reduce computational complexity. Finally, we construct admissible points for the dual problem to obtain new analytical upper bounds on the optimal cooling efficiency $\mathcal{E}(\mathrm{Pe})$. Specifically, we prove that $\mathcal{E}(\mathrm{Pe}) \lesssim \mathrm{Pe}^{2}$ for arbitrary domains and heat distributions, and that $\mathcal{E}(\mathrm{Pe}) \lesssim \mathrm{Pe}^{2}/ \ln^2\mathrm{Pe}$ for cooling flows in disks and annuli with heat source/sink distributions with a uniformly positive azimuthal average. These results generalize and improve known efficiency bounds for energy-constrained cooling flows in a disk.

papers.title: Commutative coherent rings with $\mathcal{GP}\not\subseteq\mathcal{GF}$
papers.abstract: For every field $k$, we construct a commutative coherent $k$-algebra admitting a Gorenstein projective module that is not Gorenstein flat.

papers.title: Near-optimal Tur\'an densities of $r$-graphs on $r+1$ vertices
Height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves
papers.abstract: We introduce families of Lagrange functions associated with height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves. We show that degeneracies of these families characterize geometric properties of the curves, such as inflections and vertices, and give geometric interpretations of the corresponding Lagrange multipliers in terms of contact with lines and circles.

papers.title: Broadcast Domination Number is at Most Twice the Multipacking Number
papers.abstract:
For a graph $ G = (V, E) $ with a vertex set $ V $ and an edge set $ E $, a function $ f : V \rightarrow \{0, 1, 2, . . . , diam(G)\} $ is called a \emph{broadcast} on $ G $. For each vertex $ u \in V $, if there exists a vertex $ v $ in $ G $ (possibly, $ u = v $) such that $ f (v) > 0 $ and $ d(u, v) \leq f (v) $, then $ f $ is called a dominating broadcast on $ G $. The cost of the dominating broadcast $f$ is the quantity $ \sum_{v\in V}f(v) $. The minimum cost of a dominating broadcast is the broadcast domination number of $G$, denoted by $ \gamma_{b}(G) $.
  A multipacking is a set $ M \subseteq V $ in a graph $ G = (V, E) $ such that for every vertex $ v \in V $ and for every integer $ r \geq 1 $, the ball of radius $ r $ around $ v $ contains at most $ r $ vertices of $ M $, that is, there are at most $ r $ vertices in $ M $ at a distance at most $ r $ from $ v $ in $ G $. The multipacking number of $ G $ is the maximum cardinality of a multipacking of $ G $ and is denoted by $ mp(G) $.
  It is known that $mp(G)\leq\gamma_b(G)$. In 2014, Hartnell and Mynhardt proved that $\gamma_b(G)\leq 3mp(G)-2$ whenever $mp(G)\geq2$. In 2019, Beaudou, Brewster, and Foucaud improved this bound to $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)+3$ and conjectured that $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)$. We solve their conjecture by proving that $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)$ for every graph $G$. Our proof is constructive and yields a linear-time $2$-approximation algorithm for Maximum Multipacking problem which improves the earlier approximation factor $2+o(1)$.
