papers.title: A Method of Construction of Pairwise Additive Balanced Incomplete Block Designs
papers.abstract: The existence of sets of balanced incomplete block (BIB) designs with pairwise additivity, called pairwise additive BIB designs, has been studied through direct and recursive constructions in the literature. This paper presents a new method of constructing such designs from affine resolvable semi-regular group divisible (ARSRGD) designs. Since many known ARSRGD designs are obtained from generalized Hadamard matrices, we also describe the corresponding construction of pairwise additive BIB designs from generalized Hadamard matrices. Using the construction together with known existence results for generalized Hadamard matrices, we obtain several new infinite series of pairwise additive BIB designs, including designs with parameter sets whose existence was previously unknown.

papers.title: Extremal problems for suspensions of even cycles
papers.abstract:
Given an integer $k\geq2$ and a graph $F$, the $k$-uniform suspension $\mathcal{S}^kF$ is obtained by adjoining a fixed set of $k-2$ new vertices to every edge of $F$. In this paper, we study two extremal problems for suspensions of even cycles.
  Write $K^k_t$ for the $k$-uniform clique of order $t$. Let $\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})$ and $\mathrm{ex}(n,K^k_t,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})$ denote the maximum numbers of edges and copies of $K^k_t$, respectively, in an $\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell}$-free $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. We prove that, for every $k\geq2$ and infinitely many $n$, \[\mathrm{ex}(n,K^{k}_{k+1},\mathcal{S}^kC_4)=\frac{n^{k-1/2}}{(k+1)!}+O(n^{k-1}).\] This extends a folklore result for $k=2$ and, as an immediate consequence, yields the asymptotics of $\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_4)$ for infinitely many $n$, previously established by Mubayi (for all $n$).
  Furthermore, for every $k\geq2$ and $\ell\in\{3,5\}$, we determine the order of magnitude \[\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})=\Theta(n^{k-1+1/\ell}).\] This generalizes both the classical graph case $k=2$ and a previous result of Mukherjee for $k=\ell=3$.
  The principal difficulty in both problems lies in constructing the lower bounds. Our construction for $\mathrm{ex}(n,K^{k}_{k+1},\mathcal{S}^kC_4)$ incorporates a novel block-packing structure, which yields substantially more copies of $K^k_{k+1}$ than previously known constructions. For $\mathrm{ex}(n,\mathcal{S}^kC_{2\ell})$ with $\ell\in\{3,5\}$, we establish a natural $k$-uniform version of Wenger graphs, addressing the subtleties involved in lifting extremal graph constructions to suspensions. We also give applications of our results to Tur\'an problems for simplicial complexes.

papers.title: The universal measure of nonstochastic objects
papers.abstract: The usual settings for discussing the notion of stochastic objects are very different from Kolmogorov's original structure-free setting, in which there is no predefined external structure on the objects (such as the lengths of binary strings). A natural modification of stochasticity, obtained by replacing finite sets as models with probability measures, is quasi-stochasticity. The structure-free setting is common in studies of quasi-stochasticity, and known results show that the universal machine generates non-quasi-stochastic objects with exponentially small probability. This paper shows that, on the other hand, the universal machine generates nonstochastic objects surprisingly often. It also systematically explores numerous connections between stochasticity and quasi-stochasticity in the structure-free setting. In particular, the definition of quasi-stochasticity can be modified in a natural way modelled on Kolmogorov's definition so that non-quasi-stochastic objects are produced as often as nonstochastic ones; the results for this modification imply all the results of this paper showing that nonstochastic objects are frequent.

papers.title: Discrete Approximation to Time-changed Brownian Motions
papers.abstract: We develop a general discrete approximation scheme for time-changed Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Our approximation scheme works for any smooth measure with full quasi-support on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with suitable initial distributions. Under some mild conditions on the smooth measure, the discrete approximation scheme works for every starting point. Our results in particular give a discrete approximation scheme for Liouville Brownian motions.

papers.title: A Topological Figiel-Lindenstrauss-Milman Theorem and its Applications
papers.authors: Florian Frick, Kaave Hosseini, Eric Myzelev, Arya Narnapatti, Aliaksei Vasileuski
papers.abstract:
We prove a topological generalization of the Figiel--Lindenstrauss--Milman inequality, answering a recent question of Frick, Hosseini, and Vasileuski: every nonempty strongly regular CW complex with $v$ vertices, $f$ maximal cells, and a free involution that permutes its cells has $\mathbb Z/2$-index at most $4\log v\log f$. The classical inequality for centrally symmetric polytopes is the special case of polytope boundaries.
  As an application, we show that every finite simplicial complex homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb RP^d$ has at least $\exp(\Omega(\sqrt d))$ vertices. The previous best lower bound was $\Omega(d^2)$. We also construct triangulations with $\exp(O(\sqrt d))$ vertices. Using the same method, we prove a low-dimensional Postnikov factorization theorem, which gives similar vertex lower bounds for several classical families, such as complex and quaternionic projective spaces, the $d$-torus, closed symplectic and aspherical manifolds, Grassmannians, classical Lie groups, and spherical space forms. Further applications include results in learning theory, convex geometry, computational topology, and topological bounds for chromatic numbers and Vietoris--Rips complexes.

papers.title: Exact dimensionality of stationary measures for random diffeomorphisms with all Lyapunov exponents equal and negative
papers.abstract:
We prove exact dimensionality of ergodic stationary measures for random compositions of $C^1$ diffeomorphisms of a closed manifold $M$ that contract at a single Lyapunov scale. More precisely, let $
u$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathrm{Diff}^1(M)$ such that $\log\sup_{x}\|{D_xf}\|$ and $\log\sup_{x}\|{D_xf^{-1}}\|$ are $
u$-integrable, and let $\mu$ be an ergodic $
u$-stationary probability measure. If the top and bottom Lyapunov exponents of the derivative cocycle coincide and equal $\lambda<0$, then $\mu$ is exact dimensional and $\mathrm{dim}(\mu)=h_\mu^{\mathrm{F}}(
u)/(-\lambda)$, where $h_\mu^{\mathrm{F}}(
u)$ is the Furstenberg entropy.

papers.title: Second-order perturbation bounds for Gibbs samplers under strong spatial mixing
papers.authors: Na Lin, Aaron Smith, Yiqiang Q. Zhao
papers.abstract: The basic question in perturbation analysis of Markov chains is how small changes in their transition kernels affect their stationary distributions. Classical perturbation bounds typically require the kernel error to be much smaller than $1/\tau$, where $\tau$ is a mixing or relaxation time. Although this scaling is sharp for Markov chains in general, we investigate a general "square-rooting" phenomenon in which one-step errors of order roughly $1/\sqrt{\tau}$ can be sufficient for local updates. We proved a form of this phenomenon in Lin, Liu and Smith (2025) under strong assumptions. Here we substantially weaken these assumptions, and prove this phenomenon occurs using three distinct approaches. First, block factorization applies under structural assumptions on the stationary measures of both chains. Second, approximate block-update arguments extend the result to statistically relevant Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) settings, where structural guarantees are available for the exact posterior and its associated sampler, but not for the perturbed posterior. Third, we use direct calculations for a class of models with hard constraints where neither general result is directly available. We illustrate these results in three MCMC settings and show how they directly inform the tuning of approximate MCMC algorithms.

papers.title: Optimising Selberg's method for critical zeros
papers.abstract: We revisit Zhuravlev's 1974 quantitative form of Selberg's sign-change method for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line. Zhuravlev's work, originally in Russian and little known in the West, established an explicit positive proportion of such zeros. Using modern techniques we optimise the arithmetic mean value at the heart of the method and obtain the strongest result yet known from Selberg's method, proving that more than $6.78\%$ of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line.

papers.title: Boundary regularity of harmonic functions in $C^1$ slit domains
papers.authors: Joan Domingo-Pasarin, Pablo Hidalgo-Palencia, Alejandro Mart\'inez, Clara Torres-Latorre
papers.abstract:
We establish precise upper and lower estimates for harmonic functions vanishing on the slit of a $C^1$ slit domain, with no assumption that the slit lies in a hyperplane. The classical $\sqrt{d}$ growth near the edge, $d$ being the distance to the slit, persists in this generality, up to an explicit factor \[\exp\Big( \pm C \int_\rho^r \omega(s)\, \frac{ds}{s} \Big)\] determined by the $C^1$-modulus of continuity $\omega$ of the slit, where $\rho < r$ are the two scales being compared. The upper estimates allow a right-hand side and non-zero boundary data. The correction factors remain bounded above and below by positive constants as $\rho\to0$ precisely when $\omega$ satisfies the Dini condition. Moduli of continuity beyond the Dini regime, as is the case for the logarithmic moduli arising at singular sets in relevant free boundary problems, were not covered by the previous $C^{1,\alpha}$ theory.
  Previously, the $\sqrt{d}$ growth was known for slits contained in a hyperplane, which additionally have a $C^{1,\alpha}$ edge (De Silva, Savin). For Lipschitz slits, there are boundary Harnack principles, but no growth rate is identified precisely.
  The main technical ingredient is a change of coordinates flattening a Lipschitz slit domain onto the model half-hyperplane slit, with quantitative estimates up to second order. The construction is geometric and does not use the equation, so we expect it to be useful for other boundary regularity problems.

papers.title: The fixed-point bundle method over product-of-simplex domains arising from game equilibria
papers.abstract: Developing general-purpose algorithms with global asymptotic convergence guarantees for Nash equilibria of general-sum games remains a longstanding challenge. This paper extends the fixed-point bundle framework for finite-dimensional variational inequalities (VIs) from simplex domains to product-of-simplex domains, enabling its direct application to Nash equilibrium computation. The resulting fixed-point bundle exhibits a composite fiber bundle structure. The key innovation is to construct an equivalent VI on a simplex and establish the equivalence between the two fixed-point bundle frameworks via a fiber bundle isomorphism. Exploiting this geometric equivalence, we show that the path-following algorithm for VIs on product-of-simplex domains inherits the global linear convergence guarantees of the simplex-domain framework. In numerical experiments, the algorithm attained a precision of $10^{-5}$ on all 5600 randomly generated game instances, with dimension ranging from 2-player 128-action to 128-player 2-action. Code and data are available at https://github.com/shb20tsinghua/FiberBundle_VI.

papers.title: The BAR-SOT Method: Long-term Average Cost Control as Stochastic Optimal Self-Transport
papers.authors: Sharan Srinivasan, Berke M. Turkay, Harsha Honnappa
papers.abstract: We reformulate average-cost (ergodic) control of a Markov jump process as a finite-horizon stochastic optimal transport (SOT) problem that jointly optimizes over the controlled evolution and the marginal law from which it starts and returns to (i.e., a self-transport). The constraint relating the marginal flow to the controlled generator is the basic adjoint relationship (BAR), so we call the resulting problem BAR-SOT. For any time horizon T>0, its optimal value is a constant scaling of the long-run average-cost rate. We give three equivalent formulations (through controlled processes, a Fokker--Planck constraint, and relaxed marginal measures) and show that the optimal dual is a stationary potential plus a term linear in time, with slope equal to the rate. A relative-entropy penalty on the control yields a cost-tilted Schrodinger bridge problem, computable by a Sinkhorn-type iteration when every transition rate is controlled, whose value converges to the unregularized optimum as the penalty vanishes. We develop the theory for finite Markov decision processes and then for general controlled Markov jump processes. A neural parametrization of the dual, trained as a physics-informed neural network (PINN), that encodes Harrison's equivalent-workload formulation (see Harrison 2000) matches the strong reinforcement-learning baseline of Dai and Gluzman (2022); numerically conditioning the fit of a sub-dominant transverse correction then improves on both that baseline and the best priority heuristic. On the input-queued switch, a graph-attention parametrization of the dual improves on the strongest matching heuristic we are aware of, with a parameter count that does not grow with the switch size.

papers.title: Computing the entropy rate of a quantized stationary Gaussian process
papers.abstract: The entropy rate of a uniformly quantized stationary Gaussian process is the fundamental limit on its lossless compression. It has no closed form, and the classical high-resolution approximation breaks down whenever the spectral density is small on part of the band, as routine smoothing and filtering produce. Here we present two methods for computing the rate. The first is an analytical approximation, obtained from an exact dithering identity and the Kolmogorov-Szeg\H{o} formula, in which the quantization noise power acts as a floor on the spectral density. The second is a Monte Carlo estimate of the exact rate: a minimum-phase moving-average representation makes the quantized sequence a hidden Markov process whose optimal particle filter is available in closed form, and the filter's log-likelihood on one long sequence gives the rate. The approximation agrees with the estimate to within a few millibits per sample over most of the parameter range for quantization steps up to the signal standard deviation, including processes on which the classical formula fails; for coarser steps the estimate should be used instead. At a step of a quarter of the standard deviation, linear predictive coding comes within 2 to 4 percent of the rate, FLAC within 3 to 32 percent, and general-purpose compressors remain 12 to 89 percent above it.

papers.title: Adaptive Sparse-grid Discontinuous Galerkin Approximations to the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook Model
papers.authors: Stefan Schnake, Miroslav Stoyanov, Eirik Endeve, Cory Hauck
papers.abstract: This work studies adaptive sparse-grid discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations for the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) model, a kinetic equation posed in four- and six-dimensional phase-space. Standard DG methods are rendered impractical for the BGK model by the curse of dimensionality, motivating compressed representations that adapt to the solution in time. Using the adaptive sparse-grid DG method, we quantify accuracy and compression by comparing the adaptive degrees of freedom to full-grid DG methods and by assessing the resulting kinetic and fluid quantities in both fluid and rarefied regimes. Test cases include a relaxation problem, a multidimensional Sod shock tube, and shear/expansion flows used in prior low-rank BGK studies. To build an efficient Maxwellian evaluation without violating conservation, a central obstacle for structure-perserving BGK simulations, we introduce a hybrid interpolation strategy that exploits velocity separability to recover the correct discrete collision invariants and prove conservation of the resulting discrete collision operator on adaptive sparse grids. Our results show that the adaptive sparse-grid strategy can recover accurate and physically relevant solutions with sharp gradients, and the method reduces the active degrees of freedom by factors ranging from several-fold to several orders of magnitude, with the largest reductions occurring in the six-dimensional examples. All computations are performed with the open-source ASGarD adaptive sparse-grid DG library.

papers.title: Bounds of singular sets for elliptic equations in $C^{1, Dini}$ domains with singular potentials
papers.abstract: We study the quantitative codimension-two estimate for the singular set in the boundary neighborhoods of the solutions of \begin{equation*} \Delta u+V(x)u=0\qquad\text{in }\Omega, \qquad u=0\qquad\text{on }\partial\Omega, \end{equation*} where $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ is a bounded $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ domain and $V\in L^p(\Omega)$ for some $p>n$. We first prove the explicit upper bound for the doubling index is given by $C(n,p,\Omega)(1+\|V\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^{\frac{2p}{3p-2n}})$.The analytic input is an interior volume estimate for solutions of second order elliptic equations with uniformly elliptic Dini leading coefficients and $V\in L^p$. Using the quantitative doubling index bound, boundary flattening, we show an explicit upper bound for singular sets in the neighborhood of the boundary of the $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ domain.

papers.title: Conditional Stable Laws and Rare-Event Limits for Absorbing Markov Chains
papers.authors: Bernat Bassols Cornudella, Matheus M Castro
papers.abstract: We establish conditional limit theorems, pointwise in the initial state, for absorbing Markov chains on a compact metric space $M$. We assume $L^1(M,\rho)$-continuous transition densities, irreducibility and aperiodicity. For the observable $f_\beta(x)=d_M(x,x_0)^{-\beta}$, with suitable $x_0$ satisfying $\rho(B_r(x_0))\sim C_d(x_0)r^d$, we prove that the point-process of normalised observations converges to a Poisson random measure. This yields totally right-skewed $\alpha$-stable laws for $\alpha=d/\beta\in(0,2)$ and, at the boundary value $\alpha=2$, a Gaussian limit with the non-standard normalisation $\sqrt{n\log n}$. We also establish a conditional central limit theorem for $L^2$ observables, exponential deviation bounds for bounded observables and a conditional Poisson law for visits to shrinking targets. The results and remarks have been formalised in Lean~4.

papers.title: Two-disjoint-cycle-cover edge bipancyclicity in Cartesian products
papers.abstract:
For two even integers $r_1,r_2$ with $4\leq r_1\leq r_2\leq N/2$, a graph $G$ of even order $N\geq8$ is \emph{2-DCC edge $[r_1,r_2]$-bipancyclic} if for every ordered pair $(e,f)$ of independent edges and every even integer $\ell\in[r_1,r_2]$, there exist two vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1$ and $C_2$ with $V(C_1)\cup V(C_2)=V(G)$, $|C_1|=\ell$, $|C_2|=N-\ell$, $e\in E(C_1)$, and $f\in E(C_2)$.
  We study this property for graphs defined by Cartesian products. Let $G=H_1\square\cdots\square H_d$, where $d\geq2$ and each factor $H_i$ is either $K_2$ or a bipartite graph of even order at least four that has a Hamiltonian cycle and in which every edge lies on a Hamiltonian cycle.
  We prove that $G$ is 2-DCC edge $[4,|V(G)|/2]$-bipancyclic if one of the following holds: (i) $d\geq4$; (ii) $d=3$ and at least two factors have order at least four; (iii) $d=3$, exactly one factor has order at least four, and every set of at most two edges of that factor lies on a common Hamiltonian cycle; (iv) $d=2$, both factors have order at least four, and every set of at most two edges of each factor lies on a common Hamiltonian cycle; (v) $G\cong K_2\square K_2\square K_2$.
  The theorem applies to several families of interconnection networks. In this paper, we give a sharp characterization for undirected toroidal meshes, star-cube networks, and hyperstar networks.

papers.title: A solution to a conjecture on the norm of the Copson operator minus the Identity for monotone sequences
papers.abstract: We investigate the operator distance between the Identity and the Copson operator on the cone of nonnegative, nonincreasing sequences within the Lebesgue sequence spaces $\ell^p(\mathbb{N})$. By proving the exact value of this distance, we confirm a conjecture originally formulated by A. Ben Said, S. Boza, and J. Soria in ``The norm of Hardy-type oscillation operators in the discrete and continuous settings'' (\emph{Analysis and Applications}, 2025).

papers.title: The Fixed-$q$ Edge Limit of the $q$-Krawtchouk Ensemble
papers.abstract: We study the fixed-$q$ right-edge asymptotics of the ordinary $q$-Krawtchouk ensemble. For $0<q<1$, finite polynomial duality gives a direct proof of convergence of the correlation kernels to an explicit limiting kernel. The local Jacobi limit is a shifted continuous $q^{-1}$-Hermite expression with an indeterminate moment problem, so the limiting Jacobi expression does not determine a unique self-adjoint operator. A single spectral atom, asymptotically saturating the mass bound, selects the realization and yields strong-resolvent convergence. The limiting kernel represents its positive spectral projection and admits spectral-series, Christoffel--Darboux, and partial-theta representations. After a ground-state transformation, the associated dual operator agrees with a two-step spatial Markov operator of Borodin--Corwin. For $q>1$, the limiting Jacobi operator is of Al-Salam--Carlitz~I type and is essentially self-adjoint.

papers.title: Spherical and affine Artin groups, finite quotients, and the isomorphism problem
papers.authors: Sam Hughes, Thomas Ng, Kaitlin Ragosta, Nancy Scherich, Yvon Verberne
papers.abstract: We compute the smallest non-abelian quotients of spherical and affine Artin groups. Usually, these are isomorphic to the smallest non-abelian quotients of the corresponding Coxeter groups. As applications, we deduce that two affine Artin groups are isomorphic if and only if their Coxeter diagrams are isomorphic and that irreducible spherical Artin groups are distinguished from each other by their finite quotient groups.

papers.title: The para--Krawtchouk oscillator and its continuum limit
papers.authors: St\'ephane Z. Beaulac, Nicolas Cramp\'e, Quentin Labriet, Lucia Morey, Marlon Josue Rivera Valladares, Luc Vinet
papers.abstract: The para-Krawtchouk polynomials define, through their recurrence relation, a finite oscillator model that exhibits fractional revival. We determine the continuum limit of this Hamiltonian, both from its recurrence relation and directly on the polynomials. The limit is the singular (isotonic) oscillator $-\partial_\eta^2+\eta^2+\tfrac{\gamma^2-1}{4\eta^2}$. The deformation parameter $\gamma$ survives as a central impurity of the couplings, which decays as the inverse square of the distance. This is the marginal rate, which the continuum scaling turns into a finite $\sfrac{1}{\eta^2}$ term. Using the decomposition of the para-Krawtchouk polynomials into two Hahn families, we prove the confluence, for every degree, of the eigenvectors on the two sub-lattices to generalized Hermite functions. The bispectral pair of the discrete model, which generates the Hahn algebra, becomes in the limit a pair of generators of $\su$, the dynamical algebra of the singular oscillator.

papers.title: A Smooth Hamiltonian Diffeomorphism with Two Fixed Points on $S^2\times S^2$
papers.abstract:
We give a construction of a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the equal-area symplectic product $S^2\times S^2$ with two fixed points. The argument starts with a four-fixed-point map, passes to rescaled cotangent coordinates near the antidiagonal, and reduces the local fixed-point equations to two planar saddle problems. A relative modification merges each pair of saddles, and mixed generating functions are used to transfer the modification to the original map. We include detailed explanations of the normal form along a level arc, the Moser equation, uniform existence of mixed generating functions, the order of parameter choices, and the global graph argument. This construction gives a counterexample to the degenerate version of Arnold's conjecture proposed by Arnold\cite{Arnold86} when the manifold is standard $S^2\times S^2$.
  This work is done with ChatGPT. The author gave the idea to study the limit behavior of $\Phi_\rho$. GPT suggested a key idea of using second generating function to construct this Hamiltonian. Also, most of the computation is done by GPT.

papers.title: Group-graded Ore extensions and graded simplicity
papers.abstract: We study Ore extensions $R[t;\sigma,\delta]$ of rings graded by an arbitrary group $\Gamma$. The grading of $R$ extends with $t$ of degree $\gamma$ if and only if $\sigma$ is compatible with conjugation by $\gamma$ and $\delta$ with left translation by $\gamma$. The extended grading is then unique. For nonabelian $\Gamma$ the degree of $t$ need not commute with the degrees of $R$, and this twist cannot always be removed. If $R$ is gr-simple and $\sigma$ is an automorphism, then $R[t;\sigma,\delta]$ is gr-simple if and only if it has no homogeneous normal element that is monic of positive $t$-degree. The quantized Weyl algebra shows that the graded forms of the classical necessary conditions do not suffice. Over a group algebra $kG$, these extensions correspond to actions of $G$ on the affine line, and gr-simplicity means that the action has no finite orbit. In characteristic zero this is the nonvanishing of a class in $H^1(G,k_\chi)$, and simplicity forces $G$ to be metabelian. We prove the analogous results for Poisson polynomial rings and relate the two settings by semiclassical limits.

papers.title: Para families of orthogonal polynomials
papers.authors: St\'ephane Z. Beaulac, Nicolas Cramp\'e, Quentin Labriet, Lucia Morey, Rafael I. Nepomechie, Luc Vinet
papers.abstract: The para-Krawtchouk polynomials arose in the search for spin chains with perfect state transfer; the para-Racah, $q$-para-Racah and para-Bannai--Ito polynomials followed, obtained through singular truncations of families of the Askey scheme and used in turn to design spin chains. All are orthogonal on bi-lattices; the prefix goes back to the para-Krawtchouk case, whose spectrum is that of the parabose oscillator. The representations that these polynomials provide of the corresponding algebras --- Hahn, Racah, $q$-Racah, Bannai--Ito and complementary Bannai--Ito --- are shown to be reducible. Each decomposes into a direct sum of two irreducible modules of the same algebra, one attached to each of the two interlaced sub-lattices, and the parameters of the submodules are given. The para polynomials are thereby expressed in terms of the classical polynomials that the submodules carry, and the pairing $\lambda_n=\lambda_{N-n}$ of their eigenvalues is accounted for; the three features of the bi-lattice setting on which the reduction rests are identified. The properties of the para families are then presented in a unified way in the light of this decomposition, together with the constructions through which these families arise and the settings in which they have been put to use.

papers.title: Oka Geometry of Complex Six-Spheres
papers.authors: Yun-Heng Du, Bin Guo, Yuta Kusakabe, Song-Yan Xie
papers.abstract: Alp\"oge constructed a complex structure on $S^6$ through a torus fibration with exactly three special fibres. We prove that every member of the associated admissible period family is Oka and that the family projection over each relatively compact parameter disc is an Oka map. The Oka property survives the deletion or simultaneous blow-up of any finite set of distinct points in any member. Blowing up a single point therefore produces an Oka complex manifold diffeomorphic, but not biholomorphic, to $\mathbb{P}^3$. The proofs combine explicit cyclic coverings with analytic extension and the invariance of the Oka property under holomorphic coverings.

papers.title: Averages of Artin characters and their relation to the Davenport--Heilbronn theorem
papers.abstract:
We bound the error term in the counting function of cubic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ by $\mathcal{O}_\epsilon(X^{\theta+\epsilon})$, with $\theta < 2/3$, improving upon results due to Bhargava, Taniguchi, and Thorne. The proof proceeds by relating a certain discriminant-reducing sieve, due to Bhargava, Shankar, and Tsimerman, to averages of Artin characters associated with the Artin $L$-function $\zeta_K(s)/\zeta(s)$, with $K$ a cubic field. Conditional on the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for Dedekind zeta functions $\zeta_K(s)$, we obtain further savings and show that the error term is $\mathcal{O}(X^{2/3-1/51+\epsilon})$. Moreover, for the analogous smooth counting problem, we obtain a bound $\mathcal{O}(X^{1/2+\epsilon})$ for the error term, conditionally improving results of Shankar, S\"odergren, and Templier. Our arguments can also handle finitely many splitting conditions.
  The methods we use to study cubic fields are natural extensions of methods which are used to study the one-level density associated with the above family of Artin $L$-functions. In this direction, we improve the admissible support $[-\sigma,\sigma]$, from the previously known admissible value $\sigma < 2/5$, to $\sigma < 1$, conditional on the GRH. This also proves that at least $75\%$ of these $L$-functions are non-vanishing at the central point, conditionally improving upon results of Shankar, S\"odergren and Templier.
  Finally, one may study similar questions over a rational function field $\mathbb{F}_q(T)$, with $q$ coprime to $2$ and $3$. Here, we obtain a proportion of non-vanishing of at least $75\%$ for the analogous family of $L$-functions. Furthermore, we obtain a bound $\mathcal{O}\left(X^{1/2+\epsilon}\right)$ for the error term in the counting function of cubic function fields, improving previous results of the author. Over function fields, our results are unconditional.

papers.title: The Cuntz semigroup of the graph C*-algebra of a finite graph
papers.abstract: We compute the Cuntz semigroup of a graph C*-algebra associated to a finite graph by combining Hong and Szyma\'nski's realisation of the entire ideal lattice of a graph C*-algebra, Ara, Moreno and Pardo's computation of the Murray-von Neumann semigroup of a unital graph C*-algebra and various Cuntz semigroup techniques. We also investigate certain properties of such Cuntz semigroups, and demonstrate that at the level of the Cuntz semigroup, there is no obstruction to the conjecture that the nuclear dimension of any graph C*-algebra is at most one.

papers.title: Quantum real projective spaces as quantum CW-complexes via topological graphs
papers.abstract: We use the notion and properties of topological graphs to construct a quantum CW complex for quantum real projective spaces. This construction mirrors the CW complex construction in the classical case. Moreover, we introduce multipullback even-spheres as boundaries of noncommutative "cylinders" and show that they admit a gluing akin to the gluing of balls to the ends of a hollow closed cylinder.

papers.title: Cluster structures from Legendrian double twist knots: a comparative approach
papers.abstract: We undertake a systematic comparison of cluster algebras associated to Legendrian knots of the same smooth knot type. We describe a cluster structure on the m-graded augmentation variety of Legendrian representatives of a family of double twist knots that includes all orientably Lagrangian fillable twist knots. For different Legendrian representatives of the same smooth knot type, we show that these cluster structures are equivalent. Along the way, we characterize the representatives that admit Maslov-m exact Lagrangian fillings, construct a Catalan number of such fillings for each representative, and show that any Maslov-0 fillable representative is Legendrian isotopic to the (-1)-framed closure of a positive braid. Finally, we give two Legendrian representatives of a cabled twist knot that yield equivalent cluster structures of infinite type.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of the one-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with a repulsive harmonic potential
papers.abstract: We study the one-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with a repulsive harmonic potential. For repulsive self-interactions, we prove modified scattering for initial data of arbitrary size, assuming only velocity weights and one derivative; no smallness, symmetry, compact support, or spatial moments are required. In the lens variables of \cite{HK26}, the self-consistent force carries a nonintegrable time weight. We remove it by a momentum correction that solves a forced Burgers equation; the repulsive sign makes this correction monotone, which gives bounds for large data. We also construct modified wave operators for both signs of the interaction. Together with \cite{VR24,BVR25,HK26}, this gives a scattering theory in every dimension.

papers.title: Azumaya descent and \'etale-local cyclotomic comparison: a noncommutative filtration
papers.abstract:
Bhatt-Morrow-Scholze motivic filtration on topological Hochschild homology ($THH$) is extended to Azumaya algebras over quasisyntomic rings. We prove the Azumaya descent theorem:
  $THH$ of such an algebra is equivalent, as an underlying spectrum, to $THH$ of its center,
  normalized on $\pi_0$ by the reduced trace instead of the unit map. This comparison $\Phi_A$ is not shown to be \'etale-locally cyclotomic.
  But what is cyclotomic \'etale-locally is a separate Morita trace, agreeing with $\Phi_A$ only on $\pi_0$. The resulting transported filtration is exactly the center BMS filtration, well defined up to the automorphism ambiguity of $\Phi_A$. It is insensitive to the Brauer class, reflected instead by $K$-theoretic and module-categorical pairings $THH$ does not see. We establish the analogous statement for derived Azumaya algebras over connective $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings, under a connectivity hypothesis.

papers.title: Explicit second moments of symplectic Siegel transforms
papers.abstract: We give two alternate formulations for the second moment formula of the Siegel transform over $\mathrm{Sp}(2n, \mathbb Z) \backslash \mathrm{Sp}(2n,\mathbb R)$, previously established by Athreya-Konstantoulas and Kelmer-Yu. We also provide several applications that demonstrate their usefulness.

papers.title: The Benson--Etingof--Ostrik conjecture for finite tensor categories
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic admits a symmetric tensor functor to a higher Verlinde category. This was conjectured for arbitrary symmetric tensor categories of moderate growth by Benson, Etingof and Ostrik. The proof uses higher Frobenius functors, introduced by the authors in [CF1]. The main effort is directed towards a proof of a conjecture from [CF1] about thick tensor ideals in the representation category of elementary abelian $p$-groups, which implies that the higher Frobenius functors are symmetric monoidal. In fact, we prove a refinement of the latter conjecture that relates tensoring with restricted Steinberg modules to an iterated generalised cohomology of modules of elementary abelian $p$-groups.

papers.title: Safe Leader-Follower Density Control via Higher-Order Mean-Field Control Barrier Functions
papers.abstract: Mean-field control barrier functions (MF-CBFs) enforce safety of large-scale multi-agent systems at the level of densities, but existing formulations require the control to act directly on the population to be kept safe. We consider populations that are not directly actuated and are influenced only through other, controlled populations, possibly in the presence of diffusion. We show that if the constrained population lies at directed graph distance d from the actuated one, then, under a nondegeneracy condition, the safety functional has relative degree d+1 and the control enters its (d+1)-th time derivative affinely. Higher-order safety constraints can therefore still be enforced through a convex quadratic program. We apply the framework to leader-follower density control among dangerous regions, where the follower safety functional has relative degree two and the leader safety functional has relative degree one. We characterize exactly when the two constraints are jointly infeasible and bound the tracking errors induced by the safety correction. Simulations in cluttered environments show that the proposed filter preserves follower safety, whereas enforcing leader safety alone does not.

papers.title: The $L^2$-Cartesian Numerical Radii of Hilbert Space Operators
papers.authors: Wasim Audeh, Fuad Kittaneh, Hamid Reza Moradi, Satyajit Sahoo
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a complex Hilbert space, and let $T=H+iK\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ be the Cartesian decomposition of $T$, where $H=H^{*}$ and $K=K^{*}$. We introduce the $L^2$-Cartesian numerical radius and study its basic properties. We compare it with the classical numerical radius $\omega(T)$. In particular, we establish the sharp estimate $ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\omega(T)\le \wcart{2}(T)\le \omega(T), $ and establish lower and upper bounds in terms of the Cartesian parts $H,K$. We also give an equality characterization and explicit sharpness examples. As a consequence, we obtain $\frac{1}{4}\left\|T^{*}T+TT^{*}\right\|\le \wcart{2}(T)^2\le \omega(T)^2. $ More generally, we study the $L^p$-Cartesian numerical radius and prove the sharp comparison $ c_p\,\omega(T)\le \wcart{p}(T)\le \omega(T),\qquad 1\le p<\infty. $ Finally, we present a block-operator analogue of the classical refinement of the triangle inequality.

papers.title: Lempel-Ziv Parsing with Match-Length-Dependent Windows: Universality and Limits
papers.abstract: LZ77 coders spend the same number of bits on the distance of every match, although short matches rarely pay off at long distances. With match-length-dependent windows, used in several practical codecs, a match of length $\ell$ may refer back at most $W(\ell)$ symbols: short matches get short distance fields, while long matches keep the full window $W$. This breaks the suffix closure that classical LZ77 analyses rely on: the tail of an admissible match need not be admissible. We bound the cost of this loss, and of matches missed by a practical hash search, by the phrase count of a single-window reference parse. Consequently, when the full window starts at length $O(\log W)$, greedy parsing keeps the convergence rates and the optimal finite-input rates of LZ77 under substring-complexity constraints, and when it starts at length $o(\log W)$, greedy parsing is universal for stationary ergodic sources. We then delimit what the windows gain. A calibrated schedule never increases the minimum code length and saves a polynomially small rate on some iid sources. The leading redundancy term is set by the length code instead: on uniform iid data, with logarithmic-cost lengths and a fixed full-window threshold, it is at least of order $(\log\log W)/\log W$ whatever windows the short matches use, and a short codeword for a growing longest match reduces it to $O((\log\log\log W)/\log W)$. We also quantify the gains of coding single-symbol runs by count and of Huffman coding the token fields, and obtain a consistent entropy-rate estimator by selecting the window.

papers.title: Finite-time blow-up for the real-valued defocusing energy-supercritical NLW
papers.authors: Matthieu Cadiot, Alexandru D. Ionescu, Stan Palasek
papers.abstract: We consider the defocusing nonlinear wave equations $\partial_t^2u-\Delta u+u^p=0$, with $p$ odd, for real-valued functions on $\mathbb R^{1+d}$, in the energy-supercritical case. For $(d,p)=(9,3)$, $(7,5)$ and $(6,7)$, we construct a discretely self-similar solution in a backward light cone, of the form $$u(t,x)=(T-t)^{-\frac{2}{p-1}}W^*\big(\omega^*\log\frac1{T-t},\frac{|x|}{T-t}\big),$$ where the nonzero profile $W^*$ is $2\pi$-periodic in its first variable and real-analytic up to and across the light cone. Cutting off its initial data gives smooth, compactly supported, radial data whose solution coincides with the discretely self-similar solution in the backward light cone, is smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^{d}$ except at the vertex $(T,0)$ of the cone, and blows up there at the self-similar rate. The solutions we construct here appear to be the first blow-up solutions of defocusing energy-supercritical NLW with smooth real-valued data. For comparison, we also give in an appendix, for every energy-supercritical exponent, a construction of a bounded, finite-energy, radial solution which is continuously self-similar in a backward light cone and whose supremum blows up; it is not smooth across the light cone, and the difficulty of the problem lies entirely in this regularity. Existence of the real profile is proved by a computer-assisted Newton--Kantorovich argument in a Banach algebra of Fourier--Chebyshev coefficients, with rigorous error control. The main analytic ingredients are an exact description of the mode operators for the linear part, which are hypergeometric and upper triangular in the Chebyshev basis, and a bound for their inverses that is uniform at high frequencies. All computer-assisted proofs, including the requisite codes and the approximate objects, are accessible on GitHub at \cite{code}.

papers.title: Shape optimisation of the maximum of the gradient of the torsion function on convex sets
papers.authors: Michiel van den Berg, Dorin Bucur, Mickael Nahon
papers.abstract: We analyse the boundary behaviour of the gradient of the torsion function $w_\Om$ in convex domains $\Om\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. We prove that its $L^\infty$-norm is attained at a boundary point and establish the stability of this norm under general (convex) perturbations. For problems of the form $$\sup\{\|\nabla w_{\Om}\|_\infty: \Om \subset \R^d,\textup{open, bounded and convex}, G(\Om)=m\},$$ where $G$ is either volume or perimeter, we show the existence of maximisers which are $C^1$-smooth, rotationally symmetric about an axis and contain a $(d-1)$- dimensional ball (of estimated size) in their boundary. Other constraints, whether geometric (such as diameter or circumradius) or variational (such as torsion or first Dirichlet eigenvalue), are also briefly discussed, and some of their characteristic behaviours are highlighted.

papers.title: Uniqueness for tv-regularized inverse problems with source in divergence form
papers.authors: L Baratchart (FACTAS), D P Hardin, C Villalobos-Guill\'en
papers.abstract: Inverse source problems in divergence form consist in finding a vector field with prescribed support S, whose divergence is the Laplacian of some observed potential. In this paper, we assume the unknown vector field is a vector-valued measure, and we study the corresponding least square inversion problems, regularized by penalizing the total variation, without discretizing the criterion nor the unknown. We prove that this problem has a unique minimizer in the case where S is a slender set; i.e., it has zero Lebesgue measure and each connected component of its complement has infinite Lebesgue measure. The proof relies on a refinement of Smirnov's decomposition of divergence-free measures [62] which is of independent interest.

papers.title: The Order Mass Identity of Rooted Forests, with a Direct Proof of the Extended Aldous-Broder Theorem
papers.abstract: The Aldous-Broder algorithm constructs a spanning tree from the first-entrance edges of a covering random walk. Its distribution is known, but deriving it by summing over the orders in which a fixed tree can be discovered remains difficult. In this paper, we evaluate this sum by establishing an order-mass identity for rooted forests. For real matrices with zero row sums, the identity expresses the sum of order weights associated with each root as a principal cofactor of a matrix on the roots, under a nonsingularity condition involving only the sets encountered along the growth orders of the given forest. We prove the identity using linear algebraic tools. With one root, the sum equals one, giving a direct proof of the extended Aldous-Broder theorem for every finite irreducible Markov chain started at a fixed state. With multiple roots, we derive the forest law produced by the stopped covering walk and show how it differs from the weight-proportional forest law. The identity and the resulting tree and forest laws are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Khintchine dichotomy for images of self-similar measures and almost random walks
papers.abstract: Following the celebrated breakthrough in B\'enard-He-Zhang, we prove Khintchine dichotomy for push-forwards of self-similar measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under uniform $C^{1+\alpha}$ maps. For this, we also study almost random walks on $\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{Z})$ and prove their effective equidistribution.

papers.title: On the inequality $\mu_3 < \lambda_1$ for the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator
papers.abstract: In 1952, P\'olya proved the inequality $\mu_2 < \lambda_1$ for the eigenvalues of Dirichlet and Neumann problems in domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, $d \ge 2$. In 2026, Tang and Zhang proved the inequality $\mu_3 < \lambda_1$ in the two-dimensional case. We show that $\mu_3 < \lambda_1$ for $d\ge 3$ as well.

papers.title: Absolute moments of GH distribution
papers.abstract: In this work, we focus on deriving the absolute moments of the general ized hyperbolic (GH) distribution via its mean-variance mixture structure. Conditioning on the GIG mixing variable reduces the problem to Gaussian moment calculations and known GIG power moments, avoiding direct integration with Bessel functions. The variance gamma (VG), normal inverse Gaussian (NIG), hyperbolic, Normal, and Student t distributions emerge as natural special or limiting cases of the generalized hyperbolic family. This approach offers a substantially simpler and more transparent derivation, facilitating both implementation and verification.

papers.title: Global solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the half-space
papers.authors: Hairong Liu, Jinlong Wu, Hua Zhong
papers.abstract: We study the initial boundary value problem for the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations without damping in the three-dimensional half-space and in smooth exterior domains. The velocity satisfies the no-slip boundary condition, and the electric potential satisfies the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. For small perturbations of a constant state in $H^3$, with a small initial electric field in $L^2$, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The uniform estimates combine density dissipation, tangential and normal derivative estimates, and a modified energy expressed through the Helmholtz projection. In exterior domains, boundary normal coordinates and localized elliptic estimates control the geometric terms. We also obtain algebraic decay in the full energy norm. In the half-space, finite tangential negative Sobolev norms of order $-s$, with $\frac12\leq s<1$, yield the rate $(1+t)^{-s/2}$. In exterior domains, integrable initial density and velocity perturbations yield the same form of estimate for $0<s<\frac14$. The exterior decay proof uses whole-space negative-order estimates for localized variables and the time integrability of the dissipation.

papers.title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
papers.abstract: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI.

papers.title: The symmetry group of Turk's head knots
papers.abstract: For p, q >= 3 with gcd(p,q) = 1 we show that the symmetry group of the Turk's head knot Th(p,q), the closure of the braid (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1} sigma_3 sigma_4^{-1} ... sigma_{p-1}^{+-1})^q, is the dihedral group of order 4q. This proves Conjecture R of Di Prisa and \c{S}avk for q >= 3; the case p = 3 is due to Sakuma and Weeks. The argument is diagrammatic: by the flyping theorem of Menasco and Thistlethwaite, the symmetries of a knot with a prime, reduced alternating diagram without non-trivial flypes are the symmetries of the diagram (we write out a proof for the diagrams at hand), and we show that the standard diagram of Th(p,q) has no non-trivial flypes and exactly 4q symmetries. The chirality of Th(p,q) for even p, which also follows from a theorem of Murasugi, is visible in the group. We compare the argument with the geometric one of Sakuma and Weeks for p = 3.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Referenced Belief-Guided Q-Learning for Jammer Identification and Beam-Power Control in a mmWave Model
papers.abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are expected to support high data rates and reliable connectivity while meeting requirements for energy efficiency, resource management, and communication security. Digital Twin (DT) technology represents expected network behavior and enables the actual network state to be assessed against it. Integrating DT technology with reinforcement learning (RL) supports adaptive resource allocation and security-aware decision-making. This paper presents a simulation-based DT reference and a belief-guided Q-learning (BGQL) method for joint jammer identification and beam-power control in a site-specific 28-GHz network model. Receiver-level residuals between attack-free and attacked configurations are combined with candidate spatial jamming footprints and accumulated into a normalized suspicion vector. BGQL incorporates this vector into its state, reward, and exploratory beam-selection rule. Compared with SARSA, Greedy, and Random across 30 paired Monte Carlo runs per configuration, with known jammer counts, BGQL achieves link-rate scores of 437.4-564.2 Mbit/s, rate-to-device-power scores of 60.37-76.79 Mbit/J, and localization recall of 100% for one jammer and 78%-81% for two jammers. BGQL requires 80-130 s per run versus 5-14 s for SARSA. These findings provide a matched-model simulation proof of concept for DT-referenced belief-guided learning for security-aware beam-power control in 6G networks.

papers.title: On the generators of separable unital C*-algebras
papers.authors: George A. Elliott, Chun Guang Li, Zhuang Niu
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a separable unital $\mathrm C^*$-algebra with nonempty tracial state space and strict comparison by ordinary tracial states. If $\mathcal Z$ embeds unitally into $A$, then $A$ is singly generated. In particular, every simple separable unital $\mathrm C^*$-algebra $A$ with $\mathrm T(A)\ne\varnothing$ and strict comparison is singly generated.

papers.title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problem for the Schr\"odinger Operator on a Compact Graph
papers.abstract:
We study the optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for the first $m$ eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator on a compact metric graph. We prove the existence of a solution for every strictly increasing finite set of prescribed eigenvalues. On a graph without cycles, we obtain a representation of the optimal correction as a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions, provided that the selected eigenvalues are simple and separated from the next eigenvalue. On a graph with cycles, under the same simplicity and separation assumptions, we obtain a strong limiting representation of the optimal potential in terms of eigenfunctions of approximating operators.
  For a graph with a cycle, we give a counterexample with simple eigenvalues and linearly dependent squared eigenfunctions. We also prove that linear dependence of the squares of nonzero restrictions to an edge of eigenfunctions corresponding to distinct eigenvalues forces the potential on that edge to have an analytic representative

papers.title: Remarks on the monodromy conjecture for symmetric determinantal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We compute the local and global Denef--Loeser topological zeta functions of the determinant on the space of symmetric matrices. It verifies the strong monodromy conjecture of the symmetric determinant function. The computation relates to the geometry of complete quadrics and wonderful embeddings.

papers.title: Endochain conditions on modules and $p$-quasi-Frobenius rings
papers.authors: Theophilus Gera, Amit Sharma, Manoj Kumar Patel, Pramod Kanwar
papers.abstract: Analogous to quasi-Frobenius rings, dual rings, and Johns rings, the classes of $p$-quasi-Frobenius rings, $p$-dual rings, $p$-Johns rings are introduced and used to discuss and settle principal analogues of the Faith-Menal, Faith, and FGF conjectures. A chain symmetry theorem establishes that for quasi-injective semi-projective modules with semiprime endomorphism ring, endonoetherianity and endoartinianity are equivalent and force the endomorphism ring to be semisimple artinian. Within this unified setting, it is shown that (1) two-sided $p$-Johns rings are $p$-quasi-Frobenius, giving a principal Faith-Menal analogue, with a counterexample showing that the one-sided hypothesis is insufficient; (2) semiprimary principal right ideal rings that are right injective and right Kasch are $p$-quasi-Frobenius-this affirmatively answers a question of Faith (Q2) in the principal two-sided ideal ring case and settles the principal Faith conjecture, with a counterexample showing the principal right ideal ring to be indispensable; and (3) right $p$-Johns rings that are left CF and left perfect are $p$-quasi-Frobenius, yielding a principal FGF analogue, with a counterexample demonstrating that the hypotheses are essential. Wherever needed, examples are provided to show that various classes introduced are different from the existing classes in the literature.

papers.title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
papers.abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $\beta$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.

papers.title: Chemotaxis models with signal-dependent sensitivity and a logistic-type source, III: Bifurcation and spike-like solutions
papers.authors: Le Chen, Ian Ruau, Wenxian Shen
papers.abstract:
This third paper in a series on a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model studies bifurcation of positive constant equilibria in one space dimension. We consider $$ \left\{  egin{array}{ll} u_t=\Delta u-\chi_0
abla\cdot\left( rac{u^m}{(1+v)^ eta}
abla vight)+au-bu^{1+\alpha}, & x\in\Omega,\ 0=\Delta v-\mu v+
u u^\gamma, & x\in\Omega,\  rac{\partial u}{\partial n}= rac{\partial v}{\partial n}=0, & x\in\partial\Omega, \end{array} ight. $$ where $\Omega$ is a bounded interval, $\alpha,\gamma,m,\mu,
u>0$, $\chi_0\in\mathbb R$, and $a,b, eta\ge0$. Building on earlier results on global existence, boundedness, persistence, and stabilization, we take $\chi_0$ as the bifurcation parameter and examine the effects of $ eta$ and the domain size on the bifurcation.
  Center manifold reduction yields a coefficient $ eta_{n_0}$ at a simple bifurcation mode $n_0$ of a positive constant equilibrium. The pitchfork bifurcation is supercritical if $ eta_{n_0}>0$ and subcritical if $ eta_{n_0}<0$. Stronger desensitization raises the sensitivity required for loss of linear stability. Bifurcation may be supercritical for small $ eta$ but is always subcritical for sufficiently large $ eta$. Thus, desensitization makes patterns harder to trigger and favors abrupt rather than continuous emergence. The bifurcation mode increases with domain size, allowing more complex spatial patterns.
  Under suitable conditions, we prove unbounded continuation of local bifurcation branches. We also show that large-sensitivity stationary sequences satisfying a peak-gap hypothesis develop spike-like profiles. Numerical continuation and time-evolution experiments illustrate the bifurcating branches and spike-like solutions and suggest unbounded continuation and increasingly sharp stationary profiles.

papers.title: Galois Groups of Trinomials with Small Coefficients
papers.abstract: We calculate the Galois group of $f = x^n + ax^k + b \in \mathbb{Z}\left[ x \right]$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ for all $1 \leq \left| ab \right| \leq 3$, $n$ sufficiently large and $k$ coprime to $n$. In particular, we prove that the Galois group of $f$ is the maximal one that its factorization type allows. We give a criterion for the Galois group of a factor of a trinomial to be symmetric, with an eye towards future applications. To the best of our knowledge, the only previously known explicit example of polynomials of degree $n$ with bounded coefficients and Galois group $S_n$ is $x^n - x - 1$, while recent results show that the probability that a random polynomial of degree $n$ with reasonably bounded coefficients has Galois group $S_n$ tends to $1$ as $n$ tends to infinity. Using our calculation, one can construct many new such explicit examples.

papers.title: Complete characterization of disconnected one-point unions of cycles with local antimagic chromatic number 2
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$, characterizing the structural behavior of achieving the minimal local antimagic chromatic number $\chi_{la}(G) = 2$ remains a fundamental open problem in the study of vertex-distinguishing edge labelings. This paper establishes complete characterizations for a significant structural class of disconnected graphs, specifically addressing disconnected one-point unions of cycles with at most three components. By introducing a robust algebraic approach, we show that these specific graph architectures form distinct, manageable solution families under a local antimagic 2-coloring framework. Crucially, our structural framework provides the theoretical basis for extending these complete characterizations to an arbitrary number of components, demonstrating unique edge assignments up to isomorphism. These results offer key insights into the structural properties governing low-chromatic antimagic invariants and offer significant progress toward a unified classification of graphs with $\chi_{la}(G) = 2$.

papers.title: Stability and Error Estimates for Convolution Quadrature under Radial Symbol Bounds
papers.abstract: We develop stability and error estimates for multistep convolution quadrature (CQ) under general radial bounds on the Laplace symbol. Instead of the classical single-power condition $|F(z)|\leq M|z|^{-\mu}$, we assume $|F(z)|\leq C\Phi(|z|)$, where $\Phi$ is positive, continuous and regularly varying at zero and infinity. For strongly $A(\alpha)$-stable multistep methods, we derive error estimates and stability estimates for the CQ weights, as well as error bounds for power-type inputs $g_\beta(t)=t^{\beta1}/\Gamma(\beta)$ with $\beta>0$. These estimates explicitly retain the dependence on the memory law through the factor $\Phi(t_n^{-1})$. The framework accommodates symbols whose behavior cannot be described by a global single-power. It also preserves logarithmic and multiscale factors that would be lost under a coarser power bounds. Then we apply the to fractional viscoelastic, distributed-order, and logarithmic-power memory models. Numerical experiments with backward Euler and second-order backward differentiation CQ confirm the expected temporal convergence orders for direct responses. A distributed-order PDE further illustrates temporal convergence for smooth and nonsmooth initial data.

papers.title: Stevens' Approach to Kloosterman Sums on Split Groups
papers.authors: Li Cai, Haoran Liu, Mingyu Yang, Wenyan Yang
papers.abstract: We develop a uniform framework for Stevens' approach to Kloosterman sums on split groups over $p$-adic fields. The main result reduces the bounding of Kloosterman sums to that for the so-called Pl\"ucker-constrained sets, which are certain subsets of affine spaces constrained by conditions giving by the Pl\"ucker coordinates. We then give a nontrivial bound for the Kloosterman sums on the exceptional group $G_2$. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions associated with generic representations on $G_2$.

papers.title: Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
papers.abstract:
We extend the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories (Shimizu-Yadav) to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras.
  For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. It is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same
  as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules.
  Hence rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems, with the ribbon condition $\theta_{A_0}=\id$, $\theta_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove
  that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose M\"uger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We construct examples from graded simple currents, treat the free fermion and the symplectic fermion,
  and compare with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.

papers.title: Residual-Based Adaptive Refinement in Hybrid Variational-Collocation PINNs for Singular Elliptic PDEs with Mixed Dirichlet-Neumann Boundary Conditions
papers.authors: Somnath Giri, Muslim Malik, Rishikesh Yadav
papers.abstract: Solutions of second-order elliptic PDE problems on nonconvex or cracked domains with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann conditions typically lie outside $H^2(\Omega)$. Near re-entrant corners, crack tips and points where the boundary condition changes type, the gradient grows like $r^{\lambda-1}$ with $\lambda<1$. We study residual-based adaptive refinement in hybrid variational-collocation PINNs. A multiscale Fourier-feature network is trained on a composite loss. The loss combines a variational residual tested against Legendre bubble functions, a strong-form collocation term and penalties for the Dirichlet and Neumann data. The variational term needs only first derivatives of the network, whereas the collocation term requires second derivatives and provides a residual that can be evaluated at any point. After each training stage, candidate points selected by this residual are added to the collocation set. The method is tested on five two dimensional benchmarks, namely a Mode~III crack, a cross-shaped domain with four re-entrant corners with unequal amplitude, a reaction-diffusion problem with four localized peaks, a monotone semilinear problem with a boundary layer and the Motz problem. Compared with uniform point insertion under the same collocation and iteration budget, residual-based refinement reduced the relative $L^2$ error by up to a factor of $32$, the relative $L^\infty$ error by up to a factor of $38$ and the relative $H^1$ semi-norm error by up to a factor of $15$.

papers.title: Diagonal and branchwise criteria for universal Fourier series
papers.abstract: We characterize diagonal profiles admitting universal real trigonometric Fourier series with factors in $\mathcal E_s=\bigcap_{p>s}\ell^p$ and $\ell^{s,q}$, $2\le s<\infty$, $1\le q\le\infty$. For nonincreasing profiles we obtain exact dyadic criteria and logarithmic endpoints. For independently regular odd/even sine/cosine branches we characterize simultaneous subseries, sign, and rearrangement universality for finite almost-everywhere targets. One function in every $L^p$, $1\le p<2$, supplies the coefficients. A separation example admits this realization although every compatible nonincreasing majorant with bounded relative cost belongs to $\ell^1$. Residue-class decompositions extend the criterion; a weakest-model condition permits extended-real rearrangement targets. A Walsh--Paley counterpart yields the same diagonal multiplier thresholds for ternary $\{0,\pm1\}$-universality, together with a Fourier--Walsh realization. Trigonometric realization uses Pogosyan's majorant theorem; the multiplier, factorization, projection-transfer, separation, and Walsh Fourier-origin arguments are proved here.

papers.title: Wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations
papers.authors: Jian Chen, Shaojie Yang, Zhaoyang Yin
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. We establish more general wave breaking criteria that strictly extend earlier wave breaking criteria for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. The approach relies on analyzing the monotonicity and continuity properties of a linear combination comprising the supremum and infimum of the solution's slope. Further generalizations are demonstrated via applications to the Camassa-Holm equation, the $\mu$-Camassa-Holm equation and the hyperelastic rod equation. Our refined approach yields more precise wave breaking criteria, thereby extending the theoretical understanding of singularity formation in dispersive waves.

papers.title: On the Allen--Cahn equation
papers.abstract: Using the framework developed by OpenAI, we prove that finite Morse index implies $O(R^{n-1})$ energy growth for bounded entire solutions of the quartic Allen--Cahn equation in dimensions $4\leq n\leq9$, uniformly in the center of the ball. Combined with the cited finite-index classification results, this gives planar rigidity for $4\leq n\leq7$ and, for nonconstant solutions, multiplicity-one stable minimal cone blowdowns through dimension nine. Within the framework, we derive an additive adjacent-layer interaction estimate, a weighted curvature and defect estimate with exponent $p=9/4$, and the localization needed for exterior stability. The limiting interaction coefficient $48$ is sharp in the unrestricted low-defect class with sufficiently large logarithmic selection depth.

papers.title: Christoffel transformations of symmetric $d$-connections and gap probability recurrences
papers.abstract:
We study the Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ of an even discrete weight. For the associated orthogonal polynomial ensembles on squared nodes $y=x^2$, ratios of moment determinants relate the largest-particle distributions and transfer exact gap probability recurrences between the ensembles. For positive weights satisfying the stated moment and support assumptions, this comparison requires no Pearson condition. The transformation is realized by elementary bundle modifications at zero and infinity on $\mathbb P^1$.
  When the original weight has Pearson ratio $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $\mathrm{deg}\; d=1,2$, these modifications conjugate cutoff dynamics on common stable loci of symmetric $d$-connections under the stated geometric hypotheses. The transformed recurrence coefficients are expressed explicitly as rational functions of spectral coordinates. On the unit lattice, a local recurrence formula applies to rational symmetric Pearson ratios of arbitrary degree, including outside these charts, whenever its local hypotheses hold.

papers.title: Small and large gaps between zeros of Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: For every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove unconditionally that infinitely many consecutive zeros have spacing less than $1/2+\varepsilon$ times the mean. Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we also prove a positive proportion of such spacings for the Riemann zeta-function, and infinitely many spacings greater than $3.63$ times the mean for every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function.

papers.title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
papers.authors: Brayden Letwin, Victor Reis, Thomas Rothvoss
papers.abstract: Let $\Lambda \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det \Gamma \ge 1$ for all sublattices $\Gamma \subseteq \Lambda^*$. We prove that there exists a symmetric random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a smooth, strictly positive density $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying that (1) $f$ is $\alpha$-strongly log-concave, where $\alpha = 2\pi/e$, and (2) $X + \Lambda$ is uniform on $\mathbb{R}^n/\Lambda$. Moreover, the existence of such a density characterizes this property up to a universal dilation. There are a few consequences of the above. We list some. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ \mu(\Lambda, K) = \max_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\min_{\lambda\in\Lambda} \left\|x-\lambda\right\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}{\pi}} \cdot \mathbb{E}\,\left\|G\right\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,\mathrm{Id})$. This implies an $O(n \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the flatness constant and an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ bound for the subspace flatness constant. We also compare the entire ordered spectrum of the associated flat torus on $\Lambda^*$ with that of a Gaussian, yielding an alternative proof of the reverse Minkowski theorem.

papers.title: No braiding for quantum sl2 reps - A short proof
papers.abstract: We give a short and self-contained proof that the category of all finite dimensional representations of quantum sl2 is not braided.

papers.title: Affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequalities and optimal star bodies
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish an affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequality by replacing the Euclidean fractional Orlicz seminorm with an energy obtained by minimizing over origin-symmetric star bodies of prescribed volume. Under finite lower and upper power growth assumptions, a subcritical upper growth bound, and a monotonicity condition on $t^{n/s+2}\Phi''(t)$, the resulting inequality has the same best constant as its Euclidean counterpart. The power case recovers the affine fractional Sobolev inequality of Haddad and Ludwig with the corresponding Luxemburg normalization. To establish this inequality, we investigate the underlying geometric extremal problem. For every nonzero smooth function of compact support, the existence and uniqueness of an optimal star body are proved under the growth assumptions alone, and its radial function is characterized by an equation involving $\Phi(t)+(s/n)t\Phi'(t)$. We also establish an anisotropic rearrangement inequality, together with its equality conditions under additional strictness assumptions. Moreover, the normalized local limit is investigated. The optimized energies converge to the local energy, and the radial functions of the minimizing bodies converge uniformly on the sphere. The limiting modular is determined by $\overline\Phi(t)=\int_0^t\Phi(\tau)\,d\tau/\tau$. Finally, we compare optimization over star bodies with optimization in the affine orbit.

papers.title: Convex Equilibrium Potentials for Monge--Amp\`ere: Curvature Bounds and A Posteriori Evaluation
papers.authors: Edison V\'azquez, Yingdong Lu, Tomasz Nowicki
papers.abstract: Equilibrium neural networks define their hidden state as the fixed point of a contraction, so their effective depth is set at evaluation time rather than by the architecture. Using them for fully nonlinear PDEs raises two issues that explicit networks avoid: second derivatives may grow with the effective depth, and the potential is only ever evaluated approximately. We study nonnegative softplus equilibrium networks with contraction factor $q<1$, a convex class suited to the Monge--Amp\`ere equation. A positivity cancellation in the resolvent shows that the Hessian grows at most like $(1-q)^{-2}$, rather than the $(1-q)^{-3}$ of a direct estimate, and an explicit one-neuron family shows that this exponent is sharp; third derivatives satisfy a sharp $(1-q)^{-3}$ bound. Residual-based a posteriori estimates then control the state, its input derivatives and, in two dimensions, the Hessian determinant at an approximate equilibrium. Combined with interval arithmetic on complete covers of the domain, they yield rigorous uniform bounds on the Monge--Amp\`ere residual and, through a comparison argument, on the solution error of a fixed trained network. On two manufactured Dirichlet problems on the unit disk, all six trained models are certified with residual below $0.25$ and boundary error below $0.01$. Adaptive stopping halves float64 evaluation time at best, whereas certified adaptive evaluation remains costlier than fixed depth.

papers.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2\epsilon$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_\epsilon$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_\epsilon$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_\epsilon$ and $b_\epsilon$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.

papers.title: A H\"ormander spectral multiplier theorem for fractional Hardy operators
papers.abstract: We consider the fractional Laplacian with added critical or subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator. We prove a H\"ormander spectral multiplier theorem, i.e., the boundedness of sufficiently smooth multipliers of these Hardy operators on Lebesgue spaces. The range of admissible Lebesgue exponents is optimal, but the smoothness assumption is probably not. The proof combines the Helffer--Sj\"ostrand formula with a quantitative Jaffard lemma for operator-valued matrices.

papers.title: The degree distribution in bipartite planar maps: applications to the Ising model
papers.abstract:
We characterize the generating function of bipartite planar maps counted according to the degree distribution of their black and white vertices. This result is applied to the solution of the hard particle and Ising models on random planar lattices. We thus recover and extend some results previously obtained by means of matrix integrals.
  Proofs are purely combinatorial and rely on the idea that planar maps are conjugacy classes of trees. In particular, these trees explain why the solutions of the Ising and hard particle models on maps of bounded degree are always algebraic.

papers.title: Comparing the automorphism group of the measure algebra with some groups related to the infinite permutation group of the natural numbers
papers.abstract: We prove, by a straight construction, that the automorphism group of the measure algebra and the subgroup of the measure preserving ones cannot be isomorphic to the trivial automorphisms of P(N)/fin.

papers.title: On Orthogonal Recurrent Neural Networks Quantization
papers.authors: Armand Foucault (IMT), Franck Mamalet (Comue de Toulouse), Fran\c{c}ois Malgouyres (IMT)
papers.abstract: In recent years, Orthogonal Recurrent Neural Networks (ORNNs) have gained popularity due to their ability to manage tasks involving long-term dependencies, such as the Copy-task, and their linear complexity. However, existing ORNNs utilize full precision weights and activations, which prevents their deployment on compact devices. In this paper, we explore the quantization of the weight matrices in ORNNs, leading to Quantized approximately Orthogonal RNNs (QORNNs). The construction of such networks remained an open problem, acknowledged for its inherent instability. We propose and investigate two strategies to learn QORNN by combining quantization-aware training (QAT) and orthogonal projections. We also study post-training quantization of the activations for pure integer computation of the recurrent loop. The most efficient fully-quantized models are currently the only alternatives for solving the Copy-task with 1000 timesteps. They also surpass existing quantized models on tasks requiring long-term dependencies, such as permuted MNIST as well as some Internet of Things (IoT) tasks. However, they are less effective on tasks where long short-term memory (LSTMs) and other gated RNNs outperform ORNNs.

papers.title: Stochastic Inverse Problem: stability, regularization and Wasserstein gradient flow
papers.authors: Qin Li, Maria Oprea, Li Wang, Yunan Yang
papers.abstract: Inverse problems in physical or biological sciences often involve recovering an unknown parameter that is random. The sought-after quantity is a probability distribution of the unknown parameter, that produces data that aligns with measurements. Consequently, these problems are naturally framed as stochastic inverse problems. In this paper, we explore three aspects of this problem: direct inversion, variational formulation with regularization, and optimization via gradient flows, drawing parallels with deterministic inverse problems. A key difference from the deterministic case is the space in which we operate. Here, we work within a probability space rather than Euclidean or Sobolev spaces, making tools from measure transport theory necessary for the study. Our findings reveal that the choice of metric---both in the design of the loss function and in the optimization process---significantly impacts the stability and properties of the optimizer.

papers.title: MeshCone: Second-Order Cone Programming for Geometrically-Constrained Mesh Enhancement
papers.abstract: Modern mesh generation pipelines whether learning-based or classical often produce outputs requiring post-processing to achieve production-quality geometry. This work introduces MeshCone, a convex optimization framework for guided mesh refinement that leverages reference geometry to correct deformed or degraded meshes. We formulate the problem as a second-order cone program where vertex positions are optimized to align with target geometry while enforcing smoothness through convex edge-length regularization. MeshCone performs geometry-aware optimization that preserves fine details while correcting structural defects. We demonstrate robust performance across 56 diverse object categories from ShapeNet and ThreeDScans, achieving superior refinement quality compared to Laplacian smoothing and unoptimized baselines while maintaining sub-second inference times. MeshCone is particularly suited for applications where reference geometry is available, such as mesh-from-template workflows, scan-to-CAD alignment, and quality assurance in asset production pipelines.

papers.title: How Much Weak Overlap Can Doubly Robust T-Statistics Handle?
papers.abstract: Propensity scores near zero or one can make standard confidence intervals undercover.
